Such states can be generated in a variety of physical systems and are promising resources for several quantum technologies, ranging from quantum clock synchronization to quantum communication. However, their full potential is currently limited by the fact that the entanglement dynamics often occur on timescales comparable to the achievable synchronization precision, especially in experiments aimed at distributing entanglement through noisy urban channels. In this context, accurate timing is not merely a technical detail, but a fundamental requirement for faithfully observing and exploiting the underlying quantum correlations. Here, we demonstrate the faithful distribution of a fast-evolving entangled state over a 270 m free-space channel connecting two buildings in the center of Rome. The developed system incorporates a synchronization device capable of achieving sub-50 ps timing accuracy between the two ends of the link while simultaneously supporting channel stabilization. Our results demonstrate that time-evolving entanglement can be reliably transmitted through a noisy urban free-space channel, representing an important benchmark toward long-distance free-space quantum communication and the future implementation of time-correlated entangled states in demanding scenarios such as satellite-based quantum networks.

items.title: Broadband and Large-Multimode Quantum Optical Storage with Rare-Earth Ions in Solids
items.summary: Broadband quantum memory devices are essential elements for future quantum networks. Here we propose a broadband quantum memory scheme called Hole Anti-hole Grating Echo Memory (HAGEM) for rare-earth ions in solids, which can be implemented with most of the present rare-earth ions hosted in various types of solids. Using HAGEM, a quantum memory device with one billion temporal modes per second can be developed with current available technologies. To validate the memory protocol, we conducted some proof-of-concept experiments. We provide a Eu$^\text{3+}$ molecular complex with special hyperfine level structures of which the hyperfine level separations are in a specific mathematical correlation that can be obtained by harnessing chemical engineering. Using the proposed memory protocol and material, we experimentally demonstrate a single-mode quantum optical storage efficiency of 14.9% and a memory bandwidth of 200MHz, which can easily be extended to a few GHz. In addition, a multi-mode storage of four temporal modes is achieved with a storage efficiency of 1.3%. Broadband & large-multimode quantum memory device with a long storage time enabled by HAGEM integrating with the current available entangled photon pair source and tunable delay lines, a quantum repeater network with an entanglement distribution rate on the order of 1kHz - 10kHz can be created with a communication distance around 100km. This will greatly facilitate the development of quantum networks in near future.

items.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
items.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. In some, the force is extinguished at a nonzero indentation, whether by plastic deformation or by an elastic aftereffect, so that a residual deformation remains at separation. Such laws sit uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the contact law alone does not determine the interaction of the bodies. Because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately. So must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, neither of which the equations of motion contain. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and the equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the resulting formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is also examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.

items.title: Dual Reverse Time Migration: Efficient Least-squares Imaging with Multiple Scattering in Dual Space
items.summary: Least-squares reverse time migration (LSRTM) estimates a broadband reflectivity image by iteratively minimizing the data misfit. Despite its superior imaging performance over conventional reverse time migration (RTM), LSRTM is fundamentally limited by the first-order Born approximation and incurs a high computational cost due to the iterative solution of a source-dependent model-space Hessian. We propose dual RTM, a seismic imaging framework that reformulates the inverse problem in the dual space, where the optimization variable is the scattering information of all orders, rather than being limited to the first-order scattering of the Born approximation. Unlike LSRTM, which directly estimates the reflectivity model, dual RTM reconstructs the missing scattering data (dual variable) through a fixed-point iteration governed by the full wave equation, enabling the recovery of higher-order scattering and multiple reflections without repeated background velocity updates. Furthermore, dual RTM replaces the source-dependent model-space Hessian with a source-independent data-space Hessian. A hybrid time--frequency formulation enables this Hessian to be assembled and inverted once in the Fourier domain as an offline preprocessing step, reducing the online computational cost of each dual iteration to that of a single RTM application. Numerical experiments on challenging synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that dual RTM suppresses acquisition footprints, improves amplitude fidelity, and enhances deep imaging where primary reflections alone provide insufficient illumination. These results establish dual RTM as an efficient bridge between conventional RTM/LSRTM and nonlinear waveform inversion for high-resolution large-scale seismic imaging.

items.title: Pairwise assessment correlations predict cooperation of the Leading Eight under private assessment
items.summary: Indirect reciprocity can sustain cooperation when individuals use reputations to decide whom to help. The Leading Eight norms sustain such cooperation under public assessment, where all individuals share the same assessments. Under private assessment, however, observers may disagree, yet their assessments remain correlated. Two quantities, the average fraction of good assessments $h$ and the conditional probability $h_{\mathrm G}$ that one observer assesses a player as good given that another does, are known to determine the stability of cooperation, but how $h_{\mathrm G}$ itself is determined has remained open. Within a pairwise approximation, we derive a closed equation for $h_{\mathrm G}$ that, together with that for $h$, determines both quantities for all eight norms, including third-order ones. This description substantially improves agreement with simulations over a mean-field approximation that neglects correlations, and recovers the known classification of the Leading Eight into three classes. The remaining discrepancies are largest for L2 and L5 at low error rates and decrease as assessment error increases. Relating $h_{\mathrm G}$ to the variance of individual goodness suggests that these discrepancies reflect information beyond the first two moments of the goodness distribution. Our framework provides a concise and analytically tractable tool for evaluating social norms under private assessment.

items.title: Chirality destroys oriented active solids
items.summary: We construct a hydrodynamic theory of the effect of chiral and active force densities on three-dimensional uniaxial solids. We show that in a fixed background medium active chiral force densities---that arise at lower order in gradients than odd elasticity---generically destabilise the solid state. We further show this active instability also affects isotropic chiral solids in an anisotropic medium, a situation that is relevant for cell clusters moving through the extracellular matrix. Interestingly, the instability is eliminated in a higher-symmetry solid, known as the polar elastomer; indeed, we show that chirality does not affect the leading-order mechanics of such materials. We further demonstrate that momentum-conserving polar active solids have two chiral odd elasticities in contrast to the one discussed for two-dimensional solids. However, we again find that the higher symmetry of polar elastomers eliminates one of these with the remaining one being equivalent to the two-dimensional odd elastic force density. Our results should apply to numerous biological and condensed matter systems.

items.title: Effect of chirality on active elastomers and solids in three dimensions
items.summary: We examine the effect of chiral activity on nematic and polar uniaxial elastomers and solids by constructing the general hydrodynamic equations for these phases. We start with the elastomer, which is not only invariant under rigid rotations but also under an independent rotation of the uniaxial direction, and show that this higher symmetry strongly constrains the effects of chiral activity. We then break the elastomeric symmetry by adding a symmetry-breaking term to the free energy but still retain invariance under rigid rotations. The resulting state has the symmetry of a uniaxial solid, and we show that in a fixed background medium chiral activity generically destabilises it. The force density responsible for this {instability} vanishes as the field that breaks the elastomeric symmetry goes to zero. Further, the presence of the symmetry-breaking field also allows for an additional odd elastic force density that generically destabilises momentum-conserved chiral and uniaxial solids in the inertial regime.

items.title: A Stress-Induced Tetragonal Distortion in K2OsCl6 under Pressure
items.summary: The structural behaviour of cubic (Fm-3m) K2OsCl6 under compression was investigated to 35.4 GPa using angle-dispersive synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction. Upon increasing pressure, K2OsCl6 undergoes a sequence of structural transformations from the ambient-pressure cubic phase to a tetragonal (P4/mnc) phase above 9.5(3) GPa, followed by a transition to a monoclinic (P21/n) phase beginning at approximately 14.2 GPa. The tetragonal and monoclinic phases coexist over the pressure range 14.2-17.2 GPa, while the monoclinic phase is observed as the sole phase at 17.9 GPa and remains stable up to the maximum pressure investigated. Analysis of the diffraction profiles and unit-cell parameters indicates that the intermediate tetragonal structure is likely associated with stress-induced symmetry lowering rather than a distinct thermodynamic phase. This distortion, which is adequately described by the tetragonal P4/mnc space group, is attributed to non-hydrostatic deviatoric stresses arising from the pressure-transmitting medium. Equation-of-state analysis reveals a pronounced reduction in compressibility across the structural transitions, with the bulk modulus increasing from 26(2) GPa for the cubic phase to 71(3) GPa for the monoclinic phase. The pressure-induced structural sequence is analogous to that reported for related compounds such as K2IrCl6, although the transitions in K2OsCl6 occur at lower pressures. All structural transformations are reversible upon decompression.

items.title: Outram Park Part II: Agentic Verification, Validation and Documentation as a Human Review Gate for Nuclear Data and Neutronics Software
items.summary: NJOY21 is part of a modernisation effort for NJOY2016, but mostly consists of C++ wrappers. Agentic coding represents a unique opporunity for NJOY modernisation in Rust, but agents require human expert supervision, which may be in short supply. Moreover, expert human review is the bottleneck in agentic software development as human resources are limited in this context. This work describes a methodology for how a human manager of AI agents can reasonably translate and refactor scientific software with limited domain expertise using principles borrowed from nuclear quality assurance documents. Moreover, it presents a methodology for when to allocate limited human resources for reviewing the agentically generated code. This methodology centres on agentic V&V and documentation, and it is demonstrated via construction of Monte Carlo web demos for the Rust fork of NJOY an Outram Monte Carlo (OutramMC), Rust ports of NJOY2016 and OpenMC, in Outram Park. In this work, an integrated pipeline for the Rust port of NJOY and OutramMC was demonstrated in web demos, and code to code verification and validation was performed with ICSBEP benchmarks for Godiva, HST009 and LCT008. ACE files produced with Outram Park's NJOY port were identical for more than 30 ACE files. These web demos also served as part of agentic documentation, which prepared the codebase for human review.

items.title: Odd-Parity Perturbations of Geometrically Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair
items.summary: In this paper, we study linear perturbations of a geometrically regular black hole supported by a constrained $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ scalar triplet in the hedgehog configuration. Since the individual background scalars depend explicitly on the angular coordinates, the decoupling of polar and axial perturbations cannot be concluded from the spherical form of the metric or the energy--momentum tensor alone. To settle this point, we introduce the polar and axial metric and triplet amplitudes simultaneously and derive the corresponding projections of the radiative linearized Einstein--matter equations for $\ell\geq2$. The polar equations contain only polar amplitudes, whereas the axial equations contain only axial amplitudes; hence, the two off-diagonal blocks vanish at linear order. The resulting odd-parity sector forms a closed Einstein--scalar system in which a tangent perturbation of the scalar triplet is coupled to the Regge--Wheeler metric amplitudes. We show that its scalar equation has a second-order hyperbolic principal part whenever $K_Y\neq0$, and that, for the nonlinear kinetic function supporting the background, $K_Y>0$ throughout the black-hole exterior. The coefficient of the direct metric--scalar mixing is largest at the event horizon and decreases as $r^{-4}$ at large distance, while the metric block in the vacuum limit reproduces the standard Regge--Wheeler equation and potential; the scalar kinetic coefficient simultaneously vanishes, so the full operator changes rank. These results establish linear parity decoupling and the consistency of the closed axial equations. They do not, however, constitute a proof of mode stability, which requires the reduction of the complete quadratic action.

items.title: High-Efficiency Silicon-Lithium Niobate Grating Coupler enabled by Fully-Etched Subwavelength Structures
items.summary: A new approach of silicon-lithium niobate (Si-LN) grating couplers (GCs) with a fully-etched structure is proposed. The coupling strength is engineered through subwavelength structures, allowing improved directionality. The adjoint-based inverse design method is simultaneously adopted to achieve efficient coupling between photonic circuits and fibers. Considering the birefringence of LN, the proposed Si-LN GCs are optimized and fabricated for TE mode along the crystallographic Z and Y directions. The experimentally measured coupling efficiencies are -3.3 dB and -3.9 dB along the crystallographic Z and Y directions, respectively. The measured 3-dB bandwidths are broader than 54 nm and the back reflections can be suppressed down to -15 dB over 50 nm for both directions. The proposed Si-LN GCs are realized by only single-step Si etching, offering a practical solution for fast device prototyping in Si-LN photonic integrated circuits.

items.title: Revisiting the $r_s$ expansion of the uniform electron gas in $d$ dimensions: $\log r_s$ terms from coincident Mellin poles
items.summary: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy of the uniform electron gas contains $\log r_s$ terms, where $r_s$ is the Wigner--Seitz radius. Their form depends on the dimension $d$. Adapting the Mellin-transform analysis of Feynman integrals in relativistic field theory, we write the energy of the ring series and of diagrams linear in one screened interaction line in $d$ dimensions as Mellin convolutions of a radial kernel, fixed by the diagram, with a scaling function. The scaling function depends on the momentum transfer only through its ratio to a density scale. In the Mellin variable $s$, screening places poles at $s=N(d-1)$ with $N=1,2,\dots$, and the diagram places a pole at $s=d+1$ for the rings and at $s=2$ for a polarization insertion. Once the factors $\log(1/q)$, with $q$ the momentum transfer, cancel between the vertex and self-energy corrections, as the Ward identity requires, a $\log r_s$ term appears where two poles coincide. This rule reproduces the known $\log r_s$ terms in two and three dimensions. In two dimensions it gives the coefficient of the next $\log r_s$ term, $r_s^2\log r_s$, in closed form, $7/π+4\log2/π-160/(9π^2)-16G/π^2=-0.17546$~Ry with $G$ Catalan's constant. In three dimensions the screened second-order exchange diagram alone has an $r_s\log^2r_s$ term at high density and an $r_s^{-1/4}$ term at low density, and the Fock self-energy corrections cancel both.

items.title: AirMPA: A Meteorology-to-Pollution Adapter for Global Air Quality Forecasting
items.summary: Accurate real-time forecasting of atmospheric pollutants is essential for reducing exposure risks and improving public health. Traditional numerical forecasting systems suffer from incomplete parameterizations, uncertain inputs, and high computational cost. Existing deep learning approaches improve efficiency, but often entangle meteorological and pollutant variables within unified forecasting frameworks, limiting flexibility and pollutant-specific representation learning. To address these challenges, we propose AirMPA, a decoupled autoregressive framework for meteorology-to-pollution forecasting. AirMPA predicts 13 atmospheric pollutants at 0.4° spatial resolution and 12-h temporal resolution using meteorological fields, emission priors, and historical pollutant concentrations. The model is built on an improved Swin-Transformer architecture with zonal release attention and dual-branch fusion, enabling more effective modeling of global transport continuity and heterogeneous pollutant dynamics. During training, AirMPA uses the fifth-generation atmospheric reanalysis from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ERA5) as meteorological forcing, while during inference it directly ingests forecast fields from external meteorological models, enabling stable autoregressive prediction up to 5 days ahead. Experiments show that AirMPA consistently outperforms Aurora and surpasses the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) in approximately 90% of pollutant-lead-time evaluation cases over the 5-day forecast horizon, while outperforming CAMS on all variables beyond 48 h. These results demonstrate the potential of decoupled meteorology-to-pollution forecasting for global air quality prediction.

items.title: Weak solutions for weak turbulence models in electrostatic plasmas
items.summary: The weak turbulence model, also known as the quasilinear theory in plasma physics, has been a cornerstone in modeling resonant particle-wave interactions in plasmas. Stemming from the Vlasov-Poisson/Maxwell system under the weak turbulence assumption, incorporating the random phase approximation and ergodicity, it takes the form of a integro-differential system, which describes the time dynamics of particle distribution and wave spectrum. The interaction between particles and waves can be treated as a stochastic process, whose transition probability bridges the momentum space and the spectral space. To our knowledge, there is no preceding rigorous analytical work for the quasilinear theory addressed in this manuscript. In this paper, we establish the existence of global weak solutions to the one-dimensional electrostatic quasilinear model for nonnegative, smooth, rapidly decaying initial particle distributions and nonnegative, smooth wave spectra compactly supported in a positive wave-number band. The construction uses the resonance condition to reduce the coupled system to a scalar degenerate parabolic equation, together with uniform estimates and strong convergence of the gradients of regularized approximations. When the initial wave spectrum is positive throughout a single band, we further characterize the equilibrium selected by this approximation procedure. The equilibrium uniquely minimizes a quadratic functional over a nonnegative cone and admits a geometric construction through the least concave majorant of a primitive determined by the initial data. The limiting particle distribution is non-increasing on the corresponding resonant interval and forms plateaus wherever the equilibrium auxiliary function is positive. A relative-entropy argument establishes long-time convergence to this equilibrium.

items.title: Reduced Molecular Plasma Kinetics with Non-Boltzmann Vibrational Distribution
items.summary: Vibrational kinetics can strongly affect energy transfer, chemical kinetics, and discharge behavior in molecular plasmas, but resolving all internal states is often impractical for reactor-scale simulation. Compact, physics-based vibrational closures are particularly needed when complete state-to-state (StS) data are limited. Starting from a detailed $\mathrm{H}_2$ StS plasma-kinetics framework coupled to an electron-Boltzmann calculation, this work develops a reduced vibrational-kinetics formulation. The $\mathrm{H}_2$ vibrational ladder is reduced to two non-Boltzmann groups that evolve their population and internal energy. State-resolved reaction rates and associated energy-exchange terms are projected onto the groups for subsequent tabulation in reactor-scale plasma models. StS-informed samples of the reduced-model are propagated for pulsed RF $\mathrm{H}_2$ plasmas across a scan of pulse-averaged absorbed power and compared with the corresponding StS simulations. Predictions from the sampled models reproduce the bulk plasma response, including electron density, atomic-H density, and $\mathrm{H}_3^+$ density. Discrepancies in $\mathrm{H}^-$ production and the upper-energy-group vibrational temperature persist across the sampled reductions. This indicates a limitation of the present VDF reconstruction rather than the nominal parameter choice. Tail-sensitive processes therefore require a more accurate representation of the vibrational distribution.

items.title: Measuring the Quantum Phase of Multiphoton Systems
items.summary: The quantum phase of a multiparticle system has remained a long-standing mystery in quantum physics. The absence of a phase operator that faithfully represents this physical quantity has prevented the formulation of a meaningful uncertainty relation with particle number. Here, we resolve this problem by measuring, for the first time, the quantum phase of multiparticle systems containing up to fifteen particles. We achieve this through a new quantum state tomography scheme that combines homodyne interferometry with photon-number-resolving detection. This approach enables us to reconstruct complementary photon-number and phase representations and establish the corresponding number-phase uncertainty relation. Our measurements further provide access to the mutually unbiased basis of a multiparticle system, a fundamental resource for multiparticle quantum information processing. Furthermore, we report the spatially resolved characterization of the quantum phase. These results provide an operational framework for measuring quantum phase in multiparticle systems, with implications for fundamental quantum physics and scalable multiparticle quantum technologies.

items.title: Controllable localization and manipulation of optical hollow traps by means of optical-vortex diffraction
items.summary: An optical vortex (OV) is coupled with the local intensity zero and is thus a field configuration suitable for "hollow" optical traps and optical tweezers. When an incident circular OV beam experiences diffraction at a rectilinear screen edge (SE), and the conditions of weak diffraction perturbation (the SE is far enough from the beam axis) are fulfilled, the main consequence is the OV-core displacement from its initial (axial) position. Based on the model of incident Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beam, we investigate analytically and numerically the ways of controlling the OV-core position in the diffracted-field cross section by means of changing the SE position with respect to the incident-beam axis. The results show that regulating the SE position with ~1 mcm accuracy (which is available for existing mechanical tools), controllable OV-core motion with a sub-nanometer accuracy can be realized. Possible modifications of this motion depending on the incident beam topological charge, wavefront curvature, SE properties (semitransparent screen, phase-step screen) and the distance between the diffraction plane and the observation plane are analyzed. The conditions most favorable for the micro-object trapping and manipulation are specified and discussed.

items.title: All-Dielectric Tight-Binding Photonics via a Band-Gap Vacuum
items.summary: Tight-binding photonics bridges condensed-matter physics and optics, providing a powerful framework for engineering band structures and topological phases with light. For photons, however, the vacuum is gapless, so resonators in air carry radiative tails that produce spurious long-range couplings. Here we embed resonators in a photonic band-gap vacuum (BgV), a photonic crystal whose band gap plays for photons the role vacuum plays for bound electrons. The BgV localizes each resonance exponentially, so designed short-range couplings define the lattice Hamiltonian. We thereby experimentally realize a faithful Benalcazar-Bernevig-Hughes Hamiltonian in an all-dielectric photonic crystal, resolving corner resonances and their orbitals in microwave measurements. Unlike the vacuum surrounding electrons, the BgV is itself designable, controlling relative couplings and closed-loop interference through its band dispersion and Bloch modes. Full-wave calculations and extracted models show that uniformly modifying the BgV, with all resonators fixed, switches the quantized polarization of a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger lattice and converts a zero-flux lattice into a $π$-flux one. We also numerically realize three-dimensional pyrochlore and hyperhoneycomb lattices with space groups $R\bar{3}m$ and $C2/c$, the latter a nodal-loop semimetal with topological drumhead surface states. These results establish the BgV as a designable vacuum for all-dielectric tight-binding photonics in two and three dimensions.

items.title: Surface charges in a Rydberg atom-nanowaveguide hybrid quantum system
items.summary: Hybrid quantum platforms based on highly excited Rydberg atoms coupled to nanophotonics devices offer a promising route toward scalable quantum networks and integrated quantum technologies. However, the close proximity of Rydberg atoms to dielectric nanostructures makes these systems particularly susceptible to uncontrolled surface electric fields that can lead to a degradation of the excitation process. Here, we experimentally investigate Rydberg excitation of laser-cooled $^{87}$Rb atoms via the evanescent field of an optical nanofiber in the presence of fiber-guided red- and blue-detuned light fields as used to trap ground state atoms in fiber-based dipole traps. We observe a time evolution of the Rydberg excitation spectrum when both the dipole trapping fields are on and the additional spectral features that appear can be suppressed by applying an external oscillating electric field to the system, strongly indicating that surface charge accumulation is responsible for the observed spectral feature. The experimental results are reproduced qualitatively by a model that incorporates DC energy level shifts arising from electric fields generated by charges deposited on the nanofiber surface. We identify Rydberg-ground state collisional ionization, which is enhanced by the dipole trapping fields, as the dominant mechanism for charge generation. These results provide new insight into charge dynamics at dielectric nanophotonic interfaces and establish practical guidelines for mitigating surface charge-induced electric fields in fiber-integrated Rydberg quantum systems.

items.title: A General Treatment of Coupled Cavity Resonators
items.summary: Consider several cavity resonators whose resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields are known, and suppose that they are coupled through apertures. How can the resonant frequencies and resonant electromagnetic fields of the resulting coupled-cavity resonator be expressed in terms of the original resonant frequencies and electromagnetic fields? This is a problem frequently encountered in radio-frequency systems for accelerators. One example is a multicell cavity used in high-energy electron accelerators. In this note, the resonant frequencies and resonant electromagnetic fields of such coupled cavities are examined as generally as possible, based only on Maxwell's equations and boundary conditions. Specifically, the response function of a cavity as viewed from its coupling ports, namely, its admittance matrix, is derived, and a formulation is developed to express the coupled resonant electromagnetic fields using this matrix. The resulting formulation shows that the coupled resonant modes can be described in terms of overlap integrals between the resonant modes of the cavities and the waveguide modes at the coupling apertures. It also shows that the coupled resonant frequencies are given by the zeros of the determinant of a matrix constructed from the admittance matrices. The results thus obtained are applied to simple systems to confirm the validity of the formulation. Numerical calculations based on this formulation are also carried out for periodic systems in an attempt to derive dispersion relations.

items.title: Connectivism as an Innovative Didactic Experience in Preservice Physics Teacher Education
items.summary: This chapter examines the use of connectivism as a pedagogical approach in preservice physics teacher education through a classroom experience conducted in a Contemporary Physics course at the Universidad Pedagógica y Tecnológica de Colombia (UPTC). The study involved 21 preservice teachers organized into four collaborative groups. Using a qualitative approach, students selected and discussed digital learning resources, interacted through WhatsApp, and prepared collaborative reports connecting contemporary physics concepts with scientific and technological applications. The analysis considered conceptual understanding, argumentation, questioning, critical thinking, relationships among concepts, and the use of digital resources. Students' reports and feedback indicated favorable perceptions of the collaborative activities and provided examples of conceptual connections, evidence-based explanations, and reflection on future teaching practices. The chapter discusses the possibilities of connectivist learning networks for physics teacher education, drawing on the findings of this particular classroom experience.

items.title: Optical Response in Spintronic Poisson Bolometers
items.summary: Analog bolometers based on temperature-dependent phase-transition materials such as vanadium oxide (VOx) and barium titanate (BTO) represent the state of the art in uncooled infrared detectors. Recently, the first room-temperature spintronic Poisson bolometer based on magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) was proposed and demonstrated as a promising infrared detector. Unlike conventional bolometers, the spintronic Poisson bolometer operates in a probabilistic regime dominated by Poissonian noise, where the response is governed by resistance fluctuations arising from thermally activated magnetization transitions. Spontaneous transitions between two metastable magnetic states occur even in the absence of incident light, and the transition probability increases under illumination. In this work, we experimentally study the statistical properties of the optical response of the spintronic Poisson bolometer under illumination. We demonstrate that transitions in spintronic Poisson bolometers, both in the absence and presence of light, exhibit Poissonian behavior, with transition rates and interarrival times modulated by incident radiation. Under illumination, we observe a 153% increase in the count rate accompanied by a 70% reduction in interarrival time. These results establish spintronic Poisson bolometers as a promising platform for probabilistic, high-speed, and high-sensitivity infrared detection at room temperature.

items.title: UV-cured PVA-collagen co-network with staining-free photodynamic activity against chronic wound bacteria
items.summary: Chronic wounds affect 1-2% of the global population and represent an unsustainable healthcare, financial and economic burden. Delayed healing is largely associated with bacterial infection and inadequate moisture balance, both of which remain difficult to control due to increasing antimicrobial resistance and the limited exudate management capacity and mechanical performance of current dressings. To address these challenges, we introduce a staining-free photodynamic material with work-light-triggered antibacterial activity, significant water-induced swelling (up to more than nine-fold increase in dry weight) and tunable wet state mean compression modulus (Ec: 76 - 289 kPa). The material was prepared by UV co-curing of an aqueous solution containing a poly(vinyl alcohol) derivative functionalised with both phenothiazine and methacrylate residues, 4-vinylbenzyl-functionalised type 1 rat tail collagen, and a water-soluble photoinitiator. Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy and Differential Scanning Calorimetry of the co-networks indicated the presence of characteristic chemical and thermal features of both components. 96-hour co-network incubation in vitro (pH 7.4, 37 degC) confirmed the significant retention of toluidine blue (> 93 wt.%), suppressed medium colouration, and an average mass retention higher than 98 wt.%. Exposure of the UV-cured samples to 10-min work light resulted in at least 1 log10 reduction in Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa viabilities, in contrast to dark-control conditions, while the metabolic activity of L929 fibroblasts remained above 90%. The antibacterial properties, staining-free photodynamic behaviour, water-induced swelling, and wet-state mechanical properties achieved via network integration with functionalised collagen, make this material appealing for chronic wound healing applications and for on-demand delivery of localised therapies.

items.title: Computing statistical solutions of a Mach 2000 astrophysical jet
items.summary: The multi-dimensional compressible Euler equations admit non-unique entropy solutions in turbulent regimes, and extreme-Mach astrophysical flows are a natural setting in which this breakdown of deterministic well-posedness becomes computationally visible. We compute statistical solutions of a Mach~2000 astrophysical jet, defined as the pushforward of an initial probability measure through a vectorial lattice Boltzmann method, by Monte Carlo sampling with $M=1000$ realizations on grids of up to $12.8$ million cells. Under mesh refinement the individual realizations diverge pathwise, while the statistical solution converges: Wasserstein distances of the one- and two-point marginals, the ensemble mean, and the ensemble standard deviation all exhibit stable positive convergence rates. A spatially resolved analysis along the jet axis traces this dichotomy to the structure of the one-point laws, which are numerically Dirac in the undisturbed core, skewed in the sheared turbulent regions, and intermittent two-state mixtures at the random leading front. We conclude that the computed statistical solution is non-Dirac and remains stable in the extreme compressible regime, in which no strong solution is expected to exist.

items.title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
items.summary: Bone scaffolds must reconcile a macroscale mechanical response with microscale geometric feasibility, yet conventional approaches to their design restrict attainable constitutive properties. This work presents a concurrent two-scale topology optimization framework; a conditional rectified flow generates periodic lattice microstructures, which are then refined in latent space by exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities. The resulting unit-cell geometries and their spatial assignments are jointly optimized under mechanical and feature-size constraints. In a distal rabbit femur benchmark, all eight flow-started refinements produce printable cells with maximum relative errors under 1\% across six prescribed engineering moduli. Constructing the implant from a single tiled cell reproduces intact whole-femur compliance within 0.1\% and regional strain energy within 0.35\% under four loading conditions. In human femoral reconstruction, multiscale concurrent optimization produces a cortical mid-shaft scaffold with porosity 63\% while satisfying the compliance constraint within 2\% under walking and stair-climbing loads. It achieves an 84\% porosity on a proximal cancellous scaffold with strain-energy deviations below 0.25\% under the same loads. Analysis of the learned representations reveals distinct architectural families in latent space. Further, the attention heads of the rectified-flow transformer specialize for spatial shifts -- learning the analogue of a finite-difference stencil -- and coordinate symmetries, with ablations showing their influence on generated topologies. These results establish a route to printable, mechanically constrained scaffold designs. The framework is general enough for extending to many other multiscale structural design applications including topology-microstructure co-design in metal additive manufacturing.

items.title: Real-Time Approach to the Dynamical Bethe-Salpeter Equation for Finite Systems
items.summary: We present a real-time linear-response approach to solving the dynamical Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE). The polarization part of the screened interaction is obtained from time-dependent Hartree propagation of the one-particle density matrix within an orbital basis-set representation. The frequency convolution defining the dynamical kernel is evaluated as a product in time, avoiding numerical integration and storage of the full screened Coulomb operator. The resulting nonlinear eigenvalue problem is then solved directly, going beyond the static screening approximation with full-frequency dependence in the screened interaction. We validate the method by calculating the low-lying singlet and triplet excitation energies of water, formaldehyde, and acetylene. While the deterministic scaling remains $\mathcal{O}(N^6)$, the time propagation formulation is readily compatible with grid-based stochastic sampling methods, which will open the possibility for dynamical BSE calculations of very large systems.

items.title: A Unified Physics-Informed Neural Network for Modeling Coupled Electro- and Elastodynamic Wave Propagation Using Three-Stage Loss Optimization
items.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks present a novel approach in SciML that integrates physical laws in the form of partial differential equations directly into the NN through soft constraints in the loss function. This work studies the application of PINNs to solve a one dimensional coupled electro-elastodynamic system modeling linear piezoelectricity in stress-charge form, governed by elastodynamic and electrodynamic equations. Our simulation employs a feedforward architecture, mapping space-time coordinates to mechanical displacement and electric potential. Our PINN model achieved global relative L2 errors of 2.34 and 4.87 percent for displacement and electric potential respectively. The results validate PINNs as effective mesh free solvers for coupled time-dependent PDE systems, though challenges remain regarding error accumulation and stiffness in coupled eigenvalue systems.

items.title: Quantum simulation of the Dicke model in a two-dimensional ion crystal
items.summary: Quantum many-body systems driven far from equilibrium can exhibit phase transitions, chaos and entanglement, but probing these phenomena in large, nearly closed systems remains challenging. The Dicke model, which couples an ensemble of two-level systems collectively to a single bosonic mode, provides a fundamental framework for exploring these phenomena in light-matter interactions. Here we show that a two-dimensional crystal of approximately 100 trapped ions realizes this model and accesses integrable dynamical phase transitions, signatures of chaotic dynamics and fluctuation-driven spin-phonon excitation growth. Adiabatic elimination of the vibrational mode reveals ferromagnetic and paramagnetic dynamical spin phases, whereas strong spin-phonon coupling produces irregular trajectories and local relaxation consistent with quantum thermalization. Following a quench from an unstable fixed point, correlated excitation growth precedes generalized vacuum Rabi collapses and revivals; calibrated calculations identify two-mode squeezing 2.6 dB below the standard quantum limit, supported by reconstruction from spin measurements. By connecting collective dynamical instabilities to experimentally accessible signatures of quantum correlations, these results establish large ion crystals as a scalable platform for investigating non-equilibrium light-matter dynamics and generating resources for quantum-enhanced sensing.

items.title: Multiplicative Noise in Nanolaser Amplification: From Discrete Emission Events to the Additive-Noise Limit
items.summary: Laser amplification kicks off with just a few photons in the cavity, a regime where standard additive Langevin noise cannot capture the real fluctuations. To understand how this amplification begins, we map out a single-mode photon-carrier model that links macroscopic lasers directly into nanolasers. Stationary rate equations reveal that stimulated emission takes over across a tight pump window. In nanolasers, however, spontaneous processes coexist across a much broader range. Because steady-state averages miss the individual events that lead to the macroscopic photon number, we frame the stochastic dynamics around the actual discrete transitions, deriving a state-dependent diffusion approximation. The destruction of an excited carrier concurrent with the generation of a photon creates a negative photon-carrier cross-correlation. This unavoidably leads to a correlated, multiplicative Gaussian-noise framework. We track the resulting discrete dynamics with an established, event-based Laser Markov Chain (LMC) which stochastically samples pump, relaxation, emission, and cavity-loss events keeping all physical quantities as non-negative integers. Comparing its predictions to those of our multiplicative model proves that the latter reproduces excellently well the statistical behavior of photons and carrier, as long as a continuous diffusion description holds. Once the emission drops into the few-photon regime, however, the discrete model becomes indispensable. On the other hand, at large photon counts relative fluctuations shrink to a level where the state-dependence of the diffusion matrix can be ignored, to leading order, thus returning to the classic Langevin description of the system's stochastic dynamics.

items.title: NEP-kappa 2.0: A unified framework for phonon transport and nonequilibrium thermalization with machine-learning interatomic potentials
items.summary: We present NEP-kappa 2.0, a unified framework that integrates density-functional theory, material-specific machine-learning interatomic potentials, and pretrained force models for advanced phonon calculations. A common workflow enables harmonic lattice dynamics, quasi-harmonic and stochastic self-consistent phonon treatments, three- and four-phonon transport, Wigner population--coherence transport, and time-dependent phonon dynamics. Applications to 3C-SiC, BAs, and Cs$_2$AgInCl$_6$ demonstrate consistent force-model comparisons, finite-temperature renormalization, higher-order scattering, and intermode coherence. Beyond steady-state transport, mode-resolved simulations of selectively excited 3C-SiC reveal that half of the injected optical-phonon energy reaches acoustic modes within approximately 3.75 ps, primarily through one-optical--two-acoustic scattering. Acoustic branches exhibit response times differing by a factor of five, with competing scattering channels producing a transient energy overshoot. Channel-resolved entropy production and persistent nonthermal occupations distinguish interbranch energy redistribution from intrabranch thermalization. The framework connects equilibrium phonon transport with microscopic nonequilibrium energy dynamics.

items.title: Variational Principles for Hierarchical Systems of Equations
items.summary: A unified construction of variational principles (VP) is applied to hierarchical systems of equations. The adjoint set of equations involved in this construction differ from the original hierarchy set in important ways. Notably, upward and downward nature of hierarchy are reversed between the two sets, as are boundary conditions and, most significantly, whether or not the equations are factorizable. These features may make for ease of solving one of the two sets and thereby for usefulness of the VP themselves that employ both.

items.title: A fast summation method for the DFT-D3 dispersion correction
items.summary: The DFT-D3 dispersion correction is routinely added to machine learning force fields (MLFFs) trained on dispersion-deficient functionals such as PBE. Its environment-dependent pair coefficients, however, break the atom-centered separability that fast summation methods require, forcing practitioners either to truncate D3 or to accept a substantial slowdown. We introduce FourierD3, a method that uses a functional low-rank decomposition to restore this separability and enable particle-mesh evaluation in $O(N\log N)$ time without a real-space cutoff on the dispersion sum.

items.title: \textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer
items.summary: We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.

items.title: Quantized Mereology
items.summary: This paper investigates quantized mereology, which merges quantum information theory with classical mereology, the formal analysis of the part-whole relationship. It emphasizes that information about crisp mereological relations is captured by classical bits, whereas mereological vagueness involves the use of quantum bits, or qubits, to capture mereological information. Transitioning from classical bits to qubits offers a new understanding of part-whole relations among entities that are subject to mereological vagueness. This paper methodically studies the quantized mereology that arises from the classical RCC5 formalism, one of the most widely studied formalisms in Qualitative Reasoning (QR), a subfield of Artificial Intelligence. The argument is made that this method can be extended to quantize more sophisticated QR formalisms, mirroring how strategies are used in physics to transition from classical to quantum systems. The study explores: (i) the conversion of bits to qubits while understanding that these (qu)bits convey mereological information; (ii) the representation of qubit states via set partitions, acknowledging that set theory aligns more closely with classical logic than with the complex vector spaces employed in quantum physics; (iii) demonstrating that classical QR formalisms can be seen as special cases within quantized formalisms; and (iv) showing that qubits more effectively encapsulate information about vague phenomena.

items.title: Squeezing and Decoherence of Axion Dark Matter
items.summary: Bosonic particles beyond the Standard Model, such as axions, are among the leading candidates for dark matter. If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.

items.title: Rydberg Atomic Receiver for Wireless Physical Layer: A Survey
items.summary: With the escalating development of the quantum information technologies, the Rydberg atomic receiver has been envisioned as a promising alternative to its classical electronic counterparts, attracting extensive attentions from both physics and electronic engineering disciplines. By exploiting the electrical acuteness of Alkali atoms with diverse Rydberg energy states for electromagnetic field measurement, Rydberg atomic receiver is capable of surmounting the inherent limitations on the operating bandwidth and detection sensitivity of the classical electronic counterparts. Against this background, this article provides an extensive overview of Rydberg atomic communication and sensing from fundamental theory, critical technologies to practical implementations. Firstly, the milestones of the Rydberg atomic receiver evolution was introduced. Then we provide a clear understanding of Rydberg atomic receiver mechanisms from the perspective of classical communication and sensing, and highlight the unprecedented advantages over traditional electronic receivers as well as the technical challenges. Afterwards, necessary fundamentals are presented including the Rydberg atoms, typical non-coherent/coherent structures, and explicit experimental configurations, followed by discussions on state-of-the-art development of the Rydberg atomic receiver. Specifically, advancements on electric-field detection methods for accurate measurement of amplitude, phase, frequency and polarization, are extensively investigated. Based on the established methodologies, recent innovations in Rydberg atomic communication and sensing are reviewed, ranging from waveform design and array-based signal processing to radar applications like localization, imaging and remote sensing, with practical experimental results presented. Finally, we summarize the promising research trends around Rydberg atomic receiver.

items.title: Probing Flow-Induced Chain Scission in Shear-Banding Wormlike Micelles
items.summary: We investigate the microstructural dynamics of wormlike micellar (WLM) solutions based on CPyCl/NaSal/D\(_2\)O under shear flow using spatially resolved rheo-diffusion NMR, velocity-compensated diffusion measurements, and rheo-optical imaging in a Taylor--Couette geometry. Two viscoelastic systems were examined: a non-shear-banding WLM with a molar salt-surfactant concentration ratio of \(R=0.4\) and a shear-banding WLM with \(R=0.53\). Rheo-optical and velocity measurements confirm homogeneous flow for the non-shear-banding system and the coexistence of low- and high-shear bands within the stress-plateau regime for the shear-banding system. Despite the pronounced heterogeneity in velocity and shear rate associated with shear banding, the local surfactant self-diffusivity remains spatially uniform across the gap and throughout the stress-plateau regime. Furthermore, analysis of the mean-squared-displacement scaling reveals no measurable difference between the high- and low-shear bands. These results demonstrate that the micellar microstructure remains largely unchanged despite the formation of shear bands and provide direct experimental evidence that flow-induced micellar chain scission is not a dominant mechanism governing shear banding in this WLM system.

items.title: Evaporation-Driven Nanowire Self-Assembly in an Elongated Droplet
items.summary: Drying of nanowire-laden elongated droplets is a ubiquitous process in printed electronics fabrication, where the resulting deposition pattern critically determines device performance by controlling nanowire alignment, connectivity, and percolating charge-transport pathways. However, the physical understanding of evaporation-driven deposition is still largely derived from studies of spherical droplets on homogeneous substrates. This gap limits the ability to predict and control deposit morphology in realistic printing scenarios. Here, we use mesoscale lattice Boltzmann simulations to investigate the drying of nanowire-laden elongated droplets on wettability-patterned substrates, focusing on the effects of droplet geometry, nanowire interactions, and nanowire length. The elongated droplet geometry is found to intrinsically induce distinct axial and transverse inhomogeneities in the final deposit. Increasing the effective attraction between nanowires, which mimics changes in surface chemistry or solvent conditions, can improve electrical connectivity but also promotes clustering and local ordering, reducing structural uniformity. In contrast, increasing nanowire length yields a dual benefit by improving long-range connectivity while simultaneously enhancing deposit homogeneity. Our findings provide design guidance for balancing electrical transport and structural uniformity in evaporation-driven printed electronics.

items.title: Yielding-dependent Taylor dispersion in electrokinetic-magnetohydrodynamic Casson microflows
items.summary: Longitudinal dispersion in a yielding fluid depends on the velocity distribution and on how the flow is maintained. We study a neutral tracer in pressure-assisted electrokinetic and magnetohydrodynamic flow of a Casson fluid through a slit microchannel. The nonlinear stress and velocity equations determine the yielded layers, the unyielded core and the axial flow. Mei's multiple-scale homogenization of the advection-diffusion equation then separates transverse relaxation, mean drift and longitudinal spreading, yielding the Taylor-Aris auxiliary problem and effective diffusivity. An exact pressure-driven solution gives cubic decay of the mean velocity and eighth-power decay of the dispersion enhancement near flow arrest. Under fixed pressure and electrical forcing, increasing the yield parameter from $Y=0$ to $0.7$ moves the optimum Hartmann number from $Ha_p=0.696$ to $2.634$, while the corresponding normalized diffusivity decreases from $D_T^{\mathrm C}=1.454$ to $1.015$. At fixed mean throughput and $Ha_p=1$, the trend reverses: $D_T^{\mathrm C}$ increases from $1.000433$ to $1.002311$. The homogenized energy identity traces this difference to the velocity departure from the sectional mean, including that within the unyielded core. Analytical limiting solutions, direct concentration calculations, numerical convergence studies and a coupled Casson shear test support the reduced-flow predictions. An electrolyte-based dimensional assessment identifies the magnetic optima as theoretical forcing states for representative aqueous microchannels. These results are relevant to predicting longitudinal tracer spreading in microchannels carrying fluids with a yield stress, whether pressure or throughput is controlled.

items.title: A Unified Interface Neural Network for Elliptic Interface Problems
items.summary: We develop a Unified Interface Neural Network (UINN) framework for elliptic interface problems with discontinuous coefficients. A single shared network provides a unified representation of the solution in both subdomains, while a projection--correction construction embeds the solution and flux jump conditions directly into the neural trial space. This design aligns with the classical numerical principle of incorporating interfacial physics into the approximation basis to construct interface-unfitted numerical methods. The jump conditions are therefore satisfied exactly for any network parameters. Compared with methods based on separate phase networks and numerical formulations with interface penalty terms, UINN provides a unified representation with exact enforcement of interfacial jump conditions and interface-penalty-free optimization. Those features streamline the numerical formulations and can enhance training robustness. Numerical experiments on smooth interfaces at modestly large and high coefficient contrasts demonstrate UINN's solution accuracy, near-machine-precision satisfaction of the interface jump conditions, and enhanced robustness.

items.title: Dependence of the acoustic propulsion of nano- and microcones on their orientation and aspect ratio
items.summary: Recent research revealed the orientation-dependent propulsion of a cone-shaped colloidal particle that is exposed to a planar traveling ultrasound wave. Here, we extend the previous research by considering nano- and microcones with different aspect ratios and studying how the propulsion of a particle depends on its orientation and aspect ratio. We also study how the orientation-averaged propulsion of a cone-shaped particle, which corresponds to an isotropic ultrasound field, depends on its aspect ratio and identify an aspect ratio of 1/2 where the orientation-averaged propulsion is particularly strong. To make our simulation results easier reusable for follow-up research, we provide a corresponding simple analytic representation.

items.title: Design and synthesis of laser inscribed flexible Bragg gratings containing silicon oxynitride-doped silicon thin film for authentication applications with the insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Quantum Mechanical Calculations
items.summary: Silicon-on-insulator is mostly the main driving material system for the field of silicon photonics, including PICs, due to high index contrast and compatibility with current semiconductor manufacturing processes [1]. A recent example is silicon oxynitride-doped silicon [2] discovered recently by our group, offering to set a new position for the fields of silicon photonics with a precise control of refractive index from 2.1 to 2.5 together with the photosensitivity property at different wavelengths. In this study, we demonstrate that the synthesis of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon can be performed on a flexible substrate for the fabrication of Bragg gratings (BG) at low temperatures below 100 degrees Celsius that are emerging for advanced applications. Their use in preserving ultra-fast lasers inscribed micro-information has been demonstrated numerically and experimentally due to its multispectral reflection behaviour from the ultraviolet (UV) to the near-infrared (NIR) regions. The unique structural characteristics of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon were studied at the Si L, O K and N K edges using soft X-ray absorption studies. The quantum mechanical calculations provide the potential formation mechanism of SiON-doped Si, whereas the crystal structure prediction for bulk Si3N4-xOx was conducted using the particle swarm optimization method in combination with density functional theory (DFT).

items.title: Weak-Form Recovery of Stochastic Generators
items.summary: Data-driven discovery of governing equations is well developed for deterministic systems but much less so for stochastic ones. We present a sparse-symbolic algorithm that recovers both the drift $b(x)$ and the diffusion $a(x)$ of a stochastic differential equation from a single discretely sampled trajectory. It replaces the time-indexed test functions of weak-form SINDy with state-dependent spatial kernels. Fixed-width time-window weighting induces a persistent endogeneity bias: for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process it erases the drift coefficient entirely, whatever the window shape. Spatial kernels avoid this through a martingale strong-law argument, linked to the estimating-function theory of Bibby and Sorensen. We prove consistency of the drift and diffusion estimators for the Euler-Maruyama coefficients, a $T^{-1/2}$ central limit theorem for the drift, a finite-step correction that links drift and diffusion estimation, and a correction for additive Gaussian observation noise. The theorems assume ergodicity of the Euler-Maruyama chain, which holds for the OU and multiplicative systems but not for the cubic double well, so the double-well results are empirical. The method is validated on three benchmark SDEs (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, a double well, and multiplicative diffusion), on eight further systems identified from single trajectories with elastic-net-stabilized sparse regression, and in a support-recovery experiment. Exact support recovery from one trajectory needs a long record (about $T \gtrsim 200$ on the double well) and is not guaranteed for shorter records or weakly identified systems.

items.title: Rethinking Symmetry Principles and Partial Observables With Reference Frames
items.summary: Dynamically uncoupled fields are a modelling device used in the literature on reference frames, classical and quantum. We argue that the device is not innocuous. First, uncoupled fields violate Earman's symmetry principle SP1---that every dynamical symmetry is a spacetime symmetry---and the violation, unlike the familiar Newtonian one, cannot be repaired by excising surplus spacetime structure: it arises from a deficit of dynamical structure, not an excess of spatiotemporal structure. This qualifies implicit assumptions of Earman's SP1, while leaving its diagnostic role intact. Second, uncoupled fields expose a lacuna in the partial/complete observables programme: only dynamically coupled fields can serve as bona-fide partial observables, so partial observability is derivative on complete observability. We then reinterpret the standard formalism for partial observables: qua measurable, a partial observable is a relational quantity expressed with respect to an uncoupled frame, and it remains gauge-variant. This reinterpretation vindicates Rovelli's claim that partial observables are individually measurable, against Thiemann and Adlam, and separates two properties easily conflated in the generally covariant formulations of theories: invariance under diffeomorphisms and invariance along the gauge flow.

items.title: Construction of crystal-based light sources with LWFA electron beams
items.summary: We discuss a possibility to construct a crystal-based light source (CLS) of gamma-rays using electron beams produce by Laser Wake Field Acceleration (LWFA). This state-of-the-art acceleration technique is capable of producing few-GeV, ultra-short (fs) electron beams. In the case studies presented, we demonstrate the feasibility of novel gamma-ray CLSs based on exposing single crystals to electron beams available at the ELI-ELBA. The results of rigorous numerical simulations are presented to characterise the radiation emitted emitted by 1 and 4 GeV electrons incident on a 200-micron-thick single silicon crystal along the (110) plane. The simulations were performed using the current divergence as well as a smaller value that is believed to be a realistic to achieve in the near future. We demonstrate that it is feasible to achieve a photon yield of $10^6-10^7$ photons/s in the photon energy range from 5 to 50 MeV. Looking further ahead, we also performed a similar analysis for a 4-GeV positron beam incident on much thicker targets, up to 2 mm oriented silicon crystal. In this case, the photon yield can be increased by an order of magnitude.

items.title: Microstructure-Conditioned Surrogate Models for Graded Multiscale Optimization of Mycelium Composites
items.summary: Emerging sustainable materials increasingly rely on engineered hierarchy and microstructure to achieve control of their properties and mechanical behavior. Optimizing these materials with controllable microstructures requires efficient multiscale simulations. Data-driven surrogate models for the microscale can accelerate multiscale simulations, but require large amounts of data even for a fixed microstructure. When a range of microstructures is considered, as is the case in multiscale optimization, even more data is needed to train a surrogate. To overcome this challenge, we condition a hybrid physics-data surrogate on microstructural variables using a hypernetwork. This approach enables accurate predictions of multiscale mechanical behavior for a mycelium-woodchip composite material, even when trained on small datasets. The conditioned surrogate makes multiscale simulations of functionally graded structures tractable, and we validate it against a full FE^2 simulation. We optimize a graded multiscale disk, and reduce the peak stress by 43% compared to one with a random microstructure. Then, we go one step further, conditioning the network directly on manufacturing variables that can have a complex influence on the microstructure. This is a practical route to engineer the microscale for desired macroscale behavior. This contribution highlights the benefits of microarchitectured structures and demonstrates how conditioned surrogate models enable their multiscale optimization, which will accelerate the development and design of future sustainable materials and structures.

items.title: Particle settling in turbidity currents: concentration-gradient-driven biased sampling
items.summary: We investigate the mechanisms governing particle settling in turbidity currents using Eulerian$\unicode{x2013}$Lagrangian direct numerical simulations. The Eulerian carrier flow is driven either by solutal buoyancy or particle feedback, with the Lagrangian phase comprising passive tracers or inertial particles, respectively. The effective particle settling velocity is decomposed into a fluid velocity sampled at particle positions and a particle-fluid slip velocity. The Eulerian mean profiles of these velocities are obtained using a concentration-weighted average of the coarse-grained fields. The mean sampled fluid velocity is shown to be approximately equal to the ratio of the vertical turbulent flux of particles to their mean concentration and reflects biased sampling of upward turbulent fluctuations at particle positions, despite the zero Eulerian mean vertical fluid velocity. The passive-tracer cases show that the upward bias does not require particle inertia and arises from turbulent transport acting on concentration gradients, as it persists for inhomogeneous tracer seeding but disappears under uniform seeding. For the weakly inertial regime considered here, the upward bias dominates downward-directed biases associated with particle inertia. The mean slip velocity is well approximated by the terminal settling velocity predicted for a quiescent fluid. This is consistent with a leading-order balance between buoyancy and drag in the slope-normal direction. Modelling the sampled fluid velocity from the turbulent flux and using the slip-velocity approximation yield an Eulerian prediction for the settling velocity, in good agreement with the simulation data for the dilute, weakly inertial particles considered.

items.title: Emergent Sparsity: How Many Effective Variables Survive Coarse-Graining in AlphaEarth Embeddings?
items.summary: AlphaEarth encodes each 10 m land pixel as a 64-component vector intended to support diverse global mapping tasks. Yet many scientific applications work at coarser spatial supports, for which fewer than 64 effective variables may suffice. We ask whether these vectors can be reorganized into ranked global nonlinear coordinates, how many suffice at a chosen reconstruction accuracy, and whether that number decreases with spatial scale. We thus describe effective dimension as a two-control surface over tolerance and spatial scale, rather than one intrinsic number. At each scale, a $β$-VAE scan with a common architecture produces a rank--distortion envelope, giving the smallest retained count achieved within the scanned family at each reconstruction tolerance. At 3% validation tolerance, this number falls from 24 to 7 when the scale is increased from 10 m to 78.9 km, whereas the corresponding PCA rank falls only from 46 to 38. Repeating the analysis on unit-norm targets preserves this trend.

items.title: A probability calibrator for machine-learning classifiers
items.summary: In fields such as medicine and drug discovery, the ultimate goal of a classification is not to guess a class, but to choose the optimal course of action among a set of possible ones, usually not in one-one correspondence with the set of classes. This decision-theoretic problem requires proper probabilities for the classes. Proper probabilities conditional on the features are computationally almost impossible to find in many important cases. The main idea of the present work is to calculate probabilities conditional not on the features, but on the trained classifier's output. This calculation is cheap, needs to be made only once, and provides an output-to-probability "calibrator" or "transducer" that can be applied to all future outputs of the classifier. In conjunction with problem-dependent utilities, the probabilities of the transducer allow us to find the optimal choice among the classes or among a set of more general decisions, by means of expected-utility maximization. This idea is demonstrated in a simplified drug-discovery problem with a highly imbalanced dataset. The transducer and utility maximization together always lead to improved results, sometimes close to theoretical maximum, for all sets of problem-dependent utilities. The one-time-only calculation of the transducer also provides, automatically: (i) a quantification of the uncertainty about the transducer itself; (ii) the expected utility of the augmented algorithm (including its uncertainty), which can be used for algorithm selection; (iii) the possibility of using the algorithm in a "generative mode", useful if the training dataset is biased.

items.title: Entanglement and photoelectron holography in dissociative photoionization: molecular quantum eraser
items.summary: In a double-slit experiment with a bipartite system, the visibility of interference fringes depends on the availability of which-way information. Here, we report a Bell-like state of photoelectron and residual ion in the multiphoton dissociative ionization of the D$_2$ molecule. Evidence for entanglement is provided by the correlated emission directions of photoelectron and ion, which is observed using a COLTRIMS reaction microscope. In the presence of this correlation, the holographic interference fringes contained in the photoelectron momentum distributions are suppressed, indicating the existence of which-way information. The interference pattern persists when a single ionic state is populated and thus no which-way information is available. The experimental observations and conclusions are supported by the numerical solution of the electronic-nuclear time-dependent Schrödinger equation. Our work demonstrates that coincidence spectroscopy of ions and electrons is a powerful method for studying fundamental concepts of quantum information science within the context of ultrafast light-matter interactions.

items.title: Negative partisanship drives anti-frontrunner volatility in election dynamics
items.summary: Negative partisanship---where voter mobilization is driven primarily by aversion toward an opposing candidate rather than positive alignment---profoundly reshapes modern electoral dynamics. Here, we formulate a two-dimensional piecewise map to model campaign opinion dynamics, where voter abstention arises endogenously from a latent spectrum of voter activation barriers. We show that cross-candidate rejection sensitivity triggers a non-smooth collapse of abstention, dividing the phase space into an under-mobilized regime and a fully mobilized campaign regime. In symmetric elections with radicalized voter bases, spontaneous symmetry breaking via a pitchfork bifurcation gives rise to asymmetric polling attractors partitioned by mirror-symmetric basins of attraction, where early public perceptions---encoded in initial campaign conditions---act as a deterministic catalyst selecting candidate lead lock-in long before election day. For elevated cross-rejection, the symmetric equilibrium destabilizes via a period-doubling flip bifurcation, driving persistent anti-frontrunner polling swings. Rather than predicting static candidate hegemony, our model reveals that high negative partisanship turns elections into time-sensitive dynamical systems, where final election outcomes reflect discrete sampling snapshots of an oscillating campaign trajectory.

items.title: One Component Plasmas Frequency Moments from the ISF
items.summary: Dynamic structural characteristics of classical one component plasmas (OCP) are an essential tool for understanding of strongly coupled plasmas through experiments and numerical simulations. Here, instead of the dynamic structure factor, we focus our attention on the intermediate scattering function (ISF). Theoretical results are compared to those of obtained by the method of molecular dynamics (MD).

items.title: The chair challenge: can mechanics really tell men from women? A centre-of-mass analysis of a viral party trick
items.summary: In the "chair challenge" a person stands several foot lengths from a wall, bends forward until the head touches the wall, lifts a chair and tries to stand up. Online videos suggest that women can do this and men cannot, supposedly because women have a lower centre of mass or men have larger feet. We model the body as a planar chain of rigid segments with standard biomechanical parameters and search all postures allowed by the rules for the one that places the combined centre of mass of body and chair furthest back. As a rule of thumb, the largest toe-wall distance is roughly the trunk-plus-head length minus the distance from hip to centre of mass. For a slow, static rise this limit is 2.36 foot lengths for the male and 2.49 foot lengths for the female reference model, just short of the customary 2.5 foot lengths. The limit is set mainly by trunk-plus-head length relative to foot length, not by the height of the centre of mass; in centimetres the male model actually has more room. With the body proportions of 6068 participants in the 2012 US Army anthropometric survey, the sex difference shrinks from 0.13 to 0.03-0.05 foot lengths, half to one European shoe size. Individually, only 13% of men and 22% of women would pass statically, and predicting sex from the outcome is right in 54-68% of cases (for equal numbers of men and women), against 50% for a coin and 83% for a tape measure. Shoes, age and momentum matter more than the residual sex difference. The problem suits first-year undergraduate mechanics, combining static equilibrium of an articulated body, scaling and units, an inverted-pendulum estimate and a simple classification problem. The chair challenge is a fine demonstration of static equilibrium and a lousy sex predictor.

items.title: STORM: RDMA-based Monte Carlo Transport Scheme for Distributed-Memory Particle Simulations
items.summary: Monte Carlo particle transport enables high-fidelity astrophysical radiation and neutrino simulations - from core-collapse supernovae and neutron-star mergers to accretion flows - by handling multidimensional geometries, frequency dependence, and moving media without angular discretization. However, inter-rank communication limits scalability on unstructured meshes: standard two-sided MPI requires receivers to post receives and poll completions, creating per-iteration progress overhead that grows with the number of communication partners. Such problems have not demonstrated high scaling efficiency at $O(10^4)$ cores. We present STORM (Scalable Transport via One-sided Remote Memory), an open-source library for Monte Carlo transport on general meshes, physics, and boundary conditions. STORM provides a lock-free, mesh-independent communication layer that replaces MPI's matched-send/receive semantics with Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) - one-sided operations that write directly into a remote rank's memory without involving its CPU. Each rank pair shares a single-producer, single-consumer ring buffer; RDMA writes transfer particles while receivers remain passive. A two-sided MPI backend provides a portable fallback. In an adversarial uniform-emission benchmark, the RDMA backend sustains $>97\%$ weak-scaling and $>88\%$ strong-scaling efficiency up to 13,440~cores (112~cores per network adapter), with $1.14$-$1.27\times$ speedups over the two-sided alternative. In a Hohlraum IMC benchmark at 4480 ranks, it is $1.41\times$ faster because MPI progress overhead is reduced by $6.1\times$. By decoupling communication from physics models and mesh representations, STORM removes a barrier to scaling Monte Carlo transport in astrophysical multiphysics codes, enabling coupled radiation-hydrodynamics with energy- and angle-resolved photon or neutrino transport on dynamically evolving meshes at scale.

items.title: Multigroup Implicit Monte Carlo Radiation Hydrodynamics on Moving Voronoi Meshes with STORM and RICH
