items.summary: For smooth convex--concave minimax optimization, the higher-order lower bound of Chen et al. (2026) applies to a restricted tensor-algorithm class with prescribed regularized Taylor-model updates. We establish the same bound for arbitrary adaptive deterministic and randomized algorithms, matching, up to logarithmic factors, the upper bound of Zhang et al. (2026). Fix an integer $p\ge 2$ and let $L_p>0$ bound the Lipschitz constant of the objective's $p$-th derivative on a compact convex product domain of diameter at most $D_Z>0$. Each feasible query returns the objective value and all derivatives through order $p$. For accuracy $ε>0$, set $Q_{\mathrm{tan}}=L_pD_Z^p/ε$ for tangent residual and $Q_{\mathrm{gap}}=L_pD_Z^{p+1}/ε$ for saddle gap. Let $T_E^{\mathrm{det}}(ε)$ and $T_E^{\mathrm{rand}}(ε)$ denote the high-dimensional minimax query complexities for criterion $E\in\{\mathrm{tan},\mathrm{gap}\}$, with randomized success probability at least $2/3$ on every instance. Our lower bounds and the existing upper bound give $c_pQ_E^{2/(3p-1)}\le T_E^{\mathrm{rand}}(ε)\le T_E^{\mathrm{det}}(ε)\le C_pQ_E^{2/(3p-1)}[1+\log(3+Q_E)]^{6(p-1)}$ for sufficiently large $Q_E$, where $c_p,C_p>0$ depend only on $p$. Thus the same accuracy exponent holds beyond tensor update rules, even for randomized queries and arbitrary feasible outputs. The proof constructs a scalar convex--concave chain with exactly flat gates that hide complete derivative information. Direct product-domain error witnesses and adaptive transcript arguments establish the lower bounds for both criteria.

items.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization
items.summary: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.

items.title: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
items.summary: For each prime $p$, let $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$, the limiting probability, as $n\to\infty$, that a uniformly chosen matrix in $M_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ has primitive-root determinant. As $p$ ranges over the primes, $c(p)$ has the classical shifted-totient limiting law $μ_G$ on $[0,1/2]$. Let $μ_f$ be its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. We prove that $μ_G$ has Hausdorff dimension zero and gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Every Borel set of positive $μ_G$-mass has packing dimension at least $1/2$, and local dimension fails to exist $μ_G$-almost everywhere. Both Fourier transforms satisfy the effective bound $O((\log|τ|)^{-1/3}(\log\log|τ|)^{1/3})$. In every fixed reduced progression, the empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ approach their respective limiting laws with sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$. Over unrestricted primes, these laws and their negative-logarithmic images converge in $W_1$ at rate $O_B((\log x)^{-B})$ for every fixed $B>0$. We obtain concentration expansions to every fixed inverse-logarithmic order and prove that every sufficiently short maximizing interval for $μ_f$ contains $\log3$. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a circularly symmetric random variable whose modulus is an explicit random Euler product, with convergence of absolute moments of every real order $s>-1$. For every $A>0$, the strongly additive function $f_A$ with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ has absolutely continuous limiting laws for $f_A(n)$ and $f_A(p-1)$. We give extremal estimates and certified NTT prime searches. A lattice supplement determines second distinct nonzero squared norms of type-$A$ tensor products and gives uniform cyclotomic smoothing asymptotics at $ε=2^{-c\varphi(m)}$ for every fixed $c>0$. These statements are unconditional.

items.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
items.summary: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for Hölder potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.

items.title: Randomized Matvec Lower Bounds for Simplex-Based Matrix Games
items.summary: We prove randomized matrix-vector query lower bounds for two normalized matrix-game geometries: a Euclidean unit ball against a probability simplex, with row norms at most one, and two probability simplices, with entries of absolute value at most one. Each query returns $(Ax,A^\top y)$ for arbitrary real vectors. The algorithm must return a feasible pair with full saddle-point gap at most $\varepsilon$, with probability at least $2/3$ on every admissible matrix. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, the worst-case query complexities are $Ω(\varepsilon^{-2/3}/(\log^2(1/\varepsilon)\log\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ for ball-simplex games and $Ω(\varepsilon^{-2/3}/(\log^{7/3}(1/\varepsilon)\log\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ for simplex-simplex games. The hard instances have dimensions of order $\varepsilon^{-2/3}$ and $\varepsilon^{-2/3}/\log^{1/3}(1/\varepsilon)$, respectively, and the bounds extend to larger dimensions. These lower bounds match the deterministic upper bounds of Karmarkar, O'Carroll, and Sidford up to logarithmic factors. The proof extracts a fresh Gaussian core after adaptive two-sided queries and uses uncertainty in its smallest singular value to establish linear-system solve hardness. Two reductions transfer this hardness to matrix games by converting a small full gap into a small residual, with an additional logarithmic normalization loss only for simplex-simplex games.

items.title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
items.summary: The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $κ$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $κ$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives. The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures. Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.

items.title: Functional Model for Isometric Pairs Satisfying an Automorphic Covariance Relation - I
items.summary: We derive a canonical functional model for a pair of isometric operators $(V_1, V_2)$ acting on a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ that satisfy the automorphic covariance relation $V_1 V_2 = V_2 \varphi(V_1)$, where $\varphi$ is an automorphism of the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. This extends the classical Bercovici--Douglas--Foias functional model for commuting isometric pairs to a dynamically twisted setting. When both $V_1$ and $V_2$ are pure isometries (shifts), the model simplifies to $(M_z, M_Θ W_\varphi^*)$ acting on $H^2(\mathcal{F})$, where $W_\varphi$ is a unitary weighted composition operator on the Hardy space $H^2$ and $Θ\in H^\infty(\mathbb{D}, \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{F}))$ is an operator-valued inner function such that $M_Θ$ is a shift. As an application, we establish a complete unitary classification theorem for automorphically covariant isometric pairs by identifying a complete set of joint unitary invariants. Notably, our results are novel even in the special case of rotation automorphisms ($V_1 V_2 = q V_2 V_1$ with $|q| = 1$).

items.title: $\mathbb{C}$-Motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane Spectra as $\mathrm{MGL}$-Motivic Thom Spectra and Normed $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology
items.summary: We exhibit the $p$-complete $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Eilenberg-Mac Lane spectra $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_p$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_p^{\wedge}$ as $\mathbb{E_3}$-$\mathrm{MGL}_p^{\wedge}$-motivic Thom spectra over the motivic $\mathbb{G}_m$-loop spaces $Ω_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BGL}$ and $Ω_{\mathbb{G}_m}\mathrm{BSL}$, respectively. Furthermore, for $p=2$, we compute the $\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}$-relative $\mathbb{G}_m$-Hochschild Homology $\mathbb{G}_m \odot^{\mathrm{MGL}_2^{\wedge}} {-}$, recently introduced by Bachmann-Burklund-Dundas-Østvær, of $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$ to be $\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2[\mathrm{BGL}]$ and $(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}[\mathrm{BSL}]$ as $\mathbb{E}_2$-$\mathrm{M}\mathbb{F}_2$-algebras and $\mathbb{E}_2$-$(\mathrm{M}\mathbb{Z})_2^{\wedge}$-algebras, respectively.

items.title: Meromorphic modular differential equations for the elliptic genus of Calabi--Yau varieties
items.summary: We study differential equations -- not necessarily monic -- for Jacobi modular forms. As an application, we derive a second-order differential equation for the elliptic genus of a $K3$ surface involving the logarithmic derivative of the modular invariant $j(τ)$, and we explicitly find a third-order equation with a leading coefficient of weight 12 for the elliptic genus of any four-dimensional Calabi--Yau variety. Furthermore, we propose a simple recursive algorithm for investigating second-order differential equations with leading coefficient $E_4(τ)$ or $E_6(τ)$.

items.title: On a question of Jones on tracelike vectors, cusp forms, and von Neumann algebras
items.summary: Using the theory of von Neumann algebras, Vaughan Jones showed abstractly that there is a bridge between holomorphic cusp forms and random matrices. This bridge is supplied by a distinguished function he called a {\it tracelike vector}. He posed the following problem: construct a tracelike vector to make this bridge explicit. We carry out Jones' vision for the full modular group. We construct holomorphic tracelike vectors for every finite-covolume Fuchsian group throughout the permissible Bergman range. For the modular group at the critical parameter $s=13$, we use the resulting unit tracelike vector to assign explicit group coefficients to cusp form multiplication operators, and form positive finite random matrices from a shared Haar-distributed unitary matrix. Almost surely, their normalised traces recover all joint operator moments, first as the matrix size tends to infinity, and then as the group-word cutoff tends to infinity. We also identify the limiting mixed second moment with a series of Petersson norms that involve Maass-Shimura operators of cusp forms. The exact nature of our use of AI is detailed in the introduction.

items.title: Optimal Loss Allocation and Reflected Free Boundaries in Systemic Risk
items.summary: We study a singular mean-field control problem in which a central planner allocates losses generated by bank defaults to maximize terminal system health. Every generated loss must be borne by the surviving banks, without external capital. We prove that a cutoff, or "taxing-the-richest" rule is optimal for every non-decreasing concave terminal payoff, including the survival indicator. We construct the continuous-time optimizer by solving a time-discretized problem and passing to the limit, and establish its uniqueness in law for every non-constant payoff. The optimal flow is characterized by a novel reflected free-boundary problem. We establish well-posedness in a probabilistic solution class and prove positive-time smoothness of both the free boundary and the density of surviving banks. The main difficulty is the dependence of the limiting feedback on a moving support endpoint, which is unstable under Wasserstein convergence. We address this through stochastic-order comparisons, compactness estimates for the cutoff boundaries, and an augmented call-function formulation.

items.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
items.summary: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.

items.title: Socle formulas for rigid irreducible components of Lusztig's nilpotent varieties in type $A$
items.summary: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field. For any irreducible component $C$ of a nilpotent variety of type $A$ let $π(C)$ be the irreducible representation of a general linear group over $F$ attached to it. We show that if the multisegment of $C$ is multiplicity free, $C$ is rigid if and only if $π(C)$ is $\square$-irreducible. In this case, \[ π(C*D)=soc\bigl(π(C)\timesπ(D)\bigr),\qquad π(D*C)=soc\bigl(π(D)\timesπ(C)\bigr) \] for every irreducible component $D$, where $*$ is the binary operation defined by Aizenbud and Lapid, in accordance with a conjecture of Lapid and Mínguez. We also give a computer-assisted example in $A_7$ of a non-simple rigid module $z\ne0$ which does not admit a proper rigid submodule $y\ne0$ such that $Ext_Π^1(z,z/y)=0$, answering negatively a question of Aizenbud and Lapid.

items.title: Simultaneous avoidance of length-4 patterns in ascent sequences
items.summary: Ascent sequences form a central class of combinatorial objects, as they are in bijection with several important families such as (2+2)-free posets, Stoimenow matchings, and other Fishburn objects, and are enumerated by the Fishburn numbers. We study pattern avoidance in ascent sequences for the five patterns of length 4: $0101$, $0102$, $0112$, $0120$, and $0121$. These patterns arise naturally from recent work on pattern avoidance in related families of Fishburn objects, including Stoimenow matchings and (2+2)-free posets. We enumerate ascent sequences avoiding any subset of these patterns, with the exception of the sets $\{0120\}$, $\{0121\}$, and $\{0120,0121\}$, for which the enumeration remains open. Our results reveal that the corresponding avoidance classes fall into $16$ Wilf equivalence classes and exhibit a wide range of enumerative behaviour, including connections to classical sequences such as the Catalan and Fibonacci numbers, as well as polynomial formulas and rational generating functions; several of the sequences we obtain appear to be new. Our methods combine structural decompositions with generating-tree techniques and, in several cases, rely on reductions to shorter patterns via restricted growth functions. This work contributes to the broader study of pattern avoidance across Fishburn families and highlights further connections between ascent sequences and other combinatorial structures.

items.title: Geodesically Convex Optimization in Hyperbolic Space: Matching Lower Bounds
items.summary: We establish matching lower bounds for deterministic first-order optimization of globally Lipschitz geodesically convex functions on hyperbolic space. A global minimizer lies within distance $r$ of a known point, each query returns an exact function value and a selected Riemannian subgradient, and the target objective gap is $\varepsilon Lr$, where $L$ is the Lipschitz constant. For sectional curvature $-k^2<0$, let $ρ=kr$ and $ζ=ρ/\tanhρ$. The optimal worst-case query complexity $Q^\star$, taken uniformly over dimensions, satisfies $Q^\star(ρ,\varepsilon)=Θ(ζ\varepsilon^{-2})$ for every $ρ>0$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/64$. The new lower bound covers arbitrary adaptive deterministic queries and arbitrary outputs, matching the projected-subgradient upper rate of Zhang and Sra (2016). It removes the geodesic-span and historical-halfspace restrictions of earlier matching lower bounds. The construction extends a radial source from a convex carrier with boundary. A small residual cut selects minimizer candidates while an exact hyperbolic persistence inequality keeps every historical contact valid under future carrier growth. One fixed globally convex objective and one fixed subgradient selection consequently realize all exact replies simultaneously. Each query consumes $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of a geometric potential whose available budget is $Θ(ζ)$, yielding the product lower bound in a dimension linear in the query horizon.

items.title: Small subgraphs of large minimum degree
items.summary: In 1991, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp asked to estimate the smallest $u=u(n,d,s)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph with average degree at least $d$ has a subgraph on at most $u$ vertices with minimum degree at least $s$. We resolve this problem up to polylogarithmic factors for all even values of $s$. More precisely, we prove that every $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $d\geq s$ has a subgraph on $O_s\left(\max\left\{\frac{n}{d^{s/(s-2)}}(\log n)^{180},\log n\right\}\right)$ vertices with minimum degree at least $s$, whenever $s\ge 4$ is even. This improves a result of Janzer, Sudakov and Tomon, who obtained a similar conclusion for subgraphs of average degree at least $s$. We also prove that for every positive integer $s$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a finite family $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs with minimum degree $s$ such that $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})=O(n^{2-2/s+\varepsilon})$. This is tight and is the first result of similar kind that applies to odd values of $s$ greater than 3.

items.title: Axioms for validity: e-values, p-values and data-dependent levels
items.summary: The emerging literature on hypothesis testing with data-dependent significance levels relies on a particular extension of the Type-I error. Existing arguments for this extension are heuristic. We show it is uniquely characterized by three axioms: law-invariance, agreement with classical testing on constant levels, and the preservation of (in)validity under independent selection of the level. We find that three analogous axioms characterize the e-value as a multi-decision generalization of a test in a decision-theoretic framework. We recover the p-value by dropping the invalidity half of the independent selection axiom, showing that e-values correspond to those p-values for which a data-independent choice between two invalid p-values cannot produce a valid p-value. Our main technical contribution is to show how e-values emerge in every decision problem with a notion of validity that satisfies law invariance, the independent selection axiom, and an axiom stating that a procedure that selects an invalid procedure with arbitrarily high probability must itself be invalid. In an application to post-hoc decision-making, we justify expectation-based error rates in multiple testing and recover the 'e-closure principle' as a special case.

items.title: An Inverse Problem for the Moore Gibson Thompson Equation: Injectivity and Stability
items.summary: We study an inverse problem for the variable coefficient Moore Gibson Thompson (MGT) equation in a bounded domain, where the objective is to recover an unknown initial acceleration from boundary measurements of the acoustic field. We establish both injectivity and stability of the associated measurement operator. Injectivity is established through a unique continuation property by applying a theorem of Tataru for analytically principally normal operators. The argument relies on a factorization of the third order operator into wave type components, combined with Carleman estimates and propagation techniques in the spirit of Tataru. Stability is derived through a microlocal analysis of the forward operator, based on the construction of geometric optics approximate solutions and the identification of an elliptic pseudodifferential operator arising from microlocal back propagation of the data. These results connect the MGT inverse problem with the classical theory of hyperbolic inverse problems, such as photoacoustic tomography, while highlighting new features induced by the third order dynamics and damping.

items.title: Mutual Information Constrained Chernoff Bottleneck
items.summary: The classical information bottleneck (IB) measures the relevance of a representation $U$ of $X$ to a target $Y$ by $I(U;Y)$, which does not directly characterize the error of downstream decisions. For a binary hypothesis $Y$ inferred from many separately encoded observations, the optimal error exponent is the Chernoff information between the two conditional distributions of $U$ given $Y$. We study the mutual information constrained Chernoff bottleneck, which seeks an encoder that maximizes this Chernoff information subject to a rate constraint $I(U;X) \leq R$. We show that its optimal value $C(R)$ increases strictly up to $R = H(V)$, where $V$ merges the symbols of $X$ with equal likelihood ratio, remains at the uncompressed exponent beyond, and, unlike the IB curve, need not be concave. We further show that $k+1$ outputs suffice to attain $C(R)$, where $k$ is the cardinality of $V$. We propose an alternating algorithm that updates the encoder via a generalized Blahut--Arimoto algorithm and the Chernoff parameter $s$ via a nonlinear equation, and prove that its iterates remain feasible, with nondecreasing and convergent Chernoff information. Comparing with the classical IB for $n$ samples, we show that, whenever the two objectives disagree, the IB encoder has the smaller equivocation $H(Y|U^{n})$ at $n = 1$, whereas the Chernoff bottleneck has the smaller error probability and equivocation for all large $n$. Numerical experiments confirm the theory, and on real topic-detection data from the 20 Newsgroups corpus, compressing each word to only $17\%$ of its entropy retains $90\%$ of the error exponent and nearly the accuracy of the uncompressed classifier.

items.title: Fourth moments of prime exponential sums and exceptional sets for sums and differences of primes
items.summary: We prove a square root bound for the exceptional sets in the binary Goldbach and prime difference problems under quasi Riemann Hypothesis. If every nontrivial zero of every primitive Dirichlet $L$-function has real part at most a fixed $1/2\leqΘ<11/12$, then $E_+(N)\ll_ΘN^{1/2}(\log N)^{100}$ and $E_-(N)\ll_ΘN^{1/2}(\log N)^{100}$. Here $E_+(N)$ counts the even integers greater than $2$ and at most $N$ that are not sums of two primes, and $E_-(N)$ counts the positive even integers at most $N$ that are not differences of two primes. The common analytic estimate is a fourth moment bound of the minor arcs for a smoothed prime exponential sum.

items.title: The Minimax Cost of Smoothness in Fully First-Order Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
items.summary: We study the sample complexity of finding a point with expected hypergradient norm at most $ε>0$ in nonconvex--strongly-convex stochastic bilevel optimization using fresh, globally unbiased first-order samples with bounded variance. For lower-variable smoothness order $p\ge1$, F$^2$SA-$p$ achieves $\widetilde O(pε^{-4-2/p})$ (Chen et al., 2026), but necessity of the exponent $4+2/p$ was open. We prove matching upper and lower bounds $Θ_p(ε^{-4-2/p})$ under fixed nondegenerate regularity budgets, with constants allowed to depend on $p$. The lower bound holds for unrestricted randomized algorithms under a fixed sample budget, allows dimension to grow with accuracy, and preserves global unbiasedness and all prescribed lower-variable smoothness bounds, even with a scalar lower variable and exact upper gradients. We further characterize the minimax fixed-budget complexity under $L_j=MΛ^j(j!)^β$ for $j\ge3$: $Q_{p,β}^*(ε)=Θ\left(ε^{-4}\left[\inf_{1\le r\le p,,r\in\mathbb N} r^βε^{-1/r}\right]^2\right)$, for $p\in\mathbb N\cup{\infty}$, with constants independent of $p$. At infinite order, this gives $Θ(ε^{-4})$ for $β=0$ and $Θ(ε^{-4}\log^2(1/ε))$ for $β=1$. A gradient-difference method with weighted independent batches attains these bounds uniformly in order. Thus quantitative smoothness yields precise gains, whereas qualitative analyticity alone still permits $Θ(ε^{-6})$ complexity.

items.title: A McLennan formula for equiaccessible steady states
items.summary: Near equilibrium, the Boltzmann distribution is corrected by the transient irreversible entropy flux, a result known as the McLennan formula. By expanding around equiaccessible steady states instead, we derive an analogue that can hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. At zeroth order, steady-state occupation is determined solely by local escape rates, yielding a strong form of the active-matter principle of "low rattling." The first-order correction measures the impact of traffic imbalances on the accessibility of each state, marking the onset of nonlocal determinants of relative occupation.

items.title: Sharp High-Probability Statistical Rates for Heavy-Tailed Nonsmooth Convex Optimization
items.summary: We establish sharp high-probability statistical rates for nonsmooth stochastic convex optimization under heavy-tailed noise, closing the confidence-dependence gap in both general convex and strongly convex settings. We consider composite objectives with a Lipschitz convex loss and a known proximal regularizer, accessed through fresh unbiased stochastic subgradients. The centered noise has conditional norm and directional $p$th moments bounded by $L^p$ and $s^p$, respectively, where $1<p\le2$ and $0<s\le L$. For $T$ oracle calls and failure probability $0<δ<1/10$, set $q=1-1/p$, $\ell=\log(3/δ)$, and $A=s(L^2/s^2)^q$. With initial distance bound $D$, the minimax objective error is $Θ(D(A+s\ell^q)/T^q)$ in the nonsaturated statistical regime. For a $μ$-strongly convex regularizer, the corresponding quadratic-regime rate is $Θ((A^2+s^2\ell^{2q})/(μT^{2q}))$. These rates require domination of the deterministic and finite-variance terms; matching lower bounds require $d\ge\lceil L^2/s^2\rceil$, while the upper bounds hold in every finite dimension. The new upper bounds attain known statistical lower-bound orders, replacing the previous confidence coefficient $s^{1/p}L^{1-1/p}$ by $s$, and its square by $s^2$ under strong convexity. The key is an online inequality that separates directional fluctuations from the total second moment created by rejection sampling. Localization preserves this separation under strong convexity without additional horizon logarithms. The results characterize oracle complexity with unrestricted internal computation.

items.title: An Efficient Open-Source Framework for Thermohygromechanical Phase-Field Simulation of Drying Damage Refractory Castables
items.summary: The water removal from refractory castables is a complex process involving heat and mass transport and thermohygromechanical stresses. In order to reduce the risk of explosive spalling by improving the heat-up curves, numerical models are critical to predict the castable behavior during drying. However, most of the existing models either neglect the thermomechanical stresses or consider them as an \textit{a posteriori} assessment of the likelihood of failure. The present work proposes an open-source thermohygromechanical phase-field model to simulate the drying of refractory castables and predict the occurrence of explosive spalling. The model is based on an adaptive two-scale time-stepping strategy that allows for a significant reduction of the computational cost associated with the simulation. The model was validated against literature results and qualitative comparisons with experimental data were carried out to assess its ability to predict the failure behavior of partially saturated porous media during heating. The numerical simulations were also applied to investigate the impact of different heating methods on the risk of failure during drying. It was found that even at the significantly lower heating rates typical of refractory castable drying - compared to the fire accidents that motivate most thermomechanical studies on concrete structures - thermomechanical stresses still play a significant role in the explosive spalling, a finding well established for concrete under fire but novel for refractory castables. As a consequence, it was also concluded that the use of heterogeneous heating methods can increase the likelihood of explosive spalling. Ultimately, feasible solutions to increase the drying efficiency and safety that are compatible with the industrial setting were proposed and a free, open-source implementation of the model is provided.

items.title: Gradient descent reaches arbitrary accuracy in a fixed number of large steps on multiclass logistic regression
items.summary: We show that gradient descent (GD) with step size $η$ can achieve $\varepsilon$ optimality gap on the multiclass logistic regression loss in a number of iterations $T$ that is independent of $\varepsilon$. To do so, the step size $η$ must be chosen large enough as a function of $\varepsilon$ (and properties of the linearly separable dataset), while $T$ is a constant that only depends on the data. The relevant properties of the data include the number of points and their margin (for $T$), and one additional quantity (for $η$) that turns out to be necessary in dimension $d \geq 3$. The proofs build on the known fact that, as $η\to \infty$, suitably rescaled GD becomes the perceptron algorithm, and the latter finds a perfect classifier in $T$ iterations. A similar claim was shown for two classes in dimension $d = 2$ using other proof techniques. This result adds to previous works that showed GD on the logistic regression loss can be accelerated by taking large step sizes. Those provoke a wild, oscillatory initial phase, followed by a stable phase. We provide results of this (qualitatively different) nature, too.

items.title: Closing the Accuracy Gap in Stochastic First-Order Bilevel Optimization
items.summary: We characterize the optimal accuracy dependence for smooth nonconvex--strongly-convex bilevel optimization with stochastic first-order oracles. For globally unbiased fresh-gradient observations with bounded variance, we prove an $Ω(ε^{-6})$ lower bound matching the accuracy exponent of existing upper bounds. We consider globally Lipschitz gradients, a bounded upper gradient in the lower variable, and Lipschitz lower Hessian blocks, with target $\mathbb{E}|\nabla F(\widehat{x})|\leε$. Let $L$ be the common first-order scale, $μ$ the lower strong-convexity modulus, $ρ$ the lower Hessian-variation budget, $κ=L/μ$, and $χ=1+ρ/μ$. For $ρ\gtrsimμ$, $χ\lesssimκ$, sufficiently high accuracy, and sufficiently large dimension, we establish $Ω\left(Lκ^2Δε^{-2}+L^3χ^2κ^8σ_g^2Δε^{-6}\right)$, where $Δ$ is the initial gap budget and $σ_g^2$ is the lower-gradient variance budget. The bound holds over full Euclidean spaces against arbitrary randomized adaptive algorithms, even when every sample is the gradient of a scalar function. In the common-scale regime $ρ=Θ(L)$, the leading stochastic term has condition-number dependence $κ^{10}$, compared with the achievable $κ^{11}$ dependence. The proof embeds a sequential hard objective into an exact lower response while preserving global regularity and finite gap. A multiscale decomposition limits the gradient signal carrying each new direction, yielding the required sample complexity. We complement this lower bound with a frozen-linear-tilt estimator whose bias is proportional to lower Hessian variation. Its analysis makes this structural dependence explicit and yields matching leading rates in the specified curvature-controlled and small-gap regimes.

items.title: 86 unknowns for Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals
items.summary: Recently, Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers was solved negatively by OpenAI based on a five-contact height estimate and a pole-parity construction. In this paper, we prove further that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})$ with integer coefficients whether the equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{86})=0$ has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{86}\in\mathbb Q$.

items.title: A Gradient Sampling Algorithm for Noisy Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
items.summary: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for minimizing locally Lipschitz objective functions that may be nonconvex and/or nonsmooth. The algorithm, which is built upon the gradient-sampling methodology, is designed specifically for cases when objective and generalized gradient values might be subject to bounded, uncontrollable errors. A novel assumption pertaining to such errors in nonsmooth settings is introduced that decouples the noise that may be present due to typical errors in derivative estimates with noise that may be due to misidentification of segments of differentiability of the objective. Similarly to state-of-the-art guarantees for noisy smooth optimization, it is proved for the algorithm that, with probability one, either the sequence of objective values will decrease without bound or the algorithm will generate an iterate at which a measure of stationarity is below a threshold that depends proportionally on the error bounds for the objective function and generalized gradient values. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the algorithm can indeed perform approximate optimization robustly despite errors in objective and generalized gradient values.

items.title: The Computational Complexity of Counting Linear Regions in ReLU Neural Networks
items.summary: An established measure of the expressive power of a given ReLU neural network is the number of linear regions into which it partitions the input space. There exist many different, non-equivalent definitions of what a linear region actually is. We systematically assess which papers use which definitions and discuss how they relate to each other. We then analyze the computational complexity of counting the number of such regions for the various definitions. Generally, this turns out to be an intractable problem. We prove NP- and #P-hardness results already for networks with one hidden layer and strong hardness of approximation results for two or more hidden layers. Finally, on the algorithmic side, we demonstrate that counting linear regions can at least be achieved in polynomial space for some common definitions.

items.title: Derived derivations govern contraderived deformations of dg algebras over dg (pr)operads
items.summary: We show that Hinich's simplicial nerve of the differential graded Lie algebra (DGLA) of derived derivations of a dg algebra $A$ over a dg properad $\mathcal{P}$ is equivalent to the space of deformations of $A$ as a $\mathcal{P}_{\infty}$-algebra in Positselski's contraderived dg category. This resolves Hinich's counterexamples to the general existence of derived deformations. It also generalises his results when $A$ is homologically bounded below, since contraderived deformations are then precisely derived deformations.

items.title: Asymmetry of a class of Mellin transforms
items.summary: We consider a class of Mellin transforms $μ_η$ associated with a class of functions $η$, defined for every complex $s$ in the critical strip. We establish sufficient conditions on $η$ under which $μ_η(s)$ and $μ_η(1-s)$ cannot both vanish outside the critical line for sufficiently large imaginary parts of $s$. An application is given to the case in which $η$ is the fractional part function, for which the zeros of $μ_η$ coincide with the zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

items.title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
items.summary: Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$ A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.

items.title: Optimal eigenvalues on a metric graph with densities
items.summary: We introduce and study Laplacians on a finite metric graph endowed with generalized densities, that is, measures of finite mass. One important motivation is that this setting provides a common framework for several interesting classes of operators: discrete graph Laplacians, Kirchhoff Laplacians and Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators on graphs. Our main interest lies in spectral optimization with respect to the underlying measure. In contrast to the setting of domains and manifolds, we prove that a minimal $k$-th eigenvalue exists, whereas the corresponding maximization problem has no meaning. We then establish connections between these optimal eigenvalues and the geometry of the metric graph, including a transparent geometric characterization of the first optimal eigenvalue via the resistance metric, and a Weyl law for the higher optimal eigenvalues.

items.title: A boundary integral method for computing electron repulsion integrals in heterogeneous dielectric environments
items.summary: We present a boundary integral method for evaluating electron repulsion integrals (ERIs) in dielectric environments of piecewise constant permittivity. This generalizes conventional bare-Coulomb ERIs by incorporating screening from structured dielectric surroundings, such as the substrates and/or encapsulating layers present in modern two-dimensional-material devices. We formulate the problem as a second-kind boundary integral equation for the induced surface charge on the dielectric interfaces, and discretize it with a Nyström method on adaptively refined panels. The incident potential generated by each smooth orbital source density is evaluated by a Fourier truncated-kernel method in or near to its source box, and by fast multipole method (FMM) accelerated quadrature farther away. The linear system is solved by a Krylov iteration also accelerated by the FMM. We focus on cuboidal device geometries, and retain efficiency at high aspect ratios via close-to-touching panel quadratures. We further develop a distributed pipeline that computes the full ERI tensor, comprising thousands of orbital pairs, embedded in a single dielectric geometry. We demonstrate the method on an effective three-layer graphene slab over a Si/SiO$_2$ heterojunction, focusing on the central graphene layer represented by $198$ $p_z$-like orbitals, retaining the $2613^2$ non-negligible entries of the $198^4$-sized ERI tensor. The model is resolved on $1.3$ million surface unknowns, achieving a relative error of $0.004\%$, at a cost of $22$ node-hours.

items.title: Finite convexification by Minkowski summation
items.summary: Let $A\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact set and let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a nonempty compact convex set. We study the problem of when there exists $λ>0$ such that the Minkowski sum $A+λK$ is convex. First, we show that this finite convexification is equivalent to a uniform covering condition on the exposed sets of $A$ and $K$. We then show that another characterization is possible in terms of the covering radii of the iterated exposed sets after translating each exposed face of $K$ so that its relative centroid is $0$. In the case of convex polytopes, we show that it suffices to check the exposed sets in the first level of the iteration. We also study several special cases, such as strictly convex convexifiers, lower-dimensional convexifiers, strongly isomorphic polytopes, and the planar case.

items.title: FOMTools: Development and AI-Assisted Code Generation for First-Order Methods
items.summary: We present FOMTools, an open-source Python package for developing, analyzing, and deploying first-order algorithms for parametric linear and convex quadratic optimization. The user specifies an iteration in Python, with syntax close to its mathematical description. The package represents the iteration as a computation graph of affine and piecewise affine operations. To analyze worst-case performance, FOMTools formulates a mixed-integer verification problem that maximizes a convergence residual over a specified set of problem instances and initial iterates. For probabilistic performance analysis, a batched GPU simulator collects algorithm trajectories and computes statistical bounds on the probability of exceeding a specified convergence tolerance. From the same algorithm description, FOMTools generates specialized solver code for embedded hardware, multicore CPUs, and GPUs. The package first generates the numerical data, factorizations, and matrix-vector routines without any agent. A coding agent then translates the iteration into C or CUDA code and iteratively optimizes the implementation. After each phase, the package runs the generated code on sampled inputs and compares it with a reference execution. FOMTools also serves as a CVXPYgen backend, generating and optimizing solvers for parametric CVXPY problems. We demonstrate FOMTools on sparse coding, network optimization, optimal control, and portfolio rebalancing. The verification bounds reveal worst-case behavior that sampling misses. The generated solvers run up to two orders of magnitude faster than NumPy implementations, and they outperform hand-written GPU code and the OSQP solvers generated by CVXPYgen.

items.title: Polar Switch: Fast Muon Orthogonalization with Polynomial Circuits
items.summary: Muon, a 2024-born optimizer for language models, differs from the 2015-born spectral gradient descent mainly in its fast, GPU-friendly Newton--Schulz polynomial for orthogonalizing the gradient matrix. Accordingly, a line of research proposes faster polynomial iterations for gradient orthogonalization, such as Polar Express and Gram Newton--Schulz, both built on quintic polynomials. In this paper, we introduce Polar Switch, a new approach to polynomial gradient orthogonalization. Using simple polynomial circuits, Polar Switch reaches a given high polynomial degree at a lower FLOP cost than quintic iterations. We define a circuit as a short sequence of symmetric matrix products on a few square buffers, and circuits with $k$ products form a restricted family of odd polynomials of degree up to $2^{k+1}+1$. We choose the sequence of products in each circuit, their coefficients, and how the circuits are composed by numerically minimizing a worst-case bound on the polar approximation error. This minimization is subject to a FLOP budget that accounts for symmetric matrix multiplication kernels and a rounding constraint for numerical stability in half precision. Our two recommended Polar Switch methods have 15.5--18.7\% lower runtime than Polar Express on square matrices and 8.6--16.2\% lower runtime than Gram Newton--Schulz on rectangular matrices with aspect ratios 3.25, 3.5, and 8, with comparable approximation accuracy. In pretraining Modded-NanoGPT \#91, Qwen3-0.6B, and Gemma 3-1B, Polar Switch reaches final validation losses similar to those of established orthogonalization methods. Across the more than 14 million matrices that each of the two recommended methods orthogonalized in these runs, the estimated output spectral norms never exceed the designed bounds by more than 3\%, demonstrating their numerical stability.

items.title: A two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$
items.summary: We show that a two-dimensional complex subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ carries a unique operator space structure if and only if it is isometric to $\ell_\infty^2$; the ``if'' half is the Andô's theorem. For each of the remaining spaces we exhibit an explicit non-normal $Y \in \mathcal{M}_2$, with $(I,Y)$ an extreme point of the associated matrix ball, for which the induced linear map is contractive but not completely contractive. Since every two-dimensional subspace of $\ell_\infty^3$ has the $2$-summing property, the $2$-summing property does not imply uniqueness of the operator space structure for two dimensional complex Banach spaces.

items.title: The sum-product conjecture holds for fixed-field lattice product constructions
items.summary: We study fixed-field analogues of the lattice product construction recently used by Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov to disprove the sum-product conjecture over the real numbers. These sets are of the form $A_n = P_nG_n \subset F$, where $F$ is a fixed number field, $P_n$ can be rescaled to a set of algebraic integers whose conjugates are polynomially bounded in $|P_n \setminus \{0\}|$, and $G_n$ occupies a positive proportion of a bounded box of scale $Y_n$ in a fixed positive-rank multiplicative lattice. We prove that these fixed-field constructions satisfy the sum-product conjecture, $\max\{|A_n+A_n|, |A_nA_n|\} \ge |A_n|^{2-o(1)}$ as $|A_n| \to \infty$, with no restriction on the relative growth of the two factors. More strongly, any fixed power saving in the product set forces an asymptotically maximal sumset: there exists $C > 0$ such that, for each fixed $δ\in (0,1]$, if $|A_nA_n| \le |A_n|^{2-δ}$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $Y_n \to \infty$ and $|A_n+A_n|/|A_n|^2 = 1/2 + O_δ((\log Y_n)^C/Y_n)$. In particular, the additive-box times unit-box construction of Bloom, Sawin, Schildkraut, and Zhelezov cannot produce sum-product counterexamples in any fixed totally real number field, at any relative scales. The proof combines a bound for factorizations of algebraic integers with a more general maximal-sumset theorem for coefficient sets whose nonzero-element ratios have small Weil height. The latter controls multiplication fibers and combines a lattice strip estimate with logarithmic separation derived from the theorems of Yu and Matveev.

items.title: Solutions to Monge-Ampère Equations with Low Codimensional singularities
items.summary: We construct solutions to Monge-Ampère equations whose Monge-Ampère measures contain singular components supported on low codimensional sets. We also study the regularity of such solutions. To motivate our construction, we present examples arising from optimal transport where the potential of optimal transport maps satisfy Monge-Ampère equations similar to the ones we study.

items.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
items.summary: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.

items.title: Local Constancy of the Betti Automorphic Category over the Moduli of Curves
items.summary: Nadler and Yun conjectured that the automorphic side of the Betti geometric Langlands correspondence forms a local system of categories over the moduli of curves. We prove this local constancy conjecture using purely microlocal methods, independent of the recently established Betti geometric Langlands conjecture. In particular, it follows that the Betti automorphic category depends only on the genus of the curve, verifying a conjecture of Ben-Zvi and Nadler.

items.title: Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
items.summary: Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $η^*=αz$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The $L^p$ transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification (for $p>2$) or under suitable assumptions on the initial data (for $p\geq 2$). To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$.

items.title: Gradient-Hessian Query Tradeoffs: Matching Lower Bounds in Logarithmic Dimension
items.summary: We establish matching lower bounds for the tradeoff between gradient and Hessian queries in nonconvex optimization with Lipschitz Hessian. In normalized units, the initial objective gap is at most $T$, the Hessian Lipschitz constant is at most one, and the target gradient norm is one. For sufficiently large $T$, dimension $d \ge C\log(2+T)$, and a prescribed Hessian budget $h \ge 1$ with $h+1 \le aT$, every randomized algorithm requires $Ω(\min\{Td^{1/3}, T^{3/2}/\sqrt{h+1}\})$ ordinary queries. An ordinary query returns the value and gradient; a Hessian query returns the complete second jet and is charged only to its own budget. Both budgets are worst-case caps. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary real points, and no Hessian-norm bound is imposed. The hard input law consists of fixed, globally $C^3$, coercive functions. The construction combines sequential readouts of a continuous random matrix with localized completion blocks and reliability dimensions that vary across hierarchy levels. Premature disclosures are charged by their expected task cost, while every oracle reply remains the exact jet of the presampled objective. This yields a logarithmic dimension threshold and a depth-independent third-derivative bound. Together with a translation of the NALEN upper bound of Chen, Liu, Luo, and Zhang, the result determines the query tradeoff up to absolute constants throughout the stated range.

items.title: The Structure of the Ghost and Swapping Algebras
items.summary: The swapping algebras and the ghost algebras were introduced in the papers of Labourie and Bridgeman--Labourie to encode the Poisson structure on spaces of length functions and generalized cross-ratio functions associated to $Θ$-Anosov representations. They used these algebras to show that correlation functions are stable under the Poisson bracket associated to Atiyah-Bott-Goldman's symplectic form and that length functions are convex along the Hamiltonian flow of other length functions. In this paper, we study the algebraic relationship between these two algebras. In particular, we show that the kernel of a natural surjection from the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra is generated by five families of relations. Consequently, we obtain an isomorphism from an explicit quotient of the ghost algebra onto the extended swapping algebra.

items.title: Matching Full-Hessian Oracle Complexity for Nonconvex--Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
items.summary: We characterize the oracle complexity of finding first-order stationary points in smooth nonconvex--strongly-concave (NC--SC) minimax optimization when each query provides the full Hessian in addition to the function value and gradient. For $Φ(x)=\max_y f(x,y)$, assume that $f$ has an $L$-Lipschitz gradient, a $ρ$-Lipschitz Hessian, and is $μ$-strongly concave in $y$. Let $κ=L/μ$, let $Δ$ denote the initial value gap, and define $r=ρκ^{3/2}\varepsilon/L^2$. We establish matching deterministic upper bounds and randomized lower bounds, up to logarithmic factors and additive initialization costs. When the leading term dominates initialization, the resulting minimax complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left( \frac{ΔL}{\varepsilon^2}Ψ_κ(r) \right), \qquad Ψ_κ(r)= \begin{cases} r^{1/2}, & 0<r\le 1,\\ r^{2/7}, & 1<r<κ^{7/4},\\ \sqrtκ, & r\geκ^{7/4}. \end{cases} \] Despite the stronger oracle, the optimal complexity exhibits a nontrivial dependence on accuracy, conditioning, and Hessian smoothness. In particular, these regimes exhibit accuracy dependencies $\varepsilon^{-3/2}$, $\varepsilon^{-12/7}$, and $\varepsilon^{-2}$, respectively. The upper bounds combine second-order regularity estimates for a saddle Moreau envelope with certified accelerated reduced-dual solves and amortized warm starts. The lower bounds combine an all-derivative lift with a serial composition of private-handle constructions, using hard instances chosen independently of the algorithm's realized random seed. The resulting characterization quantifies improvements over the classical first-order benchmark under gradient smoothness alone and identifies the regime in which that benchmark is recovered.

items.title: On the uniqueness of $p$-energy on the Sierpiński carpet
items.summary: For any $p\in(1,+\infty)$, it is proved that the self-similar $p$-energy on the Sierpiński carpet is unique, up to multiplication by a positive constant.

items.title: Deep Pontryagin Learning for Continuous-Time Stochastic Control with Jumps
items.summary: We develop a deep Pontryagin learning framework for high-dimensional continuous-time stochastic control problems that naturally accommodates jump-diffusions. In contrast to direct policy optimization, which repeatedly differentiates the objective through the entire time-discretized dynamics, our method separates adjoint learning from policy improvement by explicitly incorporating state-sensitivity information from the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle. For a fixed Markov control, we first compute pathwise adjoint labels by backpropagating the reward through time along simulated state trajectories, and project these labels onto the Markov state through a supervised regression step. The control is then updated by enforcing the pointwise Hamiltonian stationarity condition. We prove that the resulting projected adjoint process satisfies a discrete-time Pontryagin principle and converges, as the time step tends to zero, to the solution of the corresponding continuous-time adjoint backward stochastic differential equation. Numerical experiments illustrate the accuracy, stability, and scalability of the approach.

items.title: Symmetric Polynomials Method for the Multiple Loewner Chains
items.summary: We introduce the technique of Symmetric Polynomials in the study of Loewner chains driven by a family of stochastic particle systems including but not limited to Dyson Brownian motion. As a first application of this technique we obtain the phase transitions at the critical parameter $κ=4$ in terms of the behavior of a class of symmetric polynomials evolving in time. We obtain new proofs of the phase transitions, we also obtain new closed-form expressions relevant for the models. In addition, we apply this method for some initial deterministic multiple Loewner evolutions. Finally, as this is, to our knowledge, the first paper analyzing this method in the context of multiple Loewner chains driven by root-system based multivariate processes, we also give an overview of potential future applications of this technique in the study of these models.

items.title: Matching Lower Bounds for Randomized First-Order Methods in Hessian-Lipschitz Nonconvex Optimization
items.summary: We establish a randomized first-order lower bound for finding an $ε$-stationary point, $\|\nabla f(x)\|\le ε$, of a nonconvex function with initial gap at most $Δ$, $L_1$-Lipschitz gradient, and $L_2$-Lipschitz Hessian. Each oracle call returns the exact function value and gradient. Let $Q_{\mathrm{rand},\mathrm{FO}}^{\infty}(ε;Δ,L_1,L_2)$ denote the minimax number of calls, maximized over finite dimensions, for arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms with per-instance success probability at least $2/3$. In the regime $ε\lesssim L_1^2/L_2$ and $ΔL_2^{1/2}ε^{-3/2}\gtrsim 1$, we prove $ Q_{\mathrm{rand},\mathrm{FO}}^{\infty}(ε;Δ,L_1,L_2) \ge c\,ΔL_1^{1/2}L_2^{1/4}ε^{-7/4}, $ where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. This matches the deterministic restarted accelerated-gradient upper bound of Li and Lin (2023) and extends the sharp deterministic lower bound of Zhou (2026) to unrestricted randomized algorithms. Thus, randomization does not improve the high-dimensional worst-case query rate. The construction keeps quadratic curvature visible while revealing the forcing directions sequentially. Large eigenspaces limit preprocessing, and a scheduled-disclosure coupling makes each fresh direction incur a separate cost.

items.title: Matching Randomized First-Order Bounds for Higher-Order Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
items.summary: Does randomization improve the worst-case first-order complexity of nonconvex optimization when the objective is very smooth? We prove that, for every fixed finite integer $p\ge3$, finding an $\eps$-stationary point requires $Ω_p(\eps^{-5/3})$ exact value-and-gradient queries, even for $C^\infty$ objectives with initial gap at most one and simultaneous global Lipschitz budgets of one for derivatives of orders $1,\ldots,p$. Together with the known deterministic upper bound, this determines the accuracy exponent up to a single logarithmic factor. The lower bound holds for unrestricted adaptive randomized algorithms, unbounded query locations, and outputs that need not have been queried. One algorithm-independent hard distribution suffices in dimension $O_p(\eps^{-47/3})$. The construction combines a block-chain potential with an exact quartic core, repeated quadratic spectra, and two static Gaussian tensor perturbations. A scheduled Haar argument controls the entire adaptive query span. An innovation-only Gaussian comparison then bounds exact transcript information without assuming finite precision or a minimum query separation. This establishes the $5/3$ randomized accuracy barrier under every prescribed finite smoothness order, extending the previously matched third-order case.

items.title: Upper tail probability estimates of suprema of Gaussian processes by matrices-A number theoretic example
items.summary: We prove new lower bounds for the upper tail probabilities of suprema of Gaussian processes. We introduce a proper matrix approach. This is continuing recent works of the author on deviations of suprema and decoupling inequalities for parametrized families of Gaussian processes. An application is given to a number theoretic example related to Wintner random Möbius function.

items.title: Curvature distributions and the Steiner formula for characteristic surfaces in the Heisenberg group
items.summary: We establish a new Steiner-type formula for smooth surfaces in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group. The main novelty is that we admit characteristic points, whose presence produces nontrivial singularities both of the distance from the surface and of its tubular neighborhood. Such singularities are reflected in the Steiner formula: the expansion up to a given order $N\geq 4$ of the volume of the $\varepsilon$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)$ of a surface $S$ is no longer polynomial, in general, taking the form \[ \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)) = \sum_{j=1}^3α_j\varepsilon^j+\sum_{n=4}^N \left(α_n+β_n\log\varepsilon\right)\varepsilon^n+o(\varepsilon^N),\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0^+ . \] More precisely, under a geometric stability condition on characteristic points, we prove that the first three coefficients are integrals over $S$ of locally integrable curvature densities, coinciding with those known in the non-characteristic case. A new phenomenon appears at order $4$, equal to the homogeneous dimension of the Heisenberg group, where logarithmic terms may occur. We show that the higher-order coefficients are naturally described by a distributional analogue of Federer's curvature measures, whose logarithmic components are supported on the characteristic set. We compute the fourth-order coefficients explicitly. The proof is based on different ingredients of independent interest: (i) an explicit formula for the cut time of homogeneous surfaces, (ii) a fine analysis of the normal exponential map through blow-ups, (iii) the study of the stability of the surface cut locus under perturbations.

items.title: Sharp Fresh-Gradient Complexity of Nonconvex-Strongly-Concave Minimax Optimization
items.summary: We characterize the fresh-gradient oracle complexity of smooth nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization, with matching upper and lower bounds up to logarithmic factors. Let $Φ(x)=\max_y f(x,y)$, where $f$ is jointly $L$-smooth and $μ$-strongly concave in $y$ on unconstrained Euclidean domains, and set $κ=L/μ$. Each query returns a fresh unbiased joint gradient with conditional variance at most $σ^2$. Given initial primal gap at most $Δ$ and dual residual $\|\nabla_y f(x_0,y_0)\|\le G$, the fixed-budget complexity of finding $\|\nablaΦ(\widehat x)\|\leε$ with probability at least $2/3$ is $\widetildeΘ(\sqrtκLΔ/ε^2+κLΔσ^2/ε^4+κ^2σ^2/ε^2+\sqrtκ\log_+(G/(ε\sqrtκ)))$, where $\log_+u=\log\max\{1,u\}$. This characterization holds when $κ$ and $LΔ/ε^2$ exceed universal constants, uniformly over finite dimensions, and the suppressed logarithms are independent of $G$. It establishes the necessity of linear condition-number dependence in the global stochastic cost and identifies a separate statistical refinement cost. A proximal method separates coarse primal progress from one final refinement, while the lower bounds apply to arbitrary adaptive randomized algorithms. Dual initialization contributes only an additive logarithmic cost, yet removing its control eliminates every finite dimension-free complexity bound, even with exact gradients.

items.title: The Riemann zeta function at the zeros of real-rooted trigonometric polynomials
items.summary: Let $P$ be a trigonometric polynomial with only real zeros. We prove that at most $\frac{2}{3}$ of its zeros coincide with the zeros of the Riemann zeta function $ζ(s)$ on the critical line. We also show that \begin{equation*} \sup_{\substack{T\leq x\leq2T\\ P(x)=0}} \log \left|ζ\left(\frac{1}{2}+ix\right)\right| \geq (1+o(1))\sqrt{\frac{\log T}{6\log\log T}}. \end{equation*} These results extend the corresponding theorems of Li and Radziwill on the zeros of $ζ(s)$ along vertical arithmetic progressions. The main novelty in our approach is the use of the work of Kurasov and Sarnak and Lee-Yang representations of Alon-Cohen-Vinzant, which show that the corresponding measure $\sum_{P(γ)=0} {\bf δ}_γ$ is crystalline.

items.title: Logarithmic corrections and interacting fronts in shifting environments and competition systems
items.summary: We investigate refined large-time propagation and front interaction in a two-species Lotka--Volterra competition--diffusion system on the real line. When the faster competitor spreads into unoccupied habitat, its invasion front generates a moving heterogeneous environment for the trailing competitor, whose front position may be influenced by the leading front's Bramson delay. We first study a scalar Fisher--KPP equation in a shifting environment. Under weighted integrability assumptions on the growth profile, we determine the logarithmic front corrections up to a bounded error and identify the corresponding limiting wave profiles, thereby explicitly demonstrating how the logarithmic displacement of the environment modifies the classical Bramson correction. The resulting asymptotics distinguish locally pulled propagation, nonlocal pulling, and two critical transition regimes. In the forced-wave regime, the invasion front remains locked to the moving environment, and the dynamics select a unique stationary profile from a one-parameter family. In the nonlocal pulling regime, the favourable habitat ahead accelerates the invasion front even though the front lags behind the environmental shift. At the threshold of nonlocal pulling, the interaction modifies only the logarithmic correction and, at a further critical parameter value, produces an additional $\ln\ln t$ term. We then apply these results to the competition system. In the nonlocally pulled regime, we determine the logarithmic displacement of the trailing invasion front, explicitly quantifying the transmission of the leading species' Bramson delay, and prove convergence to the corresponding travelling-wave profile. Finally, we establish a Liouville-type rigidity principle for a class of monotone parabolic systems. This yields uniqueness of monostable travelling waves in both competition regimes.

items.title: Matching Randomized Bounds for Finite-Sum Nonconvex-Concave Optimization
items.summary: We characterize the randomized component-oracle complexity of finite-sum nonconvex-concave optimization with a bounded dual domain. For $Φ(x)=\max_{y\in Y}n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x,y)$, the goal is to find an $\varepsilon$-stationary point of the Moreau envelope $Φ_{1/(2L)}$ with probability at least $2/3$ and a fixed query budget. Let $A=LΔ/\varepsilon^2$, $B=LD_Y/\varepsilon$, and $\bar B=\max\{1,B\}$, where $Δ$ bounds the initial primal gap and $D_Y$ bounds the dual diameter. For $A$ above a universal constant, the worst-case complexity is \[ \widetildeΘ\!\left(n+A\min\left\{ \sqrt n\,\bar B+\bar B^4,\ n^{3/4}\bar B\right\}\right). \] The bounds agree within constants for $B\le n^{1/4}$ and within one logarithm for larger $B$. Upper bounds require only mean-squared averaged smoothness and concavity of the average in the dual variable; lower bounds already hold under individual smoothness. The lower constructions cover adaptive component selection, arbitrary query norms, private randomization, and outputs that were never queried. A cone construction gives the small-diameter bound, while a serial branch construction and balanced replication give the remaining two regimes. On the upper side, a persistent estimator with primal averaging complements accelerated proximal dual steps equipped with an explicit primal certificate. The characterization takes the worst case over admissible known dual domains and finite dimensions.

items.title: Geodesics in the continuous Hecke monoid
items.summary: A permuton is a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals, the limit shape of a sequence of permutations. The sticky product of permutons is a continuous analogue of the Demazure product in the $0$-Hecke monoid; on copulas, the distribution functions of permutons, it is given by the tropical $(\min,+)$ product $\odot$. We show that every absolutely continuous rotation-invariant probability measure $ρ$ on the plane, which we call the profile, generates a one-parameter family of copulas $C^ρ=\{C^ρ_β\}_{β\in[0,π]}$. A copula in this family is defined by a pair of projections of a $ρ$-distributed random vector onto directions at angle $π-β$. Along this family, the sticky product adds angles: $$C^ρ_{β_1}\odot C^ρ_{β_2}=C^ρ_{\min(β_1+β_2,π)}.$$ Hence every non-identity element of such a family is a sticky product of two others and has roots of every natural degree. The normalized inversion number of the copula $C^ρ_β$ equals $β/π$. For the Archimedean measure $\mathfrak{Arch}$ the family $C^{\mathfrak{Arch}}$ consists of the limit shapes of the permutations of the uniformly random sorting network, found by Angel et al. and Dauvergne. For the Gaussian measure $\mathcal{N}$ the family $C^{\mathcal{N}}$ consists of Gaussian copulas and contains $\mathit{Unif}$, the uniform measure on the square (the limit shape of the uniformly random permutation); its square root within this family is the Gaussian copula with correlation $-1/\sqrt2$. By the Herschel-Maxwell theorem the Gaussian measure is the only profile whose family contains $\mathit{Unif}$; nevertheless, $\mathit{Unif}$ has another, singular, sticky square root. A discrete analogue of the Gaussian family is the geometric sorting network generated by rotating independent Gaussian points: after rotation by $π/2$ its permutation is exactly uniform.

items.title: Global Dynamics and Periodic-Annulus Bifurcations in a Reversible Quintic Liénard System
items.summary: We study the global dynamics and bifurcations of the reversible quintic Liénard system $\dot{x}=y$, $\dot{y}=a_0x+a_1x^3+a_2x^5+y(b_0x+b_1x^3)$, with $a_2\ne0$. In the original five-parameter space we treat both signs of $a_2$ and determine all global phase-portrait types on the Poincaré disc with one, three, or five finite equilibria. The analysis covers generic and generalized pitchfork, saddle-node, Bogdanov--Takens, and Hopf bifurcations; nilpotent and Hamiltonian degeneracies; bifurcations at infinity; and homoclinic, heteroclinic, limit-cycle-breaking, and periodic-annulus-breaking transitions. For a parameterized class of generalized polynomial Liénard systems whose unique finite equilibrium is the nilpotent origin with exactly one elliptic and one hyperbolic sector we establish a unique critical value of the higher-order damping parameter in the intermediate-degree range, nonexistence of a large-scale periodic annulus in the critical-degree case, and its persistence when the restoring degree dominates. Here large-scale means that the annulus closure meets the boundary of the Poincaré disc. In the degree range relevant to the quintic system the critical value gives a large-scale periodic-annulus--homoclinic-orbit-family bifurcation marked by a unique separatrix connection to infinity. For the quintic system with multiple finite equilibria periodic-annulus-breaking bifurcations arise from finite separatrix connections or separatrices reaching equilibria at infinity. Using Poincaré compactification, local normal forms, rotated vector fields, and separatrix arguments we describe bifurcation sets algebraically or by uniquely characterized critical functions. We obtain complete fixed-coefficient parameter partitions outside $Ω_{14}$ and determine the admissible critical-surface configurations and their phase portraits inside it.

items.title: Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups and Kneser neighbours
items.summary: We study Eisenstein series for orthogonal groups of even unimodular lattices of signature $(n,2)$ which arise as lifts of elliptic modular forms for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on 1-dimensional cusps. When the weight is small they have to be defined by analytic continuation. In general, they will be smooth but non-holomorphic after regularization. We show exactly in which cases we obtain holomorphic modular forms by computing the intertwining factors appearing in Langlands' constant term formula in terms of standard parameters and Rankin-Selberg $L$-values. This is related to Kneser's neighbour theory of positive-definite even lattices, which also governs the eigenvalues of these Eisenstein series. In particular, we describe the space of singular weight modular forms and construct the function $Φ_{12}$, the denominator function of the Fake Monster Algebra, as an Eisenstein series. We apply these results to show that the corresponding orthogonal modular varieties are of general type.

items.title: Matching Complexity for Second-Order Stationary Point with Sample Reuse
items.summary: We consider stochastic nonconvex optimization with sample-wise Lipschitz gradients and Hessians, and reusable opaque sample handles. Gradient and complete-Hessian evaluations are charged separately, including both endpoints of a same-sample difference. For fixed positive problem parameters and in the high-dimensional worst case, we prove that the minimax total derivative-query complexity of finding an $(\varepsilon,γ)$-second-order stationary point is \begin{equation*} \widetildeΘ(\varepsilon^{-3}+γ^{-3}). \end{equation*} The upper bound combines curvature-first randomly signed negative-curvature steps with binary-ancestor derivative estimators; a truncated increment estimate charges predictable drift linearly and martingale motion quadratically. The curvature lower bound uses a deterministic smooth bounded-gradient chain, a radial barrier, and a random rotation. The new first-order lower bound is specifically robust to persistent sample reuse and to complete-Hessian access. It uses a slowly parameterized conservative sign chain, a third-order reverse stick-breaking localization inequality, and stateful relative-entropy accounting for reusable handles. Thus the total rate is near-optimally matched for every relation between $\varepsilon$ and $γ$.

items.title: Optimal Feature-Based Newsvendor Policies under Censored Demand
items.summary: We investigate a newsvendor problem where a decision-maker observes a z-dimensional vector of covariates, and wants to learn how much stock to order given a sample of size n of censored demand data to minimize costs. Demand is censored when insufficient stock is available to meet it, and past stocking quantities are known. We propose a new model-agnostic loss function approach to estimate optimal order quantities using observational data, and characterize the optimal newsvendor policy as the policy that minimizes our proposed loss function. Our method requires only a single estimation step, can be scaled to datasets with hundreds of thousands of data points, and does not suffer from the same instabilities as inverse censoring probability weighting methods. We describe how this loss function can be implemented in linear empirical risk minimization, kernel weights optimization and deep neural network algorithms, and provide excess risk generalization bounds for their out-of-sample performance. Moreover, we show through numerical experiments that our method quickly converges to the optimal policy on synthetic data, and leads to improved performance on real world retail data.

items.title: Improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri Inequalities under Constraints: Sharpness and Quantitative Remainders
items.summary: In this paper, we study improved Sobolev and Moser--Trudinger--Onofri inequalities on the sphere under moment constraints, with particular emphasis on sharp leading constants and quantitative remainder terms.
