items.title: The Forward/Inverse Duality of Controlled Emergence:A Computational Design Program from Explanation to Engineering
items.summary: The macroscopic capabilities of intelligent systems arise from the local interactions of many simple units. When such systems are deployed in the real world, their behaviour must nevertheless be constrained, leaving designers caught between releasing adaptability and preventing loss of control, yet without formal tools to resolve the dilemma. This paper proposes a unified research program for controlled emergence that restates this tension as a pair of dual problems: the forward problem explains macroscopic behaviour from local rules, and the inverse problem solves for controllable rules and readout mechanisms from a desired target. We take an augmented quintuple as the formal object shared by both ends, and decompose ``engineering'' into three independently measurable coordinates: controllability, reproducibility, and degree of formalizability. On this basis we give three testable working hypotheses (critical scale; the cooperation and trade-off between constraint and adaptability; minimal constraint) and one feasibility criterion, which reduce inverse design from unconstrained optimization to interval checking. The program takes explicit failure boundaries as its premise, does not pursue complete control, and always preserves the system's room for self-organization. The reduced pilot experiment attached to this paper serves only to verify the executability of the research protocol and does not constitute a statistical test of the working hypotheses. This design language generalizes to multi-agent artificial intelligence, the industrial internet, and emergency response systems, all of which must confront emergence and controllability at once.

items.title: Intent Demonstration in General-Sum Dynamic Games via Iterative Linear-Quadratic Approximations
items.summary: Autonomous agents should coordinate effectively without prior knowledge of others' intents. While prior work has focused on intent inference, we address the inverse problem: how agents can strategically demonstrate their intents within general-sum dynamic games. We model this problem and propose an algorithm that balances intent demonstration with task performance. To handle nonlinear dynamic games with continuous state-action spaces, our method leverages iterative linear-quadratic game approximations and provides efficient intent-teaching guarantees: the uncertain agent's belief can be driven rapidly to the ground truth, while the demonstrating agent avoids expending effort on unnecessary belief alignment when it does not improve task performance. Theoretical analysis and hardware experiments confirm that our approach enables the demonstrating agent to reconcile task execution with belief alignment and strategically manage the information asymmetry among agents, even as its intent evolves during deployment.

items.title: Large Language Models over Networks: Collaborative Intelligence under Resource Constraints
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming society, powering applications from smartphone assistants to autonomous driving. Yet cloud-based LLM services alone cannot serve a growing class of applications, including those operating under intermittent connectivity, sub-second latency budgets, data-residency constraints, or sustained high-volume inference. On-device deployment is in turn constrained by limited computation and memory. No single endpoint can deliver high-quality service across this spectrum. This article focuses on collaborative intelligence, a paradigm in which multiple independent LLMs distributed across device and cloud endpoints collaborate at the task level through natural language or structured messages. Such collaboration strives for superior response quality under heterogeneous resource constraints spanning computation, memory, communication, and cost across network tiers. We present collaborative inference along two complementary and composable dimensions: vertical device-cloud collaboration and horizontal multi-agent collaboration, which can be combined into hybrid topologies in practice. We then examine learning to collaborate, addressing the training of routing policies and the development of cooperative capabilities among LLMs. Finally, we identify open research challenges including scaling under resource heterogeneity and trustworthy collaborative intelligence.

items.title: Stability and Stabilization of Kronecker-Sum-Coupled Multilinear Systems
items.summary: Coupled dynamical systems with multi-dimensional state structures arise in many applications such as spatiotemporal processes and large-scale interconnected systems. However, existing studies primarily focus on matrix-based coupled systems or tensor-based dynamical systems without couplings. The properties of coupled tensor-based systems remain largely unexplored. In this article, we study Kronecker-sum-coupled multilinear systems under the transform-based tensor product framework. We establish fundamental tensor spectral properties showing that stability can be characterized through lower-dimensional subsystem dynamics together with slice-wise matrix stability in the transform domain. We further develop optimization conditions for state-feedback stabilization and show that the stabilization problem can be decomposed into independent subsystem problems. Finally, we analyze the computational complexity of the proposed framework and demonstrate its substantial computational advantages over unfolding-based approaches using both synthetic systems and multi-inertia motor systems.

items.title: Low-Dimensional Hermite-Gaussian Representations for Ptychographic Reconstruction
items.summary: We analyze the reconstruction error of a low-dimensional Hermite--Gaussian (HG) ptychographic method used in real-time Wigner distribution deconvolution (WDD) reconstruction. We derive an upper bound on the discrepancy between the low-dimensional, aberration-corrected reconstruction and classical Fourier-domain WDD. The bound decomposes the reconstruction error into contributions from HG--Fourier basis mismatch and aberration-coefficient mismatch, explicitly characterizing their dependence on the number of retained HG modes, Wiener regularization, aberration mismatch, and measurement dose. Numerical experiments on simulated electron and X-ray ptychographic data characterize these dependencies and demonstrate robustness to Poisson noise. These results provide theoretical and guidance for selecting the reduced representation and reconstruction parameters, enabling computationally and memory-efficient for near-real-time ptychographic reconstruction.

items.title: Distinguishing Process Change, Instrument Fault and Data-Path Corruption in Streaming Telemetry: A Reference Implementation and Benchmark
items.summary: A reading departs from what a monitoring system expects for one of three reasons: the physical process changed, the instrument is failing, or the value was corrupted between the instrument and the software. The three call for different responses and look alike in a single sample. We state the three-cause problem, prove which pairs of causes one channel cannot separate, and propose a bank of online detectors - a Kalman tracker with CUSUM and EWMA charts on its innovation, a Hampel median with generalized-ESD confirmation, a robust noise statistic with ADWIN, exact-value checks and an optional two-channel complementary filter - combined by a deterministic, inspectable attribution rule. The detectors were merged into a public algorithm library. On 2,942 injected events of thirteen fault types the method detects 96.3% (95% interval 95.7-97.0) at 0.22 false alarms per hour and attributes 91.2% (90.6-91.8) of detected events correctly from one channel and 99.0% (98.6-99.4) with a second, rate channel; from one channel only 2 of 207 detected sensor drifts are attributed to the instrument, as the problem statement predicts. Injected into recorded industrial signals, the same catalogue is detected at 80.8% and attributed correctly at 84.5%, at 3.6 false alarms per hour. On the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark the method detects 32 of 33 experiments with a median delay of 15 s, at 46 false alarms per hour against 11 for a rolling z-score.

items.title: Robust Hybrid Finite-Time Parameter Estimation Without Persistence of Excitation
items.summary: In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating parameters of a linear regression model. Using a hybrid systems framework, a hybrid algorithm is proposed allowing the estimate to converge to the exact value of the unknown parameters in predetermined finite time. Interestingly, we show that for the case of constant parameters, the convergence property of the hybrid algorithm holds while only requiring the regressor to be exciting on a given interval. For the case of piecewise constant parameters, the classical persistency of excitation condition is required to guarantee the convergence. Robustness of the proposed algorithm with respect to measurements noise is analysed. Finally, illustrative examples are provided showing the merits of the proposed approach in terms of scalability and the applicability for the general class of time-varying unknown parameters

items.title: Reliability-Preserving Compression for Deployable Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: Post-training compression of pretrained medical segmentation models commonly uses quantization, pruning, or distillation to reduce model size and computational cost. Existing medical segmentation quantization studies mainly evaluate Dice, model size, memory, and latency, but this is incomplete for safety-critical use because compressed models should also preserve uncertainty signals that indicate unreliable predictions. We study this problem in compressed MRI/CT segmentation and formalize why Dice can remain stable while uncertainty changes. Motivated by this failure mode, we propose score-guided aggregate-validated mixed precision (SGAV-MP), a post-training compression framework that selects layer precisions under reliability constraints. SGAV-MP ranks quantization actions with a compact benefit-risk score and accepts them only after full-model reliability validation on a calibration set. Across five 2D backbones and three 3D benchmarks, SGAV-MP preserves FP32-level Dice and high uncertainty-map agreement, achieving $3.59\times$--$7.8\times$ compression in 2D and $4.73\times$--$7.82\times$ in 3D. We also report backend-supported TensorRT deployment measurements separately to distinguish runtime execution from reliability-preserving storage compression.

items.title: A New Hope for PRNU on Modern Smartphones? Evidence That Device-Specific Fingerprints Survive Computational Photography
items.summary: Photo Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) is widely regarded as the most reliable marker for source camera identification. Recent studies, however, report high correlations between images and fingerprints from different modern smartphones, which calls into question the discriminative power of PRNU on these devices. Using 30 recent smartphones under controlled acquisition conditions (e.g., no digital zoom), we investigate whether the fingerprint itself is at fault or the way it is compared. We find that a component shared by all fingerprints of the same model inflates the standard signed peak-to-correlation energy (sPCE). To counter this, we propose $Δ$sPCE: the sPCE between a query image and a candidate camera's fingerprint, minus the mean sPCE between that image and the fingerprints of the remaining candidates, in the spirit of T-norm score normalization. $Δ$sPCE improves attribution accuracy, suggesting that the device-specific PRNU signal is still present. Although the limited dataset size and the dependence of $Δ$sPCE on the candidate camera set currently restrict operational applicability, these results suggest that PRNU-based attribution of modern smartphones remains feasible when fingerprints are compared appropriately.

items.title: MixiSpeech: Progressive State Distillation for One-Step Vietnamese TTS
items.summary: Conditional-flow text-to-speech (TTS) models can achieve high synthesis quality with relatively few sampling steps, but collapsing the remaining trajectory to a single update can still cause substantial quality degradation. We propose MixiSpeech, a progressive state distillation framework that converts a multi-step conditional-flow acoustic model into a one-step generator while preserving its architecture and speaker conditioning. Rather than training the one-step model directly, MixiSpeech progressively reduces the global sampling budget through a 10-4-2-1 curriculum, with each student trained to match local teacher-integration endpoints using a masked state-matching objective. We instantiate the framework on a 710-speaker Vietnamese Matcha-TTS model trained from scratch on PhoAudiobook. On 100 shared test text-speaker pairs, direct one-step inference substantially degrades synthesis quality, obtaining 1.6846 UTMOS22-Strong and 6.21% WER compared with 2.2923 and 4.65% for the 10-step teacher. In contrast, the distilled one-step model achieves 2.2678 UTMOS22-Strong, 4.63% WER, and 2.83% CER, recovering most of the quality lost at the one-step operating point while requiring only a single acoustic vector-field evaluation. End-to-end inference time decreases from 0.0662 s for the 10-step teacher to 0.0312 s for MixiSpeech, corresponding to a 2.12 measured speedup. These results show that progressive state distillation can make one-step conditional-flow TTS practical without relying on a large multi-step sampling budget. Project page: https://mixispeech.solanai.us/

items.title: Dynamically Slimmable Speech Enhancement Network with Metric-Guided Training
items.summary: To further reduce the complexity of lightweight speech enhancement models, we introduce a gating-based Dynamically Slimmable Network (DSN). The DSN comprises static and dynamic components. For architecture-independent applicability, we introduce distinct dynamic structures targeting the commonly used components, namely, grouped recurrent neural network units, multi-head attention, convolutional, and fully connected layers. A policy module adaptively governs the use of dynamic parts at a frame-wise resolution according to the input signal quality, controlling computational load. We further propose Metric-Guided Training (MGT) to explicitly guide the policy module in assessing input speech quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the DSN achieves comparable enhancement performance in instrumental metrics to the state-of-the-art lightweight baseline, while using only 73% of its computational load on average. Evaluations of dynamic component usage ratios indicate that the MGT-DSN can appropriately allocate network resources according to the severity of input signal distortion.

items.title: Probing and Mitigating Hallucinations in Speech-augmented Language Models for Automatic Speech Recognition via Small Language Models
items.summary: The widespread success of large language models in natural language processing has spurred the development of speech-augmented language models (SLMs) to extend their reasoning capabilities from textual inputs to spoken ones. Despite impressive performance, SLMs remain susceptible to hallucinations, posing challenges in practical utility. To this end, we first probe hallucinations in SLMs for automatic speech recognition (ASR) via the lens of causal mediation and behavioral analysis. To mitigate fabricated ASR hypotheses, we propose AudioSLM, a compact yet effective ASR framework built upon a small language model, which leverages alignment cues and cross-attention layers to synergistically bolster acoustic modeling and cross-modal interactions. Experiments on LibriSpeech reveal that hallucinations arise from multi-head self-attention modules with an excessive attention bias towards textual tokens. AudioSLM considerably eases ASR hallucinations and outperforms some LLM-based ASR models.

items.title: TOMORI: A Tool-Orchestrated Mixing Operator for REAPER Interaction
items.summary: Code-based agents can operate creative software, but mixing requests often describe an intended sound without specifying the edits needed to achieve it. We present TOMORI, a code-based mixing-agent harness for native digital audio workstation (DAW) control. Custom plugins provide REAPER project inspection, optional audio measurement, and execution of model-generated Lua code. All observations return as text; delivery includes an editable project and rendered audio. TOMORI-BENCH pairs 110 human-reviewed reference edits with three instruction forms and evaluates native DAW execution end to end through operation structure, parameter precision, and rendered-audio outcomes. Across 990 cases from three primary models, explicit instructions yield high reference agreement, while abstract requests reduce project agreement and audio improvement. Paired ablations show that the full workflow improves explicit execution over a single submission. Prompted audio measurement succeeds in all 28 selected abstract cases but yields no clear overall improvement on the reference-based metrics and increases tool calls. These results expose the gap between executable DAW control and precise realization of perceptual mixing goals.

items.title: CASE: Complementary Articulation-Aware Speech Encoder to Enhance Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation
items.summary: General-purpose self-supervised speech encoders provide strong acoustic representations, but their pretraining objectives are not explicitly aligned with the visible articulatory dynamics required by speech-driven 3D facial animation. We propose CASE (Complementary Articulation-aware Speech Encoder), a complementary speech encoder adapted by contrastively aligning short speech clips with continuous 3D lip-mesh VQ-VAE latents. After adaptation, the geometry branch is removed, and the audio-only CASE representation is fused with the baseline SSL speech representation through residual cross-attention, while retaining the motion-decoder architecture and objective. Across four VOCASET baselines, CASE reduces mean lip vertex error by 2.8-6.0%, and mean full-face vertex error decreases in every system. Under the same fusion protocol, CASE yields lower mean LVE than the unadapted AV-SE stream on all four generators, with model-dependent margins. Because adaptation uses Korean speech-geometry pairs and evaluation uses English VOCASET, the result is consistent with cross-language downstream transfer under a shared English-pretrained audio-visual prior.

items.title: Age-of-Information Aware Federated Learning with Finite Speed Pinching Antenna
items.summary: This paper investigates age-of-information (AoI) aware federated learning over wireless networks with finite speed pinching antennas. In contrast to existing studies that assume an infinitely high antenna moving speed, a practical round based training procedure is considered, where the pinching antenna is repositioned during the local training phase and its feasible movement range depends on the selected devices. This creates a new coupling among device selection, antenna placement, local training time, model uploading time, and AoI evolution. To characterize the impact of antenna moving speed, the rate gain over the fixed antenna and the gap to the infinite speed benchmark are analyzed. Subsequently, an overall AoI minimization problem is formulated under a round latency deadline by jointly optimizing the selected device set and the pinching antenna position. A coalitional game based device selection algorithm is proposed, where finite speed antenna placement is incorporated into the coalition utility evaluation. For antenna placement, the optimal search region is derived by exploiting the mobility constraint and device location span, based on which a branch-and-bound (BnB) algorithm is developed to obtain the global optimum. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme can accelerate learning convergence, reduce the sum AoI, and improve device participation compared with baseline schemes, demonstrating the potential of pinching antennas for enhancing federated learning through flexible spatial reconfiguration.

items.title: HyperKKL: Enabling Non-Autonomous State Estimation through Dynamic Weight Conditioning
items.summary: This paper proposes HyperKKL, a novel learning approach for designing Kazantzis-Kravaris/Luenberger (KKL) observers for non-autonomous nonlinear systems. While KKL observers offer a rigorous theoretical framework by immersing nonlinear dynamics into a stable linear latent space, its practical realization relies on solving Partial Differential Equations (PDE) that are analytically intractable. Current existing learning-based approximations of the KKL observer are mostly designed for autonomous systems, failing to generalize to driven dynamics without expensive retraining or online gradient updates. HyperKKL addresses this by employing a hypernetwork architecture that encodes the exogenous input signal to instantaneously generate the parameters of the KKL observer, effectively learning a family of immersion maps parameterized by the external drive. We rigorously evaluate this approach against a curriculum learning strategy that attempts to generalize from autonomous regimes via training heuristics alone. The novel approach is illustrated on four numerical simulations in benchmark examples including the Duffing, Van der Pol, Lorenz, and Rössler systems.

items.title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
items.summary: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.

items.title: Shared-Private Cross-Modal Discrepancy Learning for Imbalanced Multi-Source Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Audio-visual deepfake detectors are often trained under a single dataset or manipulation regime, but multi-source training collections may contain heterogeneous attacks and uneven source distributions. Training separate detectors for each source is inefficient, while a single shared detector may be biased toward dominant source-specific patterns. We study known-source imbalanced multi-source audio-visual deepfake detection using FakeAVCeleb and LAV-DF, where source identity is supplied during training and inference. To address this setting, we build on the Multi-Scale Cross-Modal Transformer Encoder (MSCT) and propose Pre-MSCT Shared-Private Feature Fusion. Our method routes \texttt{[CLS]}-augmented audio and visual tokens into a shared stream and source-specific private streams before the first MSCT block, while retaining its internal multi-scale self-attention (MSSA), differential cross-modal attention (DCA), and feed-forward operations. The shared stream models cross-source reusable evidence, while the private streams retain source-dependent residual variations. A domain-aware gated residual fusion module injects selected private evidence into the shared representation for the main fused prediction. Experiments under two controlled source-composition protocols show improved macro and worst-source AUC compared with the MRDF and MSCT baselines. These results support shared-private cross-modal discrepancy learning in the evaluated two-source setting with known source identity.

items.title: Does Expert Supervision Improve Text-to-Speech? An Empirical Study of Preference Optimization
items.summary: Preference optimization promises to improve text-to-speech (TTS) systems by learning which speech outputs are better. External expert speech seems a natural source of preferred responses, especially when student generations contain errors. Yet demonstration quality does not establish whether the student can benefit from that supervision, or whether better target fitting will produce better speech. We examine this gap across two TTS students using real and synthetic expert speech, comparing preference objectives and direct versus bridge supervision while tracking fixed-sequence likelihoods and generation metrics. With expert supervision held fixed, objectives differ markedly in their sensitivity to preference-score scaling and the resulting generation quality. Likelihood diagnostics characterize these responses, but cannot establish their benefit: expert likelihood can increase while intelligibility worsens, or decrease while it improves. Bridge supervision highlights a distinction between mitigating degradation and improving the student: it can recover performance lost under direct training without consistently surpassing the pretrained base. Route benefits vary across objectives, students, and expert sources; neither route consistently dominates. Together, these findings distinguish demonstration quality, target fitting, and generated-speech quality as complementary criteria for assessing expert supervision.

items.title: Dynamic Constraint Reconstruction Based Control Barrier Functions for Safety-Critical Control of High-Dimensional Manipulators
items.summary: Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide formal safety guarantees for constrained nonlinear systems, but their effectiveness relies on accurate system dynamics. In high-dimensional manipulators subject to unknown disturbances and model uncertainties, fixed safety constraints constructed from nominal dynamics may become inconsistent with the actual system behavior, leading to safety degradation or excessive conservatism. This paper proposes a dynamic constraint reconstruction based control barrier function (DCR-CBF) framework for safety-critical control of disturbed robotic manipulators. An extended state observer is employed to estimate lumped disturbances online, and the estimated disturbance is incorporated into high-order control barrier functions to reconstruct safety constraints according to the estimated true dynamics. To address estimation inaccuracies, a safety margin is introduced, and a sufficient condition is derived to guarantee forward invariance under bounded estimation errors. Simulation studies on a 4-DOF excavation manipulator demonstrate that the proposed DCR-CBF method achieves zero safety violation under strong unknown disturbances while significantly improving trajectory-tracking performance compared with standard and robust CBF methods.

items.title: Safe Barrier Function Control for Grid-Following Inverters under Weak Grid Conditions
items.summary: This paper proposes a barrier control approach for the safe regulation of grid-following voltage-source-converters (VSC), operating in weak grid conditions. The proposed controller aims to enhance the transient performance and synchronization properties of the VSC, providing frequency and current limiting guarantees by employing smooth control barrier functions. First, a dynamic model is derived that includes the dynamic state interactions that are omitted in quasi-steady-state approaches, revealing the destabilizing elements both during transient and steady-state performance. Then, it is analytically proven that the proposed control law guarantees frequency limitation and inner current evolution in prescribed safety regions, while counteracting the destabilizing strong coupling between PCC voltage and injected current. In addition, sufficient conditions are formulated that guarantee the stability of the closed-loop system with respect to desired operating points. The theoretic results are verified in simulations of case studies operating in varying grid strength.

items.title: VoxDub: A Bilingual Lip-Synchronized Audio-Visual Dataset for Automatic Video Dubbing
items.summary: Automatic video dubbing (AVD) requires temporally aligned speech, transcripts, and video, yet existing corpora vary in audio quality, transcription reliability, and speaking-face visibility. We introduce VoxDub, a bilingual lip-synchronized audio-visual dataset containing 766K clips and approximately 1.58K hours of in-the-wild Chinese and English recordings, covering varied speakers, scenes, speaking styles, and linguistic content. Its curation pipeline combines speech-centered segmentation with dual-ASR transcription checking, speech quality filtering, face visibility checks, and lip-speech synchronization verification. Text-to-speech (TTS) experiments show that training on VoxDub yields lower word error rates and higher speaker similarity than training on the compared audio-visual corpora, LRS3 and CN-CVS. AVD experiments show broadly comparable speech quality and subjective synchronization. These results support the utility of VoxDub for TTS and AVD training. More details are available on the project website (https://voxdub-dataset.github.io/VoxDub/).

items.title: SemVideoSte: Agentic AI for Cross-Modal Semantic Video Steganography Communication
items.summary: We propose an agentic artificial intelligence (AI)-driven cross-modal semantic video steganography communication (SemVideoSte) scheme for secure cross-modal information transmission. Agentic AI interprets the service context to determine a semantically matched public prompt and coordinates video generation, message embedding, semantic transmission, and message recovery process. A multi-mask mechanism combines variational autoencoder (VAE) reconstruction robustness, semantic transmission robustness, and latent separability to select reliable embedding positions. Meanwhile, a private digital token controls the random seed and guidance offset to construct positive and negative terminal latent states, enabling coverless message embedding during the final diffusion sampling step. Simulation results on open-source datasets demonstrate that SemVideoSte achieves high embedding capacity, reliable message recovery, and strong semantic consistency under different channel conditions. In addition, eavesdroppers without the correct digital token cannot reliably recover the secret message, and the generated stego videos effectively resist the steganalysis detection. We further establish a prototype testbed to verify the practical feasibility of SemVideoSte.

items.title: Revisiting the Relation Between Language Model Perplexity and ASR Word Error Rate for Modern End-to-End Speech Recognition
items.summary: Language model (LM) perplexity (PPL) has historically been used as a proxy for automatic speech recognition (ASR) word error rate (WER), with prior work reporting an approximately linear relation in log-log space. Modern end-to-end ASR systems challenge this assumption because they already contain internal language modeling capacity, are often evaluated without external language models, and can now be combined with neural LMs and large language models (LLMs) through different recognition strategies. This paper revisits the relation between PPL and WER for modern ASR systems. We study whether external LMs still improve current end-to-end ASR systems, whether the PPL-WER relation remains linear in log-log space, how encoder context length affects this relation, and how LLM perplexities fit into the trend observed for standard neural LMs. We further investigate internal language modeling (ILM) in attention-based encoder-decoder systems and show that ILM subtraction changes the observed PPL-WER relation, indicating that the decoder's internal LM must be considered when interpreting the effect of external LM quality.

items.title: LEO Constellations as a Decentralized GNSS Network: Optimizing PNT Corrections in Space
items.summary: With the rapid expansion of low Earth orbit (LEO) constellations, thousands of satellites are now in operation, many equipped with onboard GNSS receivers capable of continuous orbit determination and time synchronization. This development is creating an unprecedented spaceborne GNSS network, offering new opportunities for network-driven precise LEO orbit and clock estimation. Yet, current onboard GNSS processing is largely standalone and often insufficient for high-precision applications, while centralized fusion is challenging due to computational bottlenecks and the lack of in-orbit infrastructure. In this work, we report a decentralized GNSS network over large-scale LEO constellations, where each satellite processes its own measurements while exchanging compact information with neighboring nodes to enable precise orbit and time determination. We model the moving constellation as a dynamic graph and employ a momentum-accelerated gradient tracking (GT) method to achieve stable convergence despite topology changes. Numerical simulations with constellations containing hundreds of satellites show that the proposed method matches the accuracy of an ideal centralized benchmark. Ultimately, this framework supports the development of autonomous and self-organizing space systems, enabling high-precision navigation with reduced dependence on continuous ground contact.

items.title: A Multi-View Low-Latency Direction-Sensing for Low-Altitude Network via a Multi-Armed Array
items.summary: Due to the directional antenna pattern, the received signal power decreases when the target deviates from the array boresight, degrading direction-sensing accuracy. Although rotatable arrays can alleviate this problem, repeated array rotations will induce an incremental long sensing latency. To break the dilemma of harvesting the directive gain from element and making a low-latency sensing, a multi-armed array comprising multiple subarrays with different orientations is proposed to provide wide spatial coverage encompassing low-altitude and terrestrial regions while enabling multi-view direction sensing. However, the different views lead to different direction-sensing accuracies. To fully exploit the complementary information from multiple views, two fusion methods, called SNR-weighted fusion and logistic-weighted fusion, are developed. The former directly assigns fusion weights according to the estimated received SNRs, whereas the latter employs an exponential SNR mapping to further emphasize high-SNR subarrays. Furthermore, the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is derived to provide a theoretical benchmark for the proposed multi-view direction-sensing system. Simulation results show that logistic-weighted fusion achieves better accuracy in the very low-SNR regime, while both proposed methods approach the CRLB at medium and high SNRs and maintain stable sensing performance.

items.title: NeuroAct: Advancing EEG Analysis and Decoding via Dual-Loop Autonomous Research
items.summary: EEG analysis and decoding underpin brain-computer interfaces, cognitive assessment, and sleep monitoring. Fixed pipelines and reward-driven search do not explicitly determine how signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics contribute to performance or generalization gaps, leaving intervention choice underdetermined. We introduce NeuroAct, an autonomous research agent framework for EEG analysis and decoding. NeuroAct implements dual-loop autonomous research across EEG foundation models, task-specific predictors, and model combinations. In an inner loop, research, development, and review roles use evidence on signal structure, representations, predictor behavior, and training dynamics to test hypotheses, select analyses or interventions, and refine candidates using performance, stability, and cost feedback. An outer loop distills outcomes into conditional, testable recommendations with task and model conditions, then validates and revises them on subsequent tasks.We evaluate four settings: (A) EEG General Analysis, (B) Cross-task Model Optimization, (C) Single-task Open Research, and (D) Collaborative Prediction. In Setting A, NeuroAct's 80.88 macro-average exceeds BrainAgent's 63.13 by 17.75 points. In Setting B, NeuroAct raises EEGPT's mean balanced accuracy (BA) by 7.34 points and HBN Pearson's (r) from 0.6894 to 0.7362; in Setting C, it improves ADFTD BA by 16.33 points; and in Setting D, it raises Workload BA from 79.69% to 85.02%. Experience reuse raises BCIC-IV-2a BA from 34.66% to 50.81% while reducing LLM tokens by 64.02%, indicating recommendations improve cross-task performance. NeuroAct enables evidence-guided EEG research improved by cross-task experience.

items.title: RAIL-5G: A Challenging Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for AI-Based 5G Indoor Localization
items.summary: Reliable radio-based indoor localization is essential for industrial automation, yet existing methods are often evaluated in environments that do not fully reflect the severe multipath and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions encountered in real deployments. This limits our understanding of how AI, i.e., modern geometric, unsupervised, and semi-supervised localization methods generalize to industrial 5G settings. We present RAIL-5G, a public real-world 5G NR channel impulse response (CIR) benchmark recorded in an operational railway maintenance facility. RAIL-5G covers an 811m$^2$ indoor area with eight distributed radio units, robot-mounted user equipment (UE) trajectories, high-accuracy iGPS reference positions, and severe metal-induced multipath caused by train compartments and maintenance infrastructure. We benchmark geometric time-difference of arrival (TDoA), supervised fingerprinting, unsupervised channel charting, and self-supervised wireless pretraining methods. Our results highlight the difficulty of RAIL-5G: on the full dataset, TDoA reaches 7.02m mean average error (MAE), the best unsupervised method reaches 2.46m, and supervised fingerprinting achieves 0.52m. Self-supervised pretraining reduces the labeling effort by up to one order of magnitude, but the remaining gap to supervised learning shows that robust AI-based localization under severe multipath remains an open challenge. The dataset and code are available at https://iis.fraunhofer.de/rail-5g.

items.title: ChronoChart: Setup-Agnostic Channel Charting for Label-Free Indoor Localization
items.summary: Accurate radio-based indoor localization remains challenging in multipath-rich and dynamic indoor environments. Supervised fingerprinting methods achieve high positioning accuracy by learning mappings from radio channel measurements to physical locations, but require costly position labels and frequent recalibration. Channel Charting (CC) addresses this limitation by learning low-dimensional representations of Channel State Information (CSI) without position labels, yielding channel charts in which nearby points correspond to nearby physical locations. However, prominent CC methods rely on setup-specific dissimilarity metrics, such as ADP-, CIRA-, or PDR-based distances, and on precomputed $O(n^2)$ distance matrices, limiting scalability and transferability across radio systems. We propose ChronoChart, a timestamp-supervised CC framework that requires only CSI and timestamps without prior knowledge for training. Our method jointly optimizes complementary objectives: a triplet loss using temporally derived positive and negative samples to establish coarse global structure, a temporal-proximity loss that promotes smooth trajectories in the chart, and a joint-embedding loss that enforces consistency between representations of different augmentations. Evaluated on real-world 5G, MIMO, and passive UWB data, our method matches or exceeds prior CC baselines that depend on tailored distance metrics, and remains scalable and applicable across heterogeneous radio systems.

items.title: Image Restoration with Impulse Noise Based on Minimax Concave Penalty: Grayscale and Color Images
items.summary: In today's world-where social networks play a significant role-images serve as one of the most important tools for transferring concepts. Image degradation caused by noise or blurring hinders the effective transmission of the information we expect to derive from an image. Consequently, developing image restoration methods capable of revealing crucial information is of great importance. In this work, a model for impulse noise image restoring is proposed by using a Minimax Concave Penalty. The proposed model is applicable to both color and grayscale images. Then, a numerical algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers is introduced, and the convergence of the method is analyzed both theoretically and numerically. In the final step, the proposed method is evaluated through simulations on several examples, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness.

items.title: Learning Speaker-Activity-Conditioned WavLM Speaker Embeddings with Real Conversational Data
items.summary: End-to-end neural diarization with vector clustering (EEND-VC) is a strong framework for long-form conversational diarization, where speaker embeddings are used to link local speaker decisions across windows. Conventional EEND-VC systems extract these embeddings by cutting out regions assigned to each local speaker, preferably using only non-overlapped speech. This works well when enough clean target-speaker speech is available, but it discards useful speaker evidence in overlapped regions and becomes unreliable when a local speaker appears mostly in overlap. We propose a speaker-activity-conditioned embedding extractor that adapts a pretrained WavLM-MHFA speaker verification model to extract target-speaker embeddings directly from full conversational windows. Inspired by the recently proposed diarization-conditioned Whisper (DiCoW) model for target-speaker ASR, frame-level diarization-dependent transformations inject local speaker-activity information into intermediate WavLM representations while preserving the pretrained initialization. Experiments on multiple conversational diarization benchmarks show that fine-tuning with limited real meeting data reduces speaker-confusion errors and improves EEND-VC diarization performance. The results further indicate that real conversational data provides an effective alternative to large-scale simulated-mixture training for diarization-aware speaker embedding extraction.

items.title: Receiver Design for Continuous-Time AFDM based on Pre-Filter De-Chirp
items.summary: Affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is a promising waveform for future high-mobility communications due to its Doppler robustness and diversity gain. However, existing continuous-time AFDM relies on chirp-dependent wideband receive filtering, which increases noise power and causes channel-energy leakage. In this paper, we propose an AFDM reception scheme based on pre-filter de-chirp for doubly selective channels. The coupling between de-chirp and the channel is first characterized, yielding an equivalent path representation with delay-coupled effective Doppler shifts. The discrete affine Fourier transform (DAFT)-domain equivalent channel is then derived under general transmit pulse shaping and linear time-invariant receive filtering, showing that the effective filtering kernel depends only on the relative sample offset and avoids the additional spreading caused by conventional chirp-dependent filtering. The receive-noise power is further analyzed, and an explicit expression for the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gap is obtained by the required receive-filter bandwidths. Simulations verify the theoretical SNR analysis and show that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms the conventional scheme while approaching ideal discrete-time AFDM.

items.title: Distributionally Robust Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Home Energy Management under Electric Vehicle Uncertainty
items.summary: The electrification of residential energy systems and adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) create demand-side flexibility. However, random driving behaviour makes it difficult to ensure EV readiness at departure and maintain thermal comfort. To address this, we formulate residential scheduling as a distributionally robust (DR) chance-constrained Markov decision process, whose 2-Wasserstein ambiguity set guards against tail risk and distribution shift in EV behaviour. The intractable DR chance constraint is then replaced by a sufficient tightened expectation constraint under the nominal distribution. The resulting problem is solved by a Lagrangian soft actor--critic with distributional cost critics, and an online boundary guard enforces EV reachability and thermal comfort within the actuator limits at every step. Five controllers are compared over one year in Wellington, New Zealand, under a degraded forecast. The proposed controller is the cheapest controller that meets the EV target on every day and both chance constraints under forecast error and random driving behaviour. Compared with the rule-based baseline, the only other controller to do so, it lowers the annual cost by 8.6% and the comfort violation hours by 69%. The ablation study confirms that the boundary guard ensures pointwise feasibility within the actuator limits, and the DR chance constraint reduces tail risk.

items.title: Joint Training Scattering Matrix Learning and Channel Estimation for Beyond-Diagonal Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
items.summary: Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS) generalizes the conventional diagonal RIS (D-RIS) by introducing tunable inter-element connections, offering enhanced wave manipulation capabilities. However, realizing the advantages of BD-RIS requires accurate channel state information (CSI), whose acquisition becomes significantly more challenging due to the increased number of channel coefficients, leading to prohibitively large pilot training overhead in BD-RIS-aided multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) systems. Existing studies reduce pilot overhead by exploiting the channel correlations induced by the Kronecker-product or multi-linear structure of BD-RIS-aided channels, which neglect the spatial correlation among antennas and the statistical correlation across RIS-user channels. In this paper, we propose a learning-based channel estimation framework, namely the joint training scattering matrix learning and channel estimation framework (JTSMLCEF), which jointly optimizes the BD-RIS training scattering matrix and estimates the cascaded channels in an end-to-end manner to achieve accurate channel estimation and reduce the pilot overhead. The proposed JTSMLCEF follows a two-phase channel estimation protocol to enable adaptive training scattering matrix optimization with a training scattering matrix optimizer (TSMO) and cascaded channel estimation with a dual-attention channel estimator (DACE). Specifically, the DACE is designed with intra-user and inter-user attention modules to capture the multi-dimensional correlations in multi-user cascaded channels. Simulation results demonstrate the superiority of JTSMLCEF. Compared with the current state-of-the-art method, it reduces the pilot overhead by $80\%$ while further reducing the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) by $82.6\%$ and $92.5\%$ in indoor and urban micro-cell (UMi) scenarios, respectively.

items.title: Secure Distortion-Aware GNN Precoding under Active Eavesdropping in Cell-Free Networks
items.summary: This paper considers a cell-free (CF) network under active eavesdropping. We show that nonlinear power amplifier (PA) distortion, together with the per-access point (AP) large-scale-gain fingerprint of the attack, can be exploited across cooperating APs to enhance physical layer security (PLS). Classical zero-forcing (ZF)-artificial noise (AN) precoders rely on a linear transmitter and an unbiased estimate, and thus cannot exploit either. We propose a distortion aware graph neural network (GNN) precoder that designs the signal beams at cooperating APs and exploits both the PA distortion and the per-AP fingerprint to enhance the secrecy rate, combined with a null-space AN block to form the GNN-AN scheme. The GNN is trained on channel estimates biased by an uplink pilot-spoofing attack to maximise the average per-user secrecy rate. Simulations across different numbers of APs show uniformly higher outage secrecy rates than ZF-AN under attack, reaching gains of 15% at the 1% outage level and 8.9% at the 5% outage level at L = 32 APs, input back-off (IBO) = -1 dB, and attacker-to-targeted user pilot power ratio of 0.5, under the same signal/AN power split.

items.title: A Novel OFDM-FMCW Waveform for Low-Complexity Joint Sensing and Communication
items.summary: With the advent of 6th Generation (6G) wireless networks, integrating Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) and Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) waveforms presents a promising solution for simultaneous communication and sensing. While OFDM offers high communication performance, it requires complex transceivers for sensing applications. Conversely, FMCW is easily implemented for sensing but provides low data rates for communication. This letter derives the mathematical relationship between OFDM and FMCW, showing how FMCW can be generated from the diagonal elements of the OFDM modulator (\ie, the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) matrix). We propose a novel approach that leverages the DFT matrix to seamlessly integrate these two waveforms, minimizing interference and enabling high data rate communication alongside low-complexity sensing receiver design. Extensive simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of our technique in achieving simultaneous sensing and

items.title: WULPUS PRO: Multi-mode Ultra-Low-Power Wearable Ultrasound and Array Imaging with CMUT Support
items.summary: Wearable ultrasound enables continuous monitoring of physiological processes such as muscle dynamics, bladder volume, and cardiovascular activity. Existing fully wearable ultra-low-power platforms are limited to shallow, low-channel A-mode sensing, while larger multi-mode systems are too bulky and power-hungry for true wearability. We present WULPUS PRO, a runtime-programmable wearable ultrasound acquisition platform measuring $39\times21\times6 \mathrm{mm}$ and weighing $5 \mathrm{g}$. It integrates $30 \mathrm{V}$ excitation, 16 time-multiplexed channels, a low-noise receive front-end with up to $70 \mathrm{dB}$ gain, $14 \mathrm{MHz}$ bandwidth, time-gain compensation, and $45 \mathrm{dB}$ SNR. The platform supports deep-tissue echo acquisition up to $2.2 \mathrm{MHz}$ in RF-sampling mode and $8 \mathrm{MHz}$ in envelope-detection mode. We demonstrate B-mode imaging in a 16-channel ultra-low-power wearable with sub-millimeter axial and millimeter-scale lateral resolution in phantom experiments, while consuming $40 \mathrm{mW}$ at $50 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF and under $60 \mathrm{mW}$ at $300 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF. WULPUS PRO supports both piezoelectric and capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducers, enabling integration with skin-conformal polymer-based CMUT arrays. As a host-agnostic acquisition front-end, it exposes standard data and power interfaces for BLE- and Wi-Fi-based wearable hosts. We demonstrate wireless transmission with external BLE and Wi-Fi modules and project 1-2 days of BLE operation at $50 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF and over 3 h of Wi-Fi streaming at $300 \mathrm{Hz}$ PRF using a $300 \mathrm{mAh}$, $6.4 \mathrm{g}$ Li-Po cell. WULPUS PRO establishes a new class of fully programmable, B-mode-enabled, ultra-low-power wearable ultrasound platforms.

items.title: Joint Beamforming Optimization and Dynamic Tracking in RIS-Enabled Secure ISAC Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled secure integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system, where the direct links between the base station (BS) and users are blocked, and the mobile eavesdropper is treated as the sensing target. The mobility of the eavesdropper induces time-varying wiretap channels, potentially compromising secure transmission when outdated eavesdropper information is used. To address this challenge, the BS dynamically tracks the eavesdropper over consecutive time slots and exploits the predicted state information to adapt its transmission strategy. A sum secrecy rate maximization problem is formulated by jointly optimizing the BS beamforming, artificial noise, and RIS reflection coefficients, subject to a constraint on the tracking error covariance to ensure the required sensing accuracy. To tackle the resulting nonconvex optimization problem with temporal coupling, an iterative algorithm integrating an extended Kalman filter (EKF) with an alternating optimization framework is developed. Specifically, the EKF recursively predicts and updates the eavesdropper's state, while the joint optimization problem is decomposed into four tractable subproblems that are solved iteratively. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves improved secrecy performance while effectively tracking the trajectory of the mobile eavesdropper, compared with benchmark schemes.

items.title: Revisiting Beamforming Design for Stable Millimeter-Wave Communications Under Blockages
items.summary: This paper investigates robust analog beamforming for millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications under stochastic path blockages using multi-panel arrays. Conventional designs concentrate beams on the line-of-sight (LoS) path to maximize array gain, but this approach is highly vulnerable to sudden disconnections when the LoS path is blocked. To overcome this limitation, we propose a multi-beam design that exploits both LoS and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) paths for stable communications. The major contribution of this work is to establish a theoretical foundation for multi-beam design, where closed-form expressions for the cumulative distribution function (CDF) and outage probability of the spectral efficiency (SE) are derived. To design the optimal multi-beam based on the derived outage probability, we formulate a panel allocation problem to determine the assignment of panels to specific paths. The optimization problem can be solved by two algorithms based on brute-force search. Through computer simulations, the validity of the theoretical analysis for multi-beam design is confirmed, and the proposed algorithms substantially reduce the outage probability while maintaining average SE performance, thereby achieving stable communication.

items.title: Generalized and Unified Power Flow Framework for Converter-Dominated AC/DC Power Grids
items.summary: Modern power grids increasingly rely on power electronic interfaces, requiring steady-state power flow analysis to accommodate diverse operating modes and network structures. Conventional approaches often rely on system-specific formulations and sequential approaches to handle such complexity. However, these approaches may limit applicability to diverse grid configurations and lead to convergence and computational issues. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a generalized and unified Newton-Raphson (NR) power flow framework for AC/DC hybrid grids. For generalized operational modeling, conventional and droop operating modes of generators and interlinking converters are represented through a common set of coefficients. For generalized structural modeling, models of AC transformers and DC/DC converters accommodate different transformer winding configurations and converter operating modes. For a unified solution, augmented variables are introduced to incorporate droop deadbands, output limits, and converter station losses into a single NR formulation, eliminating the need for sequential outer loops. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, its results are compared with those obtained from existing power flow methods and electromagnetic transient simulations across transmission networks, distribution networks, and microgrids. The implementation is made publicly available to facilitate its use in analyzing AC/DC hybrid grids.

items.title: Dynamic Skill-Based Routing for Call Centers with Transfers: A Value-Based Framework
items.summary: We consider a multi-class, multi-pool queueing model of a telephone call center in which a service completion does not always end the call. The caller may be transferred to another agent for a second service, so the assignment of an agent to a call affects not only the caller's waiting time but also whether the call is resolved and how much further work it creates. We model these transfers as Markovian routing from original to rework classes, and the system manager dynamically assigns agent pools to classes so as to maximize the value generated by service, net of transfer penalties and waiting and abandonment costs, over a finite horizon. Focusing on the Halfin-Whitt heavy-traffic regime, we derive an approximating Brownian control problem. Its Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a semilinear partial differential equation whose dimension equals the number of classes. Building on the deep splitting method of Beck et al. (2021), we develop a simulation-based computational method that approximates the value function and its gradient by neural networks, and we use it to construct an implementable routing policy for the original (prelimit) system. We calibrate the model to publicly available data from a large U.S. bank call center. In all test problems we consider, the proposed policy outperforms the best available benchmark policy we could find.

items.title: Normalizing Flow for Neural-Enhanced Track-Before-Detect
items.summary: Multiobject tracking (MOT) is a fundamental capability in autonomous navigation, radar and sonar systems, as well as 6G integrated sensing-and-communication (ISAC) networks. In this paper, we propose a neural-enhanced track-before-detect (TkBD) framework that operates directly on complex-valued raw signals and learns a latent representation of unmodeled propagation effects during runtime. We introduce an environment-dependent latent intensity variable that characterizes the signal power of each object in the shared propagation environment. The probability density function of this intensity variable is represented by a normalizing flow and trained online in an unsupervised manner within the sequential Bayesian inference procedure. The learning objective is derived from a variational Bayes formulation by maximizing the evidence lower bound (ELBO), thereby accounting for the uncertainties inherent in the Bayesian TkBD problem. To enable scalable inference, we make use of a recently introduced Bayesian TkBD framework that combines belief propagation, which avoids high-dimensional operations, with sequential Monte Carlo methods for efficient low-dimensional updates.

items.title: Dynamic Quantum-Assisted Co-Design of Controller and Lyapunov Candidate Parameters for Nonlinear Systems
items.summary: This paper proposes a dynamic quantum-assisted co-design framework for nonlinear closed-loop systems in which controller parameters and Lyapunov candidate parameters are redesigned jointly at successive decision epochs. Unlike conventional nonlinear control designs that typically tune controller gains offline and perform stability analysis separately, the proposed method embeds performance improvement and sample-based Lyapunov verification within a unified online optimization loop. The main novelty is a two-step computational structure that first contracts the continuous admissible search region around the current operating condition using a Black-Hole calibration procedure and then constructs a finite binary representation only over this calibrated region. The encoded objective is obtained from sampled nonlinear closed-loop evaluations and approximated by a local quadratic pseudo-Boolean surrogate, enabling an Ising-type Hamiltonian representation suitable for quantum-assisted optimization. Quantum imaginary time evolution is then used to explore the encoded Hamiltonian, and the resulting candidate bitstrings are decoded into continuous controller and Lyapunov parameters. To reduce dependence on the surrogate model, the decoded candidates are re-evaluated using the original nonlinear closed-loop cost and Lyapunov penalties before the final update is applied. The framework can accommodate sampled forms of different Lyapunov decay specifications by modifying the corresponding penalty and is numerically evaluated on first-order nonlinear consensus, second-order nonlinear consensus, and induction motor drive control examples. The implementation code used to generate the reported results is available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DQCLS-NS}{GitHub}.

items.title: Learning Waypoints and Passage Events for Decentralized Multi-Quadrotor Trajectory Planning
items.summary: Multi-quadrotor passage planning requires coordinated spatial routes and passage times under vehicle dynamics and actuation constraints. Optimizing these decisions jointly couples temporal allocation, nonlinear motion, and inter-vehicle interactions, creating a computational challenge for local trajectory generation. We propose a learning-optimization framework that predicts spatial waypoints and ordered passage events for independently solved quadrotor planners. A common physical time grid aligns the vehicles, with intermediate events fixed by the networks and terminal progress optimized locally to permit different completion metrics. Differentiable sequential convex programming incorporates rigid-body dynamics and rotor-thrust bounds, allowing collision and completion gradients to train both networks through the generated trajectories. In a two-quadrotor evaluation across 24 layouts, the adapted policy passes physical feasibility and sampled separation checks in all five held-out layouts. Their mean completion metric decreases by 1.52% relative to the inherited policy. The median forward time is 21.01 ms on the held-out exchange layout with matching numerical trajectory references. These results demonstrate that learned spatial and event parameters can coordinate independent rigid-body planners while preserving local vehicle constraints in the evaluated scenarios.

items.title: LLM Agents as Suppliers of Physical System Models: Calibration and Acceptance in Modelica
items.summary: To procure a model of a device, a client hands a supplier a description, sometimes with recorded data or a target response, and accepts the model against this handover. We let LLM coding agents act as the supplier on handovers with data, building Modelica models from library components for four simulated systems and a real switching magnet, and ask what acceptance certifies. Several agents reach the noise floor, but a handover admits a set of models: the description leaves parts of the structure open, and the data narrow it only to the agreed accuracy. We therefore accept by membership in this set, not by matching one reference, and add layers above behaviour: a physical invariant exposes an energy-creating model at the noise floor. Interpretability becomes a property of the delivered model, tested on a variant, read where none exists and shaped through the handover. Most failures are fits delivered with a systematic residual on their own fitting data, where the handover left open how close is close enough. In a follow-up, stating a threshold makes the agents compare against it, and more deliveries pass. The argument applies wherever a handover underspecifies a model meant to be read, not only run.

items.title: Finite-Time Capture by a Dubins Pursuer Against Unknown Evader Strategies
items.summary: We consider a planar pursuit-evasion problem in which a Dubins pursuer seeks to capture a slower first-order point-mass evader that can change its heading instantaneously. First, we propose a turn-rate feedback law with a single tunable gain and derive an explicit admissible gain interval that guarantees finite-time capture against any admissible evader strategy while satisfying the turn-rate constraint. Next, we obtain an explicit capture-time bound and characterize the turning authority required for the gain interval to be non-empty. Finally, we show that the dependence on the evader's speed bound can be removed by deriving a speed ceiling, computable solely from the pursuer's parameters, below which the guarantees hold at the maximum allowable gain. Numerical simulations illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

items.title: Cyclic Reformulation-Based Identification and Polytopic Uncertainty Modeling for Multirate Systems
items.summary: Modern control systems increasingly rely on heterogeneous sensors operating at different sampling rates, where intermittently missing outputs pose fundamental challenges for system identification. This paper proposes a non-iterative, control-oriented identification method for multirate systems based on cyclic reformulation. The method transforms multirate data into an expanded time-invariant representation and yields M parameter sets from a single input-output dataset, where M is the least common multiple of the sensor sampling periods. These parameter sets, expressed in a common state coordinate of the original dimension, are used in two complementary ways: their centroid, in which each output row is averaged over the phases at which that output is observed, serves as a noise-reduced nominal model, while their convex hull gives a polytopic uncertainty model whose vertices can be used directly in vertex-based LMI robust control design. Building on the exact cyclic-structure recovery established in the authors' preceding work, the paper contributes the centroid and polytopic models and evaluates them under finite noise through output-level validation statistics. Numerical simulations support both models: an illustrative SISO example shows that the centroid attains higher validation FIT than the best individual vertex and substantially outperforms an interpolation-based baseline, while a MIMO multirate sensing example confirms that the constructed polytope contains models whose validation FIT exceeds 95% on average even at the highest tested noise level. The resulting polytope is a data-derived uncertainty description obtained from a single experiment, so that the framework links multirate system identification with robust-control-oriented uncertainty modeling without iterative EM-type optimization.

items.title: LowNet: Looped Wavelet Neural Networks with 24 Learnable Parameters for Solving Poisson Equations
items.summary: Poisson equations frequently appear in various fields, such as mathematics, physics and informatics. Solving Poisson equation, however, is challenging. Traditional methods are not data-specific, although have high certainty. They require a large number of iterations due to the CFL numerical stability. In contrast, deep learning methods are data-driven and more efficient, but require accurate training data and suffer from heavy computation. To tackle these issues, we propose a wavelet-inspired Poisson solver with 24 trainable scalars. The proposed network has several advantages. First, it is compact. It has four independent $5\times5$ kernels, each represented by six parameters, leading to 24 scalars in total. Such compact format can be deployed on most devices. Second, thanks to the loop design, it achieves higher accuracy than previous methods. A residual loop reuses the wavelet block without increasing its parameters. Numerical experiments confirm that such loop indeed improves the solving accuracy. On 10000 images, one, two, and three loops of the wavelet block lead to PSNRs of $47.27$, $74.14$, and $100.74$ dB, respectively. Third, the proposed method is computationally fast. Thanks to the wavelet transform, the proposed method has linear computation complexity, leading to high computation performance. In short, we propose a novel looped wavelet neural network with compactness, accuracy and efficiency for solving Poisson equations. Our method can be applied in various fields, such as computational fluid dynamics, image reconstruction, biomedical engineering, electromagnetic field simulation.

items.title: Stable Inversion of Discrete-Time Linear Periodically Time-Varying Systems via Cyclic Reformulation
items.summary: Inverse systems for discrete-time linear periodically time-varying (LPTV) plants are fundamental to feedforward control and iterative learning control of multirate and periodic systems. Building on the classical cyclic reformulation, which converts an N-periodic system into an equivalent LTI system at the original sampling rate, this paper derives an explicit closed-form N-periodic state-space realization of the inverse for an arbitrary uniform periodic relative degree r >= 0 (defined through the periodic Markov parameters). The technical basis is a structure-preservation property: after absorbing a phase shift for r >= 1, the LTI inverse of the cycled plant provably retains the cyclic (block-circulant/block-diagonal) structure, so that the periodic inverse matrices can be read off block-by-block, in exact correspondence with the LTI inverse. The resulting inverse system is real-valued, causal for r = 0 and r-step-delayed for r >= 1, operates at the original sampling rate, and reconstructs the input exactly under matched initial conditions, with geometric error decay otherwise. Through this correspondence, its stability is shown to be equivalent to the invariant zeros of the cycled plant - the periodic invariant zeros of the plant - lying in the open unit disk, which generalizes the minimum phase condition of the LTI case and is verifiable on a single constant matrix pencil. Numerical examples illustrate the construction, the stability characterization, and the implementation as an online periodic filter.

items.title: DF-PALM: Dynamic Fusion Prompt Learning for Audio--Language Models
items.summary: Few-shot audio classification requires audio--language models to distinguish variable acoustic events from limited labeled data. PALM's main formulation adapts encoded class representations without changing pretrained encoders, but its class representations remain input-independent and classification uses audio features without class-conditioned refinement. We introduce DF-PALM, a dynamic feature-space prompting framework that combines audio-conditioned class representations with asymmetric cross-attention for audio refinement. Class representations are conditioned after text encoding, held fixed across fusion layers for each input, and reused for final scoring. Both pretrained encoders remain frozen, avoiding audio-conditioned text-encoder passes. With PENGI as the frozen backbone, the main 16-shot evaluation covered 11 benchmarks and six baselines. DF-PALM achieved 80.69% mean accuracy and 80.32% macro-averaged F1, exceeding PALM by 4.11 and 4.30 percentage points, respectively. Paired benchmark-level tests supported both gains after Holm correction. Across four shot settings, DF-PALM achieved the highest mean accuracy and macro-averaged F1 among the four evaluated prompt-learning methods. The gains extended to LAION-CLAP and OpenFLAM, with significant improvements over PALM in both metrics. At 50 candidate classes, operator-counted inference floating-point operations increased by 0.39% relative to PALM. These results support instance-conditioned feature-space adaptation as an effective approach to few-shot audio classification. Our code is publicly available at GitHub https://github.com/sunyulin0421/DF-PALM.

items.title: Coupling-Aware Pinching-Antenna Radiation for Heterogeneous NOMA Users
items.summary: Pinching-antennas systems (PASS) offer reconfigurable wireless channels via low-cost dielectric mediums by creating line-of-sight (LoS) communication links. Most of the existing PASS cover mechanisms of equal power pinching antennas for conventional bit-based communication, whereas flexible radiation control remains largely unexplored, particularly for heterogeneous semantic and bit users. In this paper, we investigate the performance of semantic communication (SC) using an adjustable radiation model over PASS, where the coupling strength between the dielectric waveguide and each pinching antenna is determined by the antenna-waveguide spacing. Specifically, the non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted heterogeneous users are served by multiple pinching antennas using spacing-controlled adjustable radiation ratios. Uunder this setting, we maximize the semantic spectral efficiency (SE) subject to the bit-user quality of service (QoS) requirement, successive interference cancellation (SIC) feasibility, and the minimum adjacent antennas spacing constraint. An alternating optimization (AO) approach optimizes users power allocation and positions of pinching antennas. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proportional power PASS model in providing higher semantic SE in different geometrical and numerical settings compared to conventional benchmark schemes.

items.title: ATLAS: Expert-Guided Sustainable Satellite Backhaul for Off-Grid Wildlife Monitoring
items.summary: Remote wildlife monitoring increasingly depends on high-fidelity cameras and sensors deployed far from grid power and terrestrial networks. Low Earth orbit satellite links can provide connectivity in these settings, but their high power draw and variable bandwidth, combined with intermittent on-site solar harvesting, make continuous backhaul infeasible. Current systems therefore filter at the edge, with motion triggers that waste limited energy and bandwidth on environmental artifacts, or fixed vision models that cannot follow evolving expert objectives. We present \textsc{ATLAS}, an expert-guided edge-to-cloud system that treats satellite backhaul as a scarce resource for off-grid wildlife monitoring. \textsc{ATLAS} uses foundation models to compile natural-language expert intent into semantic scoring logic, combines semantic relevance with environmental and energy state, and uses a constrained reinforcement-learning scheduler to decide which clips to upload and when. As a representative case study, we deployed \textsc{ATLAS} for over six months across 18 off-grid salmon-monitoring river sites. \textsc{ATLAS} achieves a mean clip-selection accuracy of $87.4\%$, exceeding mean baseline accuracy by $26.4$ percentage points, while maintaining near-continuous operation through low-solar periods in which baselines incur 16.0\% downtime.

items.title: Identifiability-Guided Composite Load Modeling of AI Data Centers
items.summary: The rapid growth of AI data centers introduces large, workload-dependent loads whose protection and reconnection behavior can affect power-system transient stability. Calibrating dynamic models of such loads is challenging because treating all associated elements as freely estimable may lead to weakly identified or physically confounded parameterizations. This paper proposes an identifiability-guided calibration framework for a composite load model with separate IT, cooling, and auxiliary branches. A nuisance-projected Fisher-information criterion characterizes the local identifiability of the cooling-motor composition, while a workload non-equivalence result shows that voltage-only recalibration cannot reproduce workload-dependent responses. Guided by these results, a grey-box estimator trained with branch-level supervision learns the workload-to-power relation and the cooling composition, while retaining a prescribed UPS protection law and an externally anchored reconnect-ramp duration. The learned workload relation is then distilled into a closed form for transient-stability simulation. Evaluation using 300,000 MIT Supercloud GPU power-utilization samples and 12,600 IEEE 39-bus fault scenarios yields an aggregate active-power $R^2$ of 0.948, compared with 0.856 for an LSTM baseline. Removing branch-level supervision preserves relatively high aggregate accuracy but substantially degrades cooling-component recovery. Under unseen deep voltage sags, the proposed model achieves a transient $R^2$ of 0.750, compared with 0.033 for the LSTM. Closed-loop simulations further show that cooling composition and protection behavior can affect retained-load states and voltage responses near protection thresholds.

items.title: RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
items.summary: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is severely under-constrained by limited X-ray projections. Learned reconstruction can provide complementary anatomical information, but using it as a prior in patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction introduces two challenges. First, the discrepancy between the learned prior and current reconstruction is spatially non-uniform: some local differences contain useful missing 3D information, whereas others reflect prior bias. Second, even a volumetrically beneficial correction can conflict with the observed X-ray measurements. Since X-ray measurements are line integrals, spatially separated corrections may affect overlapping rays, with their signed projection responses reinforcing or partially canceling in the measurement residual, so their feasibility cannot always be assessed independently. In this paper, we introduce RePrior, a multi-stage progressive prior-correction framework that addresses correction actionability, measurement feasibility, and representation expressivity. Selective Correction Proposal (SCP) first identifies actionable signed local corrections from prior--reconstruction discrepancies. Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation (MCR) then jointly enforces their consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements, while Hybrid Residual Enhancement (HRE) recovers additional correction capacity through complementary voxel- and Gaussian-domain degrees of freedom around the reconciled anchor. RePrior requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning. RePrior gains approximately 2.6~dB in 3D PSNR over R$^2$-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN. Beyond prior-assisted reconstruction, it delivers additional gains in volumetric quality and observed-view projection fidelity, with consistent gains in held-out-view fidelity in the backbone-matched evaluation.

items.title: Bellman Language Models: Solving the Recurring Decisions of LLM Agents
items.summary: A general observation in agentic workflows, especially bounded ones, is that the decision space of the LLM, when we separate a decision from generation, starts approaching saturation: the agent meets the same states again and again, and after enough conversations it stops meeting new ones. LLMs generally don't treat these decisions as an optimization problem and instead re-derive them from their context/prompt on every turn. We show that treating decision making within reasonable bounds as an optimization problem, solving it once, and reusing the solved decisions can often make an agent faster, cheaper and more reliable.
