Our approach, which we call Discretize, Then Decide, starts from data such as the workflow's own logs or, when none exists, runs of the LLM agent itself. It reads each conversation into discrete states and estimates the probability of each outcome and the cost of each move, until no new states appear and the probabilities stop changing. It then solves the resulting Markov decision process. The solution runs as a controller around the model, sending moves whose content is fixed in the state, such as a tool call or a templated reply, and any state it hasn't seen is sent back to the LLM. We call an LLM run this way a Bellman language model (BLM), after Richard Bellman's equation for the best move in each state. On $τ^2$-bench telecom, the controller with no model solves 79% of tasks. As a BLM, Qwen3.8-27B, an open model, goes from 29% to 96% with 93% fewer model calls. For Claude Opus 5.5, which solves 96% of tasks on its own, running it as a BLM cuts model calls and cost per task by about 98% and lets it solve 2 more tasks. On InventoryBench, the solved policy with no model beats every published method. Where the hard part is writing content rather than choosing moves, such as resolving SymPy issues, few decisions can be solved in advance, and a BLM helps little.

items.title: Dual Task Vector Merging: Leveraging Emotion and ASR Knowledge for Low-Resource Alzheimer's Disease Detection
items.summary: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) detection from speech benefits from both paralinguistic and linguistic cues, yet model training is frequently constrained by limited data. Fine-tuning a large pretrained speech encoder can easily overfit, while a frozen probe leaves the encoder's task-relevant knowledge underutilized. Therefore, we propose Dual Task Vector Merging, a parameter-efficient method that adapts a frozen wav2vec 2.0 backbone using task knowledge learned outside the AD task. Specifically, we inject two task vectors, derived as weight deltas from emotion- and ASR-fine-tuned wav2vec 2.0 models, into each transformer layer. During AD training, only layer-wise merging coefficients and a linear classification head are optimized, updating less than 0.1% of the parameters required for full fine-tuning. Speaker-independent experiments on ADReSS and ADReSSo show that dual merging improves over frozen probes, LoRA, and full fine-tuning, in the main binary settings, and gives the best results when combined with LoRA. Evaluation on PROCESS further shows that our advantages transfer to three-class HC/MCI/dementia classification when paired with LoRA. Experiments under reduced training data (20%, 40%, and 80%) confirm reliable gains in low-resource settings.

items.title: FairShare: Auditable Geographic Fairness for Multi-Operator LEO Spectrum Sharing
items.summary: Dynamic spectrum sharing (DSS) among multi-operator low Earth orbit (LEO) mega-constellations is essential for coexistence, yet prevailing policies focus almost exclusively on interference mitigation, leaving geographic equity largely unaddressed. This work investigates whether conventional DSS approaches inadvertently exacerbate the rural digital divide. Incorporating Keplerian orbital dynamics, inter-beam co-channel interference, and three real-world constellation geometries (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper), we conduct large-scale, 3GPP-compliant non-terrestrial network (NTN) simulations across 20 orbital snapshots spanning 10~minutes of satellite motion. The results uncover a stark and persistent structural bias: SNR-priority scheduling induces a $1.84\times$ mean urban--rural access disparity, with temporal fluctuations reaching $3.9\times$ during favorable interference conditions. Counter-intuitively, increasing system bandwidth amplifies rather than alleviates this gap. To remedy this, we propose FairShare, a lightweight, quota-based framework that enforces geographic fairness. FairShare not only reverses the bias, achieving an affirmative disparity ratio of $Δ_{\text{geo}} = 0.68\times$ with zero variance across all orbital snapshots and interference conditions, but also reduces scheduler runtime by 3.3\%. This demonstrates that algorithmic fairness can be achieved without trading off efficiency or complexity, and that it remains invariant to physical-layer dynamics. Our work provides regulators with both a diagnostic metric for auditing fairness and a practical, enforceable mechanism for equitable spectrum governance in next-generation satellite networks.

items.title: A Hierarchical Optimisation Framework for Integrated Electric-Hydrogen-Transport Systems
items.summary: Integrated electric-hydrogen infrastructures are becoming increasingly important with the growing deployment of electric vehicles (EVs) and hydrogen vehicles (HVs) in transport systems. However, the strong coupling between vehicle scheduling and multi-energy dispatch introduces significant operational challenges. This paper models an integrated electric-hydrogen-transport system (EHTS) and proposes a hierarchical optimisation framework that couples vehicle scheduling and downstream energy dispatch through a sequential, demand-driven two-layer structure. In the vehicle scheduling layer, a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) algorithm is developed to avoid repeated optimisation solving, enabling real-time EV charging and HV refuelling under non-preemptive service and within-interval sequential assignment. The resulting charging and refuelling demands are subsequently passed to the energy dispatch layer, where a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based approach is designed to optimise battery operation, hydrogen-tank operation, and PV generation allocation to minimise the overall operational cost of the EHTS while satisfying the scheduled transport demand. Representative case studies, together with comparative, ablation, and generalisation analyses, demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework. Furthermore, the learned dispatch policy maintains strong performance across diverse transport-demand scenarios and PV penetration levels without retraining, demonstrating robust generalisation capability for practical deployment.

items.title: AgentSoV: Virtual Sensing for LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Stream of Variation
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MASs) solve complex tasks through interacting agents, yet their reliability is difficult to analyze because failures depend on both individual agents and how information and errors propagate across the system. Existing approaches largely treat this as post-hoc failure attribution, but do not provide a common model across heterogeneous MAS architectures or support broader analysis of information influence and observability. We introduce AgentSoV, a virtual-sensing framework that models MAS execution as a stochastic dynamic system through Stream of Variation (SoV). AgentSoV maps heterogeneous trajectories into diagnostic stages, constructs virtual measurements from observable outputs, and learns cross-stage variation propagation with a state-space model. Its representation is architecture-aware in stage dependencies yet architecture-agnostic in analytical language, supporting chain-structured, orchestration-based, and directed acyclic graph (DAG)-structured MASs. Without re-executing the MAS, AgentSoV supports three system-level analyses: failure attribution identifies where abnormal variation enters; stage-input influence quantifies how strongly intermediate inputs affect downstream outcomes; and virtual-sensor placement selects complementary observations under a monitoring budget. Experiments across multiple MAS architectures demonstrate a unified approach to fault localization, information influence, and observability. AgentSoV reframes agentic execution as a dynamic system to model rather than merely text to inspect, providing insights for MAS structure and component design.

items.title: HEL: A Heterogeneous Extensible Layer for GPU-Resident Runtime Orchestration
items.summary: We describe a GPU-resident runtime system, HEL, built on stateful services that persist throughout the lifespan of a user application. A HEL programmer expresses a workload as an application that spawns coroutine-like tasks, which are then scheduled and run by the HEL runtime. HEL supports synchronous and asynchronous tasks, tasks with runtime dependencies, batched task submission, and automatic retries. Applications and tasks run alongside each other on the spatially partitioned GPU. Using producer-consumer and host-RPC benchmarks together with a PFPL compression case study, we show that HEL demonstrates a performance advantage for underutilized GPUs and for scenarios where HEL enables hiding task latency.

items.title: Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machines as Unsupervised Encoders for Biomechanical Movement Sequences
items.summary: Biomechanical movement recordings are continuous, high-dimensional time series, and analyzing them without manually labeling them requires representations that capture how movements evolve over time. Most unsupervised representation-learning pipelines, however, treat each observation frame independently and discard this temporal structure, while energy-based models that could capture it have not extensively been adapted to biomechanical signals. So, this paper implements the Recurrent Temporal Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RTRBM), a recurrent energy-based model, into an unsupervised encoder that maps windows of movement data to fixed-length embeddings, and tests what its recurrent structure contributes. We adapt the model to continuous-valued signals, stack it into a deep architecture, and integrate it into the SIT-FUSE segmentation pipeline. We evaluate the embeddings on simulated musculoskeletal reaching and on two real gait datasets, using clustering, reconstruction, and walking-speed classification of unseen subjects, and compare them against non-recurrent and non-probabilistic baselines, including a control that removes the recurrent connection. Clustering the embeddings recovers movement structure tied to progress toward the target without any labels, which also transfers to unseen episodes. On gait data, the embeddings outperform PCA and autoencoder baselines under a nonlinear probe. However, removing the recurrent connection does not yield a measurable loss on the reaching task, and simple per-channel summary statistics classify walking speed at least as well as the embeddings. The model is therefore a working, verified encoder for SIT-FUSE, while the evidence for a benefit of recurrence is mixed, and the learned embeddings did not outperform simple summary statistics on gait.

items.title: Authenticated Contradictions from Desynchronized Provenance and Watermarking
items.summary: Cryptographic provenance standards such as C2PA and invisible watermarking are positioned as complementary defenses for content authentication, yet the two verification layers are technically independent: neither conditions on the output of the other. This work formalizes and empirically demonstrates the $\textit{Integrity Clash}$, a condition in which a digital asset carries a cryptographically valid C2PA manifest asserting human authorship while its pixels simultaneously carry a watermark identifying it as AI-generated, with both signals passing their respective verification checks in isolation. We construct metadata washing workflows that produce these authenticated fakes through standard editing pipelines, requiring no cryptographic compromise, only the semantic omission of a single assertion field permitted by the current C2PA specification. To close this gap, we propose a cross-layer audit protocol that jointly evaluates provenance metadata and watermark detection status, achieving 100% classification accuracy across 3,500 test images spanning four conflict-matrix states and three realistic perturbation conditions. Our results demonstrate that the gap between these verification layers is unnecessary and technically straightforward to close.

items.title: Is User Calibration Still Necessary for Continuous Myoelectric Control? A Closed-Loop Comparison of Calibration-Free Controllers
items.summary: The need for user-specific calibration remains an often-cited barrier to widespread adoption of myoelectric control. Cross-user models trained on large multi-user datasets can now recognize gestures from unseen users without calibration, but they have been evaluated almost exclusively offline, leaving open whether calibration is still needed in closed-loop control. This study compared six calibration-free controllers, trained on 306 users of the EMG-EPN-612 dataset and used without any calibration data from the test participant, against three calibrated controllers in a closed-loop Fitts' law target-acquisition task with sixteen participants. The calibrated controllers achieved higher offline balanced accuracy (90.6% against 73.1% for the best controller of each paradigm), but completion rates did not differ significantly between paradigms, and the highest completion rate was achieved by a calibration-free controller. Calibrated controllers moved faster on successful acquisitions, partly because of their individually fitted speed mappings, though not significantly after correction for multiple comparisons. However, every calibration-free controller produced more direct and stable trajectories than every calibrated controller, even after adjusting for cursor speed. Offline accuracy did not predict completion rate across controllers or within participants, and across paradigms higher offline accuracy was associated with poorer trajectory quality in 15 of 16 participants. Without any calibration data from the end user, a model trained across a large population matched calibrated control in completion rate and exceeded it in trajectory quality. The offline accuracy gained through calibration should therefore not be taken as evidence of a closed-loop benefit.

items.title: Joint Probabilistic Shaping and Symbol-Level Precoding for Covert LEO Satellite Downlinks
items.summary: The wide footprint of low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite downlinks exposes the mere occurrence of a transmission to any receiver within it. This paper studies covert multiuser LEO downlinks, where a passive warden at an unknown but fixed ground location accumulates observations as the satellite moves. We jointly optimize the precoding and the occurrence probabilities of the multiuser symbol combinations to provide covertness against such wardens. Each phase-shift keying (PSK) symbol vector is decomposed into a relative pattern and a common rotation, so that shaping the pattern probabilities leaves the symbols of every legitimate user uniformly distributed. We develop probabilistically shaped symbol-level precoding and probabilistically shaped block-level precoding. We derive the exact chi-square divergence of the warden's Gaussian-mixture observation over the complete session and, by bounding the leakage over a continuous location uncertainty region, obtain certificates that guarantee covertness throughout that region. The certified covertness level is minimized under robust constructive-interference, power, and entropy constraints through an alternating optimization whose updates are equivalent to convex conic problems, and the optimized probabilities follow a Maxwell--Boltzmann-type law. Numerical results show that shaping substantially reduces the certified covertness level of both precoding structures, particularly under large location uncertainty, low elevation, and scarce power.

items.title: Degradation Aware V2G Dispatch for Co-Optimization of Parking Facility and Edge Data Center Located in the Airport Campus
items.summary: This paper studies an airport campus where long stay EV parking, airport buildings, and an AI data center share a single grid connection. The campus pays a commercial electricity tariff that charges for both the energy used and the highest power drawn during peak hours. Parked EVs can send power back to the campus through vehicle to grid (V2G) chargers and lower this peak. This paper proposes a two stage method. In the first stage, a linear program schedules EV charging and discharging to maximize the operator's profit and also sets a fixed daily payment to EV owners. In the second stage, a search chooses the share of energy savings paid to owners. The model guarantees that every owner is paid enough to take part, pays for battery wear so that EVs discharge only when it is worth the wear, and assigns charging ports on a first come, first served basis. In the case study, 400 V2G chargers are added to 1200 existing Level 2 chargers, serving 5000 expected sessions under summer and winter rates. In a summer week, V2G raises operator profit by $4978 compared with smart charging and lowers the high peak demand by 4400 kW (9%). The best contract gives owners 70% of the energy savings and earns 21% more than a fixed payment alone. Doubling the V2G ports to 800 lowers the peak further but reduces profit, because owner payments grow faster than the savings. V2G pays back within 10 years if a bidirectional charger costs less than about $1800 more than a standard one. Compared with a 5 MW/10 MWh stationary battery, V2G cuts more peak demand at $409 of investment per kW instead of $1522 and needs no extra land, while the battery does not pay back within its lifetime.

items.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling
items.summary: Unified audio-video creation requires a single model capable of text-conditioned joint synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing across both modalities. Existing methods rely heavily on paired corpora, which are scarce for joint generation and even rarer for editing. Consequently, they are spent learning single-branch generative and editing capabilities that abundant unimodal data could readily teach, rather than on the cross-modal coupling. Furthermore, prevailing systems apply a single shared noise schedule to both modalities, neglecting two critical limitations. First, due to the significant discrepancy in information density, video requires prolonged high noise to organize spatial and motion structure, whereas the sparser audio signal can settle earlier during the synthesis process, the dynamics a uniform schedule might compromise. Second, lockstep denoising leaves asymmetric workflows, such as conditioning on one modality to synthesize or edit another, untrained. We present UniAVC, which addresses both obstacles. It first trains each branch on unimodal dataset to full generative and editing competence, and subsequently dedicates paired data to exploit cross-modal correspondence. Modality-decoupled schedulers meanwhile warp the noise schedule independently from a shared timestep, while subtasks with one clean modality directly supervise asymmetric configurations. These settings respectively enable intent-aware editing, which preserves one modality intact while enlisting it to constrain the other, and post-inference self-refinement, which regenerates only an unsatisfactory branch against an accepted one. UniAVC thus spans multiple creation tasks from a single set of weights without task-specific adapters.

items.title: Evidence Field: Adaptive Covering Programs for Medical Imaging
items.summary: Medical image classifiers typically return predictions without a native contract for independently reconstructing their spatial decision computation. Evidence Field is a trainable spatial-program architecture that jointly produces class scores, selected covering programs and signed evidence. Its encoder combines absolute and image-relative response fields with associative spatial moments and learned characteristic sums. A typed classifier scores individual regions and parent-conditioned multiplicative groups; a covering recursion selects scale, partition and composition. We establish exact one-fold coverage, optimality within the registered grammar, a bound relating smooth training to hard inference, signed-score conservation and class-centred offset invariance. Direct contractions and their adjoint specify arithmetic and storage scaling on two- and three-dimensional grids. Native output records bind inputs, parameters, supports, types and contextual dependencies to individual and ensemble predictions. In a separately reported histopathology application, patient-separated training and evaluation across held-out centres provide empirical evidence for the architecture. Trained mechanism and corrected-loss comparisons distinguish predictive effects from implementation correctness; independent readers reconstruct descriptors, routes, scores and probability mixtures. The principal contribution is a coupled representation, decision and evidence architecture whose selected computation can be reproduced independently.

items.title: Sample complexity of weak-signal latent-variable models
items.summary: We study parametric estimation in latent-variable models in the weak-signal regime, where a small signal-strength parameter $β$ controls the dependence of the observations on the unknown parameter. At $β=0$, this dependence disappears, so all parameter values induce the same observed distribution, which we call the null law. We develop a unified framework for analyzing sample complexity in the weak-signal regime by expanding the likelihood ratio around this shared null law in powers of $β$. We prove that if the unknown parameter is first globally identifiable at order $r$ in this expansion, then estimation to fixed accuracy requires at least on the order of $β^{-2r}$ samples. We further identify a likelihood-separation stability condition that is necessary for any estimator to attain this rate and, under mild regularity conditions, sufficient for both maximum likelihood and method-of-moments estimators to attain it. We also study the regime in which the target accuracy vanishes together with the signal strength, and show that global localization and local refinement may be governed by different likelihood orders, leading to distinct statistical scales. Finally, we apply our framework to broad classes of algebraically structured latent-variable models, including additive-noise channels and exponential-family models.

items.title: Provable Bounds on the Hessian of Neural Networks: Derivative-Preserving Reachability Analysis
items.summary: We propose a novel reachability analysis method tailored for neural networks with smooth activations. Our method relies on constructing an end-to-end first-order Taylor expansion of the network and bounding the remainder. To enable this, we develop a scalable algorithm for computing closed-form bounds on both the gradient norm and Hessian norm of the network. A key component is a loop transformation of the activation functions, which leverages their monotonicity to sharpen the bounds. This yields a local abstraction that preserves the network's value and gradient at the expansion point. For larger input domains, we integrate this local model into a branch-and-bound scheme, recursively refining the overapproximation. We validate our approach through extensive experiments and demonstrate scalability and accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art verification baselines.

items.title: Finite-Calendar Admission and Deadline-Aware Pruning for UWB Audio
items.summary: Isochronous ultra-wideband (UWB) audio transport must deliver a complete service data unit (SDU) before its presentation deadline; fragment reception rate and aggregate throughput do not directly characterize this objective. We formulate admission and online service over a periodic calendar of finite exchange opportunities, explicitly accounting for fragmented SDUs, bounded attempts, calendar alignment, and timing uncertainty. For equal-duration, freely assignable opportunities, an interval-demand condition characterizes finite-job reservation feasibility, and an earliest-deadline-first construction realizes a feasible reservation. A separate necessary capacity bound identifies loads that cannot sustain complete-SDU delivery even with no transmission errors. For online overload control, we study a deadline-aware policy that discards an SDU when its outstanding fragments exceed the remaining eligible opportunities. Across 3,456 replicated scheduling runs and 432 supplemental sensitivity runs, pruning raises eight-stream burst-loss timely completion from 45.441\% to 59.399\%, a paired difference of $13.958\pm2.080$ percentage points (pointwise 95\% interval). At four streams, round robin instead attains slightly higher completion, while heavy overload causes pronounced per-stream imbalance. A finite design enumeration and an evaluated multi-stream fragmentation envelope quantify the interaction among scheduling, payload overhead, and capacity. These findings distinguish provable admission conditions from online deadline salvage and expose the aggregate-throughput versus per-stream-service tradeoff in UWB audio scheduling.

items.title: Three Machines Suffice for Local Hardening of Electromechanical Oscillations
items.summary: The single-degree-of-freedom swing equation with sinusoidal coupling is locally softening: its oscillation frequency decreases with oscillation level near a stable equilibrium. Nonlinear modal interaction, however, can reverse this trend in multimachine systems. This letter gives a necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict leading-order local hardening, measured with respect to canonical action, in two symmetric three-machine operating-point families with equal or opposite power injections at the equal-inertia machines. An exact two-coordinate reduction expresses the condition in terms of a squared modal-frequency ratio and a dimensionless nonlinear coupling measure. The proof retains the induced mean shift and second harmonic and shows that the companion modal family remains locally softening. The criterion recovers both an equal-inertia hardening example and an exact large-inertia threshold. Coherent aggregation recovers the two-machine softening law, whereas the infinite-bus limit retains two dynamic rotor angles and permits hardening. An exact coherent-group extension preserves the selected periodic family, frequency, and canonical action for every finite machine count greater than two. Thus, three finite-inertia machines are the minimum permitting local hardening in the stated undamped, lossless classical model.

items.title: Enhancing Speech Large Language Models through Reinforced Behavior Alignment
items.summary: Speech large language models (SpeechLMs) can process spoken requests, yet still lag behind text-prompted large language models (LLMs) on instruction following and reasoning. We argue that this gap is not only an ASR or representation problem: the same semantic instruction can induce different response policies when spoken with different speakers, accents, noise conditions, prosody, or disfluencies. We propose Verifiable Invariant Reinforced Behavior Alignment (VIRBA), a reinforcement-learning framework for aligning SpeechLM behavior across acoustic realizations of the same semantic intent. VIRBA builds multi-view spoken instruction groups, scores sampled responses with semantic preference, rule-verifiable correctness, cross-acoustic invariance, and adaptive reasoning rewards, and optimizes the model with Cross-Acoustic Group Relative Policy Optimization (CA-GRPO). The resulting objective moves SpeechLM alignment beyond teacher imitation toward robust reasoning policies that remain stable across realistic spoken realizations. Experiments with recent SpeechLM baselines, disfluency robustness, spoken QA, audio reasoning, and speech-to-text translation show the largest gains on reasoning-heavy and acoustically perturbed spoken prompts.

items.title: RF-GPT: Teaching AI to See the Wireless World
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) and multimodal models have become powerful general-purpose reasoning systems. However, radio-frequency (RF) signals, which underpin wireless systems, are still not natively supported by these models. Existing LLM-based approaches for telecom focus mainly on text and structured data, while conventional RF deep-learning models are built separately for specific signal-processing tasks, highlighting a clear gap between RF perception and high-level reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce RF-GPT, a radio-frequency language model (RFLM) that utilizes the visual encoders of multimodal LLMs to process and understand RF spectrograms. In this framework, complex in-phase/quadrature (IQ) waveforms are mapped to time-frequency spectrograms and then passed to pretrained visual encoders. The resulting representations are injected as RF tokens into a decoder-only LLM, which generates RF-grounded answers, explanations, and structured outputs. To train RF-GPT, we perform supervised instruction fine-tuning of a pretrained multimodal LLM using a fully synthetic RF corpus. Standards-compliant waveform generators produce wideband scenes for six wireless technologies, from which we derive time-frequency spectrograms, exact configuration metadata, and dense captions. A text-only LLM then converts these captions into RF-grounded instruction-answer pairs, yielding roughly 120,000 RF scenes and 0.625 million instruction examples without any manual labeling. Across benchmarks for wideband modulation classification, overlap analysis, wireless-technology recognition, WLAN user counting, and 5G NR information extraction, RF-GPT achieves strong multi-task performance, whereas general-purpose VLMs with no RF grounding largely fail.

items.title: A Mathematical Framework for EEG Functional Connectivity: Taxonomy, Measure Relationships, Identifiability, and Analytical Bounds
items.summary: Electroencephalographic (EEG) functional connectivity is quantified using diverse measures of statistical dependence, spectral coupling, phase synchronization, information transfer, directed interactions, cross-frequency coupling, and network topology. An important question is what can be inferred about one connectivity measure from another. This paper develops a mathematical framework that treats connectivity measures as mappings from an explicitly defined admissible state space to observable values. For a source measure and a target measure, the set of target values compatible with an observed source value is defined as a cross-connectivity attainable set. This formulation distinguishes exact determination, conditional determination using additional information, bounded inference, approximate identification, and non-identifiability. The framework is extended to multichannel connectivity matrices, graph measures, and dynamic connectivity. It also incorporates the influence of filtering, referencing, volume conduction, source leakage, inverse modeling, epoch duration, and estimator assumptions on admissible inferences. Analytical examples examine relationships between covariance and correlation, mutual information and correlation under joint Gaussianity, coherence and phase-locking value under restrictive signal conditions, and the general non-identifiability of the phase-lag index and weighted phase-lag index without additional assumptions. By making assumptions and attainable values explicit, the framework provides a systematic basis for determining what connectivity results can and cannot establish about other measures.

items.title: An integrated interpretable control effectiveness learning and nonlinear control allocation methodology for overactuated aircraft
items.summary: Nonlinear dynamics and the strong couplings that arise between multiple effectors undermine the assumptions behind conventional, linear control allocation techniques. When flight enters regimes where nonlinear effects dominate, linear allocators exhibit reduced accuracy due to increased model mismatch, which subsequently degrades performance and robustness of the flight control system. High fidelity onboard models and black box data driven approaches can recover accuracy across the flight envelope, but respectively impose computational burdens prohibitive for real time allocation and sacrifice the interpretability required for verification and fault diagnosis. This paper addresses these limitations by learning an explicit, physics constrained analytical model of the control effectiveness mapping from representative flight data using Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics. The resulting mapping is compact, interpretable, and admits analytical derivatives, enabling efficient computation within nonlinear solvers that additionally incorporate actuator dynamics, without requiring an onboard model. An online adaptation mechanism monitors prediction residuals and refreshes the model when significant plant changes are detected, providing graceful reconfiguration under actuator failures and varying operating conditions. The methodology is evaluated on a high fidelity nonlinear benchmark aircraft across a range of aggressive maneuvers, achieving accuracy comparable to a full nonlinear onboard model while substantially reducing computational cost relative to established baselines.

items.title: Comparison of Current-Limiting Strategies for Grid-Forming Converters Under Grid Faults
items.summary: This paper investigates the performance of three state-of-the-art current-limiting strategies for grid-forming (GFM) converters under grid faults. These highly effective strategies include virtual admittance control, virtual admittance control enhanced with virtual power feedback, and the recently developed cross-forming control. The performance comparison addresses two crucial requirements for GFM converters under grid faults, namely transient stability and reactive current injection. The comparison indicates that the virtual admittance control enhanced with virtual power feedback shows the most promising transient stability performance, while the cross-forming control exhibits superior reactive current injection performance. Thus, individual benefits of each strategy can be obtained by properly combining them.

items.title: SpikeAid: A Streaming Spiking Hearing Aid Framework for Joint Noise Reduction and Wide Dynamic Range Compression
items.summary: Modern hearing aids combine noise reduction (NR) with wide dynamic range compression (WDRC) to suppress background interference while compensating for the reduced auditory dynamic range associated with hearing loss. Conventional systems typically process NR and WDRC as separate stages, although the output of NR directly affects the signal levels and envelopes that determine subsequent compression. Recent end-to-end neural approaches can jointly optimize these processes, but their dense computation remains challenging for always-on hearing aids. In this work, we propose SpikeAid, a causal end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) framework for joint NR and WDRC. SpikeAid consists of an NR-Net that constructs complementary speech and noise representations and a WDRC-Net that estimates the corresponding branch gains, with both components jointly optimized according to the final hearing aid objective. To capture the multiscale temporal structures required by joint NR and WDRC in a computationally efficient manner, we further introduce the Delayed Resonate-and-fire Neuron (DRN), which incorporates bio-inspired heterogeneous dendritic delays and resonating dynamics. Experimental results on the hearing aid task show that SpikeAid improves key objective metrics over cascaded processing and outperforms existing spiking speech-processing baselines. Evaluation on the public Intel Neuromorphic Deep Noise Suppression (N-DNS) Challenge further demonstrates state-of-the-art neuromorphic speech-denoising performance with DRN. Finally, we designed an FPGA-based neuromorphic hardware system for efficient deployment of SpikeAid, where it achieves over two orders of magnitude higher energy efficiency than conventional CPU/GPU implementations, demonstrating its potential for energy-efficient hearing aid applications.

items.title: MIRA: A Modular Open-Source Micro-UAV for Indoor Research
items.summary: Indoor robotics research increasingly relies on micro-UAV platforms whose airframes, electronics, and control software are open to modification. Off-the-shelf platforms often lack the low-level access that such modifications require, while building a custom vehicle demands substantial engineering effort before the first flight test, leaving many laboratories working within constraints that limit the scope of their research. We present MIRA (Modular Indoor Research Architecture), an open-source micro-UAV for indoor research, built around a replicable 3D-printed PLA airframe with detachable arms and a containerized low-level software package that manages the companion-to-autopilot communication bridge via Micro XRCE-DDS. Designed as a white-box architecture, its core subsystems, including the companion computer, are individually replaceable without firmware refactoring, which supports local fabrication, crash-localized repair, and component substitution from existing laboratory inventory. We characterize MIRA through autonomous flights comprising takeoff, hovering, trajectory tracking, and landing within an optical motion-capture volume. The communication pipeline sustains a median companion-to-autopilot latency of 0.02 ms, with the external motion-capture link as the main remaining latency source, and time-domain analysis shows that structural vibration remains stable during dynamic maneuvers and below the reference level adopted in this work. All design files and software are released openly to support replication and extension by other laboratories.

items.title: Multi-Agentic AI for Intent-Driven and Conflict-Aware rApp Policy Orchestration in Open RAN
items.summary: Open radio access network (O-RAN) enables a multi-vendor ecosystem that accelerates xApp development for near-real-time (RT) network management. However, this openness shifts a combinatorial coordination burden to the Non-RT layer, where rApp policies compose xApps from a growing catalog to realize operator intents. Coexisting intents further compound this challenge, as conflicts may arise among xApp actions, rApp policies, and their cross-layer interactions. To maximize intent admission while maintaining key performance indicator (KPI) compliance across incoming and incumbent intents, we propose a large language model-based Multi-Agentic AI framework. A Reasoning Agent screens candidate xApps against KPI contracts and produces a joint intent admission and xApp assignment decision. On post-deployment KPI violations, a Diagnosis Agent identifies the root causes of failure, labels the conflict mechanism, and guides the Reasoning Agent in subsequent attempts. Experimental results show that the framework based on GPT-OSS 120B achieves 28.6% more KPI-compliant cases and admits over 15* as many incoming intents as state-of-the-art baselines. Under the Qwen 72B variant, Diagnosis increases compliant cases by 50.0%, quadruples admitted intents, and reduces deployment attempts by 32.6%. A live deployment conforming to O-RAN specifications further validates the feasibility of the proposed solution for conflict-aware rApp policy orchestration in real networks.

items.title: Virtual Speech Therapist: A Clinician-in-the-Loop AI Agent for Speech Therapy Planning
items.summary: This paper presents a proof of concept of the Virtual Speech Therapist (VST), an intelligent multi-agent based system designed to support stuttering assessment and individualized therapy planning through artificial intelligence (AI) driven workflows. VST integrates deep learning (DL) based stuttering detection fSD with large language model (LLM) based agentic system to assist clinicians in developing evidence informed therapy plans. The VST system begins with the acquisition and feature extraction of given speech samples, followed by the detection of stuttering types. Building on these speech driven information S, VST initiates an agentic reasoning process in which specialized LLM agents autonomously generate, critique, and iteratively refine individualized therapy plans P. A dedicated CriticAgent πca acts as a structured self-refinement mechanism, reviewing the generated therapy plans P and identifying areas for potential improvement in consistency, methodological soundness, and alignment with available evidence and professional guidelines. The resulting therapy plan P is presented then as a draft for clinician review. Clinician feedback can then be incorporated to produce a revised plan P, thereby maintaining a clinician-in-the-loop (CITL) paradigm. An initial evaluation, involving expert speech language pathologist (SLP) examines the clinical interpretability and feasibility of the generated therapy plans. Taken together, the results show the potential of VST to augment clinician-led therapy planning and provide a promising basis for future studies evaluating its integration into real world clinical settings. An interactive user interface for the proposed prototype is available online at: https://vocametrix.com/ai/stuttering-therapy-planning-agent, facilitating interactive stuttering assessment and stuttering therapy planning.

items.title: From Inference to Control: Structure-Guided Control of Hypergraph Dynamics
items.summary: Controllability determines whether a system's state can be guided toward any desired configuration, making it a fundamental prerequisite for designing effective control strategies. In the context of networked systems, controllability is a well-established concept. However, many real-world systems, from biological collectives to engineered infrastructures, exhibit higher-order interactions that cannot be captured by simple graphs. Moreover, the interaction structures might be unknown and difficult to measure directly. Here, we close this gap by combining hypergraph inference with the identification of controllable nodes. Building on the inferred structure, we design a controller that, given a set of controllable nodes, steers the system toward a desired configuration. We formulate analytical controllability guarantees for polynomial systems. For non-polynomial dynamics on hypergraphs, we propose a heuristic method for identifying controllable nodes and validate the proposed approach using Kuramoto oscillators.

items.title: Target Sensing in Full-Dimensional MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems Via Coupled Tensor Decomposition
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has been recognized as a key enabler for future wireless communication systems. However, existing ISAC designs based on MIMO-OFDM generally fail to fully exploit the spatial degrees of freedom and the communication data payload, resulting in restricted target sensing performance. To cope with this issue, in this paper we propose a novel target sensing method for full-dimensional (FD) MIMO-OFDM ISAC systems based on coupled tensor decomposition. We first characterize the system model of FD MIMO-OFDM ISAC, where the base station employs a large number of antennas in two dimensions and facilitates both sensing and communication via the data payload of OFDM signals. Then, we formulate the problem of estimating target parameters as a coupled canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) problem, which jointly leverages the echo signals of communication data payload over multiple subcarriers in the frequency domain. The theoretical analysis indicates that the formulated coupled CPD problem possesses a more relaxed uniqueness condition compared with the ordinary CPD problem, thereby enabling more stable target sensing performance through the pure communication data payload in FD MIMO-OFDM ISAC. In addition, we develop a coupled CPD-based target sensing algorithm, where the target parameters, including azimuth and elevation angles, ranges, and velocities, are extracted from the decomposed factor matrices. Numerical results show that the proposed target sensing method achieves a higher success rate and more accurate parameter estimation than existing tensor decomposition methods.

items.title: Distributed Real-Time Cooperative Model Predictive Control
items.summary: This paper presents a novel distributed real-time iterative method for cooperative linear Model Predictive Control (MPC) with polyhedral state and input constraints, implementing a relaxed, recentered logarithmic barrier function. The method transforms centralized MPC problems into a distributed framework using temporal-spatial splitting, facilitating efficient online implementation. To achieve real-time performance, we introduce a distributed convex nonlinear optimization solver with guaranteed global linear convergence. By executing this solver with a fixed number of iterations per sampling time, the resulting near-optimal MPC controller ensures closed-loop stability while maintaining fixed computational complexity. The proposed approach is validated through an illustrative example involving a spring-vehicle-damper system benchmark, demonstrating both its effectiveness and computational efficiency.

items.title: Widely Linear-Enhanced IQ Imbalance Interference Cancellation for AFDM-FTN Systems
items.summary: Internet of Things (IoT) networks require reliable and spectrally efficient wireless links to support massive device connectivity and high mobility applications. To meet these requirements, this paper investigates a widely linear (WL)-empowered receiver design for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) with faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling under practical receiver in phase and quadrature imbalance (IQI). The considered AFDM-FTN system couples the direct and image branches with FTN induced intersymbol interference (FTN-ISI) and delay-Doppler spreading in the affine domain. To address this coupled interference structure, a unified conjugate augmented input output model is established for IQI impaired AFDM-FTN systems. Based on this model, a WL minimum mean square error receiver with parallel interference cancellation (WL-MMSE-PIC) is developed, where WL-MMSE preprocessing is followed by the proposed hard decision PIC (HD-PIC) and damped soft decision PIC (SD-PIC). The proposed receiver is further analyzed in terms of the local stability of HD-PIC, a genie aided performance reference under ideal residual interference cancellation, and the impact of the AFDM chirp parameter on the post equalization interference distribution. Simulation results show that the proposed WL-MMSE-HD-PIC and WL-MMSE-SD-PIC receivers achieve significant error rate performance gains over the conventional linear-MMSE and WL-MMSE baselines. The results further show that FTN signaling provides a nominal spectral-efficiency gain, while residual-coupling-based chirp-parameter selection reduces the post-equalization residual coupling and improves detection reliability for high-mobility IoT links.

items.title: Fluxion: A Differentiable DSP Runtime from Training GPU to Real-Time Edge
items.summary: Native real-time audio engines meet audio deadlines but are hard to connect to machine-learning workflows, while tensor frameworks integrate with machine learning but process audio as offline batches without timing guarantees; runtime layers built on them inherit the host's scheduling and deployment footprint. This paper presents Fluxion, a Rust audio DSP runtime for cascaded second-order sections, FIR filters, and delay-line effects. Fluxion implements the parts that are specific to DSP: closed-form filter design, forward kernels, analytic adjoints for the recursion, and stability checks. It relies on existing libraries for the autodiff graph, GPU code generation (tested here on CUDA), and array interchange. One graph algebra is lowered to a differentiable training engine and to an allocation-free real-time engine; between them, a trained graph is checked for stability and frozen into a versioned artifact that an edge device checks again before playback. We compare Fluxion with six framework-hosted and native baselines under one float32 protocol. Among the systems that compute the exact recursion, Fluxion has the highest GPU throughput when data stays on the device and the highest throughput on most CPU workloads, while its CPU training step is slower than those of torchaudio and GRAFX. Its test suite checks the audio thread for allocations with an instrumented allocator, and we report measured latency tails. Fluxion is open source at \url{https://github.com/matteospanio/fluxion}.

items.title: Mode-Weighted Transport Certificates for State-Dependent Reflected Switching Diffusions
items.summary: State-dependent switching diffusions can contract in law even when individual modes are expansive. We establish a computable, constant-one contraction certificate on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and compact convex domains with normal reflection. The mode-weighted transport cost combines spatial separation with a discrete graph penalty and retains spatial dependence when the modes differ. A synchronous Brownian coupling and a maximal coupling of jump clocks in equal modes lead to separate equal- and unequal-mode generator inequalities. We give a complete regularization argument for the nonsmooth cost, including the drift and jump errors, the sign of reflection, and the limiting Itô-Dynkin calculation. A resolvent proof transfers contraction to probability-valued weak solutions of the no-flux Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov system, while an explicit Foster-Lyapunov condition ensures existence and uniqueness of an invariant law on the whole space. For fixed weight ordering and decay rate, certificate synthesis is a semi-infinite linear feasibility problem; on compact domains, a Lipschitz-buffered finite mesh provides a rigorous test. One-dimensional and planar examples illustrate the certificate and its numerical verification.

items.title: Beyond Geometric Closure: Measuring and Diagnosing Mechanical Consistency in Visual Dynamics
items.summary: Visual accuracy leaves open whether predicted motion obeys dynamics. We introduce a framework for measuring and diagnosing mechanical consistency in visual dynamics. An independent SI audit of rigid closed chains separates geometric admissibility, reaction-free actuator effort, and work--energy balance. Continuous scoring measures progress against fixed engineering targets, while reference replay quantifies measurement error. With three seeds per setting, we evaluate KeyCLD and CON across 343 planar assemblies at 64/256 pixels and V-JEPA + AC and LingBot-VA on 100 shared spatial test assemblies. CON reduces image MSE by 37.6%/37.2% relative to persistence, yet neither planar model attains valid native geometry. At 256 pixels, calibrated RGB replay places forecast errors far above measurement error. With exact states, KeyCLD preserves geometry and RK4 training raises its score from 52.65 to 64.30. In both spatial pathways, CAD/IK reconstruction restores geometry while mean actuator residuals exceed five times the engineering targets. The interventions distinguish gains in visual prediction and geometric admissibility from remaining force and energy errors.

items.title: Severity-Channel Conditioning: An Injection-Level Study for Consumer-Device Deblurring
items.summary: Motion-deblurring models lose substantial accuracy when transferred from professional cameras to smartphone-derived imagery. This paper studies whether a severity descriptor, partly derived from the paired sharp target, helps adaptation on the iPhoneBlur consumer-device benchmark. Under a shared update budget, input concatenation of a severity map is compared with global feature modulation by capture metadata, spatial feature modulation by the severity map, and a tier-contrastive output objective, together with an unconditioned spectral-loss control, all fine-tuned from the same domain-adapted latent-diffusion baseline. The primary experiment is an oracle diagnostic: target-derived information is supplied at inference. For the evaluated model pair, input concatenation improves overall peak signal-to-noise ratio from 31.23 to 31.30 dB, whereas feature modulation, the contrastive objective, and the spectral-loss control do not exceed the baseline. The gain is positive on 87.2% of test images and on 14 of 15 held-out source videos; this video-level analysis describes the evaluated checkpoint pair and does not establish robustness to retraining, and three training seeds are reported separately. The input-level gain recurs on a transformer backbone. In one exploratory run, zeroing the channel at inference retains most of the gain in peak signal-to-noise ratio but lowers structural similarity below the baseline. A normalized-step diagnostic does not support the expected larger-gradient explanation. The results characterize the evaluated configurations and do not establish injection location as the sole cause, a spatial-locality mechanism, or a reliable deployment advantage.

items.title: Physics-Informed Koopman Learning for Data-Efficient System Identification of Automated Vehicle Dynamics
items.summary: Understanding how a particular automated vehicle reacts to nearby traffic can improve motion prediction, control development, traffic simulation, and safety evaluation. However, commercial automated driving systems are proprietary, and single encounters may provide only a few seconds of noisy data. Standard physical models are interpretable but inflexible, whereas neural models are often data-hungry. We propose a physics-informed Koopman framework that combines a calibrated car-following law with a correction learned from the observations. A weak-form estimator learns this correction from velocity measurements integrated over time, avoiding noise-sensitive numerical differentiation. The resulting continuous-time model predicts the follower's response and provides interpretable measures of driving behavior. Experiments on OpenACC and CATS-CF evaluate 5-, 7-, and 11-second histories. Averaged over these histories, the constant-time-headway branch reduces speed prediction error by 16.0% and 15.4% on OpenACC and CATS-CF, respectively, relative to the best neural baselines. The PI-Koopman branches achieve the lowest mean speed and gap errors among the physical and neural comparators. Weak-form estimation reduces acceleration-field reconstruction error by 74.5% in noisy known-law simulations and noise-induced field perturbation by 91.6% in paired real-vehicle measurements. The same PI-Koopman system identification supports following-mode recognition with an approximately eleven-fold difference in median residual variance between human drivers and automated vehicles, and a single residual threshold achieves 85.4% balanced accuracy. The branch informed by the intelligent driver model takes a median 17 to 26 ms for identification and forecasting on the tested central processing units, supporting frequent target adaptation.

items.title: Exploiting Beam Squint for Near-Field Wideband Beamforming in Multi-User OFDMA Systems
items.summary: The beam squint effect has traditionally been viewed as detrimental to near-field wideband beamforming due to the reduction of beamforming gain towards the desired direction. In this paper, we show that it can instead be harnessed as a benefit in a hardware-constrained orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) system, where the system, equipped with a single radio-frequency (RF) chain, aims to serve multiple spatially distributed users by allocating different subcarriers to different users. By exploiting the beam squint effect, flexible frequency-dependent beamfocusing patterns are realized via parallel true-time-delay (TTD) units, enabling nearly full beamforming gain across users. In particular, we formulate a max-min rate optimization problem that jointly designs the time delays, subcarrier-user association, analog beamforming, and power allocation. To tackle the resulting nonconvex mixed-integer problem, a two-stage optimization framework is proposed. In Stage~I, subcarrier-user association and structured analog beamforming are jointly optimized. In Stage~II, power allocation is obtained via bisection search and inverse water-filling. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve a significant improvement by utilizing beam squint to serve multiple spatially distributed users in OFDMA systems.

items.title: Passive Smartphone-Microphone Phonocardiography for Joint Maternal-Fetal Cardiac Well-Being Monitoring: A Longitudinal Self-Recorded Case Study in Late Pregnancy
items.summary: Maternal and perinatal deaths are concentrated in low- and middle-income countries, where routine fetal monitoring is largely inaccessible. With the prevalence of smartphone as personal assistive gadget, we ask whether a phone's built-in microphone, with no extra hardware or emitted signal, can serve as a software-only maternal-fetal cardiac screening aid when moved from the chest to the lower abdomen? We report a longitudinal, self-recorded case study of a single subject (Z) over the last five weeks of a singleton pregnancy, later delivered at term without complications: 28 short, uncontrolled recordings (rest, morning, post-exercise). Lacking maternal/fetal ground truth, we exploit the prior that maternal and fetal heart rates occupy largely disjoint frequency bands, blindly decomposing a Shannon-energy envelope into two candidate-rate bands, and additionally probe a slower breathing-rate band as a rest/exercise discriminator. A fast, regular, fetal-plausible rhythm was recovered from most recordings and remained essentially unchanged across maternal activity states, consistent with normal fetal cardiac autonomy; a slower, noisier maternal-plausible rhythm was recovered less reliably. Beat-to-beat variability proved largely noise-dominated at our short window lengths, and the breathing-rate probe did not significantly separate rest from exercise; both are reported as negative findings. We position the work within AI for global health: a low-cost screening aid for remote and underserved communities, pending reference-validated follow-up, not a replacement for clinical monitoring.

items.title: ASR Personalization in Pathological Voice: Accuracy, Efficiency, and Duration Effects
items.summary: Automatic Speech recognition (ASR) struggles with Pathological speech due to persistent speaker-specific mismatch. In clinical and accessibility scenarios, only limited target-speaker data is typically available, making full model retraining impractical. We present a component-level analysis of LoRA adaptation in Whisper, investigating how adapter placement interacts with the model size, training efficiency and utterance-duration in single-speaker settings. Our experimental comparative study shows that while scaling reduces errors, it does not eliminate mismatch. Furthermore, the full attention LoRa provides the most reliable accuracy, and the best time--accuracy trade-off. Improvements vary across utterance length, with medium-length recordings benefiting the most, while short and long utterances remain challenging. These findings highlight the importance of adaptation placement and duration-dependent evaluation, under challenging, data-scarce personalization scenarios.

items.title: SLIM: Semantic-based Low-bitrate Image compression for Machines
items.summary: In recent years, the demand of image compression models for machine vision has increased dramatically. However, the training frameworks of image compression still focus on the vision of human, preserving unnecessary details and limiting bitrate efficiency for machine vision tasks. In this paper, we propose Semantic-based Low-bitrate Image compression for Machines, termed SLIM. This proposed framework consists of two key components: RoI-focused latent compression and semantic latent enhancement with dual cues. First, the latent compressor is trained to focus on Region-of-Interest (RoI) areas that are semantically and functionally important for machine vision tasks in the latent space, while requiring no explicit masks during inference. Second, to compensate for severe information loss at extremely low bitrates, a diffusion-based semantic decoder enhances the compressed latent with a pretrained diffusion model guided by two complementary cues provided by an RoI-focused latent and text-based semantic guidance. This design preserves RoI details that are critical for machine perception while maintaining semantically coherent and artifact-suppressed non-RoI regions under extremely low bitrates. Experimental results show that SLIM consistently achieves strong performance across diverse machine vision tasks under the same bits per pixel condition, compared to conventional image compression models for machines. Our code is available at https://github.com/mcml-official/SLIM

items.title: Discrete Phase-Shift Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces using Uniform Reference Directions
items.summary: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) enable programmable control of the wireless propagation environment through adjustable reflecting elements. A fundamental challenge in RIS-assisted communications is the optimization of discrete phase shifts to maximize the received signal power. While recently developed algorithms can obtain optimal solutions with linear complexity, their computational cost may still be excessive in applications requiring large-scale simulations, real-time adaptation, or repeated optimization over numerous channel realizations. This paper proposes a low-complexity discrete phase-shift optimization algorithm based on multiple reference directions within the feasible optimality sector. By evaluating candidate phase configurations generated from uniformly distributed reference directions, the proposed method systematically improves upon existing approximation approaches that rely on a fixed set of reference directions. The number of reference directions serves as a design parameter that enables a controllable trade-off between computational complexity and optimality. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves substantial computational speedups while maintaining a small optimality gap relative to the optimal solution. The results further show that increasing the number of reference directions progressively reduces the optimality gap, providing flexible operating points that can be tailored to application-specific complexity and performance requirements.

items.title: Performance Analysis of Discrete-Activation Pinching-Antenna Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates discrete-activation pinching antenna (DAPA) systems, where a finite set of pinching antennas (PAs) is deployed along a dielectric waveguide, from which PAs are selectively activated to serve users. Performance analyses are developed for both orthogonal multiple access (OMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) by explicitly accounting for the system geometry and discrete PA activation. Specifically, analytical expressions for the outage probability (OP) and ergodic rate (ER) are derived. Furthermore, the discrete-to-continuous gain ratio (DCGR) is introduced to quantify the normalized ER gain of a finite PA deployment relative to the single-PA and continuous-activation references. Monte Carlo simulations validate the derived expressions and show that DAPA systems can closely approach continuous-activation performance with only a moderate number of candidate PAs. For example, under the considered setup, DAPA with five PAs recovers approximately 92% and 90% of the continuous-activation ER gain under OMA and NOMA, respectively, at a transmit power of 0 dBm.

items.title: Physical AI: A Survey of Models, Learning, Systems, and Open Challenges
items.summary: Physical AI aims to enable intelligent systems to perceive, reason, act, and learn through interaction with the physical world. Unlike purely digital intelligence, physical agents must operate under partial observability, uncertain dynamics, embodiment constraints, and real-time requirements, while their actions continuously reshape the environment and subsequent observations. Recent advances in foundation models and robot learning have expanded the capabilities of physical agents, yet achieving reliable autonomy requires more than improvements in individual models. This survey presents a comprehensive, system-level review of Physical AI, organized around the closed-loop process of physical interaction. We examine the foundations and recent developments in task representations and memory, predictive and action-generating models, data and learning methods, embodiment and control, computing systems, evaluation, and safety. Beyond reviewing individual advances, we investigate how these components interact and collectively shape the capabilities and limitations of Physical AI systems. Building on this integrated perspective, we identify fundamental challenges in generalization, resource-efficient learning and execution, reliable state tracking, safety, recovery, and continual adaptation. We argue that advancing Physical AI requires moving beyond isolated model performance toward integrated systems capable of robust, efficient, safe, and autonomous physical interaction under changing real-world conditions.

items.title: SENTRY: A Streaming Edge Network Trust Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Real-time voice cloning has enabled large-scale streaming deepfake and vishing attacks, while existing Network Detection and Response (NDR) solutions rely on GPU-based post-processing that requires buffered audio and generalizes poorly to unseen speech synthesis models. This paper presents SENTRY, a hardware-oriented, streaming trust engine for inline deepfake detection at the network edge. SENTRY employs an integer lifting-wavelet front end together with a bank of multiplier-free transforms, including wavelet-packet envelopes, Walsh-Hadamard sequency profiles, waveform micro-statistics, and long-term spectral features, designed so that acoustic analysis needs only integer add, shift, compare and bitwise operations. A supervised gradient-boosted tree classifier is combined with an unsupervised Mahalanobis out-of-distribution detector trained solely on authentic speech, and their outputs are fused by a lightweight logistic layer to produce graduated LOG, CHALLENGE, or DROP actions. Under a closed-set protocol, SENTRY reaches 98.75% accuracy at a 1.25% equal-error rate (EER) on WaveFake, with perfect separation of HiFi-GAN and WaveGlow; its supervised track alone achieves an AUC of 0.9994 (fused: 0.9993). On ASVspoof 2019 LA (attacks A01-A06) over an 8 kHz mu-law telephony channel, it reaches 94.75% accuracy at a 5.05% EER, with a supervised-track AUC of 0.9948 (fused: 0.9884) and per-attack EERs below 7%. In our prototype, the feature front end runs as bit-exact integer code on one Arm Cortex-A53 core, and the classifier and fusion stage are synthesized for a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC using no DSP slices, returning a decision 220 ns after a feature vector is ready. These results indicate that deepfake screening can be placed inline without GPUs or floating-point hardware; generalization to unseen generators is left to future work.

items.title: Low-Bit Distributed Constrained Optimization with Application to Optimal Scheduling and Allocation
items.summary: This paper proposes a distributed resource allocation algorithm in which each agent communicates only the sign of its local cost gradient, a single bit per directed link per iteration. The algorithm is based on Laplacian-gradient dynamics and preserves the equality (demand) constraint at every iterate, guaranteeing anytime feasibility irrespective of termination time. First, we provide a complete Lyapunov-based convergence analysis for the fixed-step-size regime: the iterates are shown to enter, in at most O(1/\varepsilon^2) iterations, a neighborhood of the optimizer whose radius scales as O(τ) in the decision variable and O(τ^2) in the cost residual, where $τ$ is the step-size. Crucially, the step-size bound is a time-invariant network constant (depending only on the graph Laplacian spectrum and the cost curvature bounds), so no adaptive tuning is required. Second, we characterize the invariant set under B-connected, weight-balanced digraphs, strictly weaker than the all-time connectivity and doubly-stochastic weights assumed in most prior work, and show that any odd, sign-preserving nonlinearity yields the same invariant-set and descent structure, with the single-bit protocol being the extreme communication-minimizing instance of a broader nonlinear class. Third, we address local box constraints via smooth penalty relaxation and quantify explicitly how the penalty weight interacts with the step-size bound and the optimality gap. Simulations on economic dispatch (1000 generators) and CPU scheduling (500 servers) demonstrate that the single-bit protocol achieves 5-60 times reduction in total communication cost relative to multi-bit baselines, at the price of a tunable and explicitly bounded optimality gap. A diminishing step-size schedule is shown empirically to eliminate this gap; its formal convergence analysis is identified as an open problem.

items.title: Adding Heavy-Ball Momentum to Distributed Constrained Optimization for Energy Resource Management Subject to Time-Delays and Quantization
items.summary: This paper studies a hybrid discrete-time signed gradient-consensus method with heavy-ball momentum, paired communication delays, and fixed logarithmic quantization. The method preserves the aggregate supply-demand equality at every iteration. For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.

items.title: New Results for Networked Control of Nonlinear Plants Subject to Transmission Delays
items.summary: This paper studies networked control for nonlinear plants subject to several network-induced constraints, with a particular focus on transmission delays. In the context of general nonlinear networked control systems, a standard approach for guaranteeing stability is to construct a storage function, coupled with a single timer variable, to analyze the maximum allowable transmission interval (MATI) and maximum allowable transmission delay (MAD). In this paper, we propose a new approach that assigns each signal that is either \textit{in transit or most recently updated}, to an individual timer variable. This enables the individual characterization and compensation for the dynamics of each potential updating error. Subsequently, based on a novel construction of timer-coupled storage functions, the dynamics of these timer variables is designed and investigated, leading to less conservative conditions on the MATI and MAD than those by the standard approach while still ensuring closed-loop input-to-state stability with respect to external disturbances. Finally, simulation results are given to illustrate the advantages of these new results.

items.title: Dual Secure Sensing and Communications in MA-Enabled Networked ISAC Systems
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is envisioned as a cornerstone technology for next-generation networks, yet it introduces significant security risks in both communication and sensing domains. To mitigate the coverage limitations inherent in conventional mono-static or bi-static setups, this paper proposes a networked ISAC framework empowered by movable antennas (MAs). By leveraging flexible antenna reconfiguration, MAs provide additional spatial degrees of freedom to significantly boost beamforming gain and interference suppression. Specifically, we investigate a novel dual-domain security paradigm where networked base stations collaboratively protect uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmissions from communication eavesdropping while simultaneously safeguarding target sensing data against sensing eavesdroppers (SEs). To this end, we formulate a joint optimization problem to maximize the sum of secrecy rates, subject to sensing requirements, SE eavesdropping probability constraint, and practical MA deployment constraints, by jointly optimizing receive combiners, transmit beamformers, UL power allocation, and MA positions. To address this non-convex problem with highly coupled variables, an efficient alternating optimization algorithm is proposed, integrating closed-form solutions for receive combiners, successive convex approximation for transmit beamforming and UL power, and a tailored sensing-aware multi-candidate particle swarm optimization for the high-dimensional MA positioning. Extensive numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms, demonstrating that the proposed MA-enabled networked cooperative ISAC design significantly outperforms conventional fixed-position antenna-based designs in terms of security performance, while achieving notable power- and antenna-saving gains.

items.title: Movable Antenna-Enabled Multi-Static Cooperative Secure ISAC: Architecture, Mechanisms, and Enabling Technologies
items.summary: The broadcast nature of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) signals exposes them to physical-layer security (PLS) threats, including eavesdropping and jamming. Conventional fixed-position antennas provide limited spatial flexibility under highly correlated legitimate, sensing, and adversarial channels, while multi-static cooperative ISAC offers distributed spatial diversity but remains vulnerable to information leakage. To address these limitations, this article proposes a novel movable antenna (MA)-enabled multi-static cooperative secure ISAC framework centered on dual-scale spatial reconfiguration. Specifically, continuous MA repositioning reshapes local propagation channels, while distributed multi-static nodes provide complementary network-level spatial diversity. Their synergy transforms local antenna geometry and distributed network geometry into a unified controllable spatial resource for jointly enhancing communication, sensing, and PLS. This article first presents the system architecture of the proposed framework and its representative application scenarios, followed by an analysis of the physical-layer mechanisms underlying the resulting gains. Subsequently, we elaborate on the key enabling technologies for practical deployment. A case study further demonstrates the communication-sensing-security trade-off and antenna-saving potential of the proposed framework. Finally, open challenges and future research directions are identified toward practical MA-enabled multi-static secure ISAC networks.

items.title: Long Listening Thoughts: Eliciting Open Auditory Reasoning with Deliberative Perception and Cognitive Refinement
items.summary: We introduce Long Listening Thoughts (LLT), a framework for constructing post-training datasets that improves audio reasoning by pairing deliberate perceptual grounding with explicit cognitive behaviors. On audio understanding and reasoning benchmarks, large audio-language models (LALMs) are limited primarily by perceptual errors, yet existing post-training datasets rely on audio descriptions of limited diversity. Through a four-stage pipeline, LLT (1) builds multi-aspect dense audio descriptions spanning semantic, acoustic, and temporal information, (2) generates more challenging questions, (3) synthesizes incorrect reasoning traces, and (4) extends short reasoning traces into long ones via a thought-continuation strategy that elicits cognitive behaviors such as verification and backtracking. Using LLT, we synthesize 1.6M reasoning traces and train Qwen2.5-Omni-7B with a two-stage pipeline of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by direct preference optimization (DPO). This improves accuracy on MMAU Test-mini (71.5 to 78.2), MMAR (56.7 to 63.7), and MMSU (60.6 to 66.0).

items.title: Rate-Cost Tradeoffs in Nonlinear Control
items.summary: We study finite-horizon rate-cost tradeoffs for general stochastic control systems, including nonlinear systems. Under an average control cost constraint, we show that the minimum expected communication rate lies within an additive logarithmic gap above the normalized directed information minimized over causal control policies. This establishes directed information as the operationally relevant quantity governing rate-limited control, extending its previously established roles in causal source coding and linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control to general nonlinear control systems.

items.title: Lifting Safety Through Reduced-Order Model Architectures: An Invariant Manifold Approach
items.summary: Reduced-order model architectures are often used to decompose complex safety-critical control design tasks into tractable subproblems. In this paradigm, one must ask: when does the safety of a reduced-order model lift to safety of the full system? Taking an invariant manifold perspective, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of smooth, regular lifts of compact safe sets from reduced-order models. Our characterization relies only on asymptotic stability of an embedding of a reduced-order safe set, without additional robustness or rate conditions. We apply these results to study control barrier functions in reduced-order model architectures and lifts of safe sets through cascades. Further, we use our conditions to obtain topological obstructions to the tracking of safe, kinematic reduced-order models for mechanical systems. We conclude by using these obstructions to inform safe hierarchical control design for an underactuated satellite on SE(3).

items.title: Safe Driving in Occluded Environments
items.summary: Ensuring safe autonomous driving in the presence of occlusions poses a significant challenge in its policy design. While existing model-driven control techniques based on set invariance can handle visible risks, occlusions create latent risks in which safety-critical states are not observable. Data-driven techniques also struggle to handle latent risks because direct mappings from risk-critical objects in sensor inputs to safe actions cannot be learned without visible risk-critical objects. Motivated by these challenges, in this paper, we propose a probabilistic safety certificate for latent risk. Our key technical enabler is the application of probabilistic invariance: It relaxes the strict observability requirements imposed by set-invariance methods that demand the knowledge of risk-critical states. The proposed techniques provide linear action constraints that confine the latent risk probability within tolerance.
